species.description: A fast growing hardy small to medium shrub, around 2 to 3 metres high and 2 metres wide, massed with golden ball flowers in spring. Naturally grows in dry or moist soils, well drained gravels or sandy soils and adapts well to clay.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance and drought resistant

species.description: This is a very fast growing small tree with beautiful grey feathery foliage and bright yellow flowers in winter. The winter flowering is often so prolific that can hide the foliage. The colour and texture of the leaves is a year round feature. This species does tend to seed itself so it is best not to plant it near areas of natural bushland to prevent it from establishing feral populations, however, in urban areas it makes a magnificent small street tree, growing from 6 to 8 metres tall.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance

species.description: Sterling Silver is a striking, spring-flowering acacia - a dwarf shrub form of the Coastal Myall Wattle. The broad silver leaves are a definite highlight making it an excellent foliage contrast to the bright yellow blooms in early spring. The acacia will become a sprawling shrub and responds well to a light prune to keep it from getting too leggy. The flowers are like many Acacias being strongly fragrant, they also attract bees and the seed pods will entice seed eating birds like Rosellas.
species.maintenance: Fertilise every six months with a slow-release Australian Native feed for best results.

species.description: A large evergreen shrub with reddish brown stems and soft, needle-like leaves that come in matte gray-green with reddish tips. New growth is yellow-green. Fragrant, bright yellow, puffy flower clusters bloom in winter.
species.maintenance: No Maintenance. Prune branches as needed.

species.description: Lime Magik is a large shrub to small tree, depending on the situation, with the most beautiful soft lime foliage. It is eye catching with its graceful willow like form, and makes a great contrast plant. It grows to 6 metres tall and 2-3 metres wide, and is good for screening. Frost tolerant, good for sun to part shade, and adapts to most soils from clay to loam and well drained. A great low maintenance plant which can be pruned to shape.
species.maintenance: Once established very low maintenance. In very hot conditions water once a week. A little native fertiliser during spring will boost growth.

species.description: Acacia dealbata, commonly known as silver wattle, is a fast-growing evergreen tree native to southeastern Australia. It is known for its distinctive silver-grey, fern-like foliage and abundant, fragrant, bright yellow flowers. It is widely cultivated in Australia and overseas (where it is often called "mimosa") as an ornamental feature tree and for windbreaks. The cut flowers are popular in the floral industry.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance.

species.description: Acacia implexa, also known as Hickory Wattle or Lightwood, is a fast-growing, native Australian tree valued for its ornamental qualities, timber, and ecological benefits. It is a medium-sized tree that grows to 8–15 meters, with distinctive sickle-shaped leaves and pale yellow, ball-shaped flowers. Its name comes from its twisted seed pods, and it is known for being hardy, drought-tolerant, and good for erosion control.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance

species.description:
• Blackwood Wattle is a medium-sized to large tree that can reach heights of up to 100 feet (30 meters) in its native habitat.
• It features feathery, bipinnate leaves with numerous small leaflets, giving the foliage a fern-like appearance.
• The tree produces fragrant, golden-yellow flowers in globular clusters in late winter to early spring, adding to its ornamental appeal.
• The timber of Acacia melanoxylon is highly regarded for its strength, durability, and attractive dark color, making it a valuable timber tree.
species.maintenance:
1. Pruning: Prune as needed to maintain shape and remove any dead or diseased branches. Pruning can also help improve air circulation within the canopy.
2. Watering: Provide regular watering during the tree's establishment period. Once established, it can tolerate periods of drought but benefits from occasional deep watering.
3. Fertilization: While mature trees generally do not require heavy fertilization, you can apply a balanced, slow-release fertilizer in spring to promote healthy growth.

species.description: The Australian native plant Acacia myrtifolia, also known as myrtle wattle or red-stem wattle, is a fast-growing, evergreen shrub. It is appreciated for its attractive reddish stems and year-round foliage. This hardy species is found in all southern Australian states in coastal and near-coastal areas. Typically a rounded, bushy shrub that grows 1 to 2.5 meters tall and about the same in width, though some prostrate forms exist. Mature plants have leaf-like flattened stems called phyllodes, which are the main foliage. They are green, elliptical, and often slightly curved, measuring 2–9 cm long and 5–30 mm wide. The stems often have a reddish colour. The flowers are globular heads of a creamy-white to pale-yellow color. They appear in spring, typically from July to October, though this can vary by region.
species.maintenance: Myrtle wattle is a resilient plant that tolerates full sun and moderate frosts once established. It is adaptable to most well-drained soils and requires little maintenance.

species.description: Dense, spreading small to medium shrub, 2-4 m high, often with arched or pendulous branches bearing many short, sharp spines, and yellow, globular flower clusters, arising from leaf axils on short stalks. Flowers August to November. Fruit is a straight or slightly curved pod, seeds 2-10 dark and shining, attached to a short, persistent, pale brown funicle. Drought tolerant and may be frost tender when young but is frost tolerant later. Tolerates acid and alkaline soils. Grows in open forests and disturbed sites of any aspect. Soil preference is for dry, shallow gravelly, sandy and stony soils
species.maintenance: No Maintenance

species.description: This is a small shrub with prickly phyllodes, making it useful as a barrier or hedge to deter humans and animals. This protective environment can also provide shelter for small birds. Flowering through autumn and winter to spring, Acacia ulicifolia can give some extra colour in the garden through this period with its globular pale yellow blooms.Light shade is ideal, and a slightly moist root area, although it still needs a well drained soil.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance.

species.description: Acanthus mollis, commonly known as Bear's Breeches or Oyster Plant, is a striking herbaceous perennial from the Mediterranean. It is grown for its large, glossy, deeply lobed dark green leaves that form architectural rosettes to around 80–100cm tall and wide, and for its dramatic flower spikes — reaching up to 1.5m — bearing tubular white flowers hooded by purple bracts in late spring to summer. A bold, sculptural plant for shaded borders, courtyards, and architectural plantings; tolerates dry shade once established and may die back in hot summers, regrowing from rhizomes in autumn.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance once established. Cut back spent flower spikes and tatty foliage after flowering to refresh the clump. Mulch annually. Tolerates dry shade but appreciates supplementary water through dry summers. Spreads via rhizomes — can be vigorous once settled, so contain if you want to keep it in check.

species.description: Also commonly known as the Pineapple Guava, the Feijoa is a very hardy evergreen shrub with decorative flowers and delicious fruit in autumn and early winter. Flowers are a soft pink with a white underside and have large, protruding, vivid red stamens, while fruit is green skinned and has a sweet taste of pineapple, apple and mint. Foliage is a mid-green with a grey underside
species.maintenance: Hardy and quite drought tolerant; however, to get good fruit production it is important they get adequate water during the flowering and fruiting seasons (spring and summer). Give them lots of compost and composted manure and keep the base weed-free and mulched. They have a shallow root system with feeder roots around the dripline of the tree.

species.botanical_name: Acer p. dis. Viridis Std Weeper

species.description: Acer palmatum 'Elegans' is a deciduous Japanese Maple selection grown for its finely-cut, deeply divided leaves — seven narrow lobes with sharply serrated margins that give the canopy a lacy, layered translucence. New growth emerges soft green flushed with red at the margins, deepens through summer, and turns orange to crimson in autumn. Develops a graceful spreading, tiered habit to around 3–4m. Best in dappled shade with shelter from hot wind, where the leaf detail and the winter branch structure both carry.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance. Mulch well to keep the root zone cool and evenly moist. Shelter from hot afternoon sun and drying northerlies — leaf scorch is the main failure mode in Melbourne. Prune only in mid-winter when fully dormant, and minimally: the natural layered branch structure is the feature and does not recover well from heavy cuts.

species.description: Acer Palmatum Japanese Maple is a stunning small to medium deciduous tree, with foliage being deep green in color turning a purple.
species.maintenance: Consistent water conditions and yearly mulch beyond tree drip line, but do not cover the base line bark. Pruning should consist of shaping and not hedging during winter.

species.description: Acer palmatum 'Osakazuki' – Japanese Maple is a compact, deciduous ornamental tree with a broad, rounded canopy and standout autumn performance. Large green leaves turn a deep scarlet-red in autumn—regarded as some of the most vivid among Japanese Maples. They look excellent in courtyards, Japanese-style gardens, or planted as a seasonal focal point in residential landscapes where colour contrast and form are important. Moderate growth rate and a well-structured habit make it a strong choice for smaller spaces, feature planting, or bonsai use. Consistent seasonal colour, refined shape, and versatility across ornamental settings make this a reliable option for gardens requiring bold visual impact.
species.maintenance: Japanese maples generally benefit from as little [pruning](https://www.thespruce.com/all-about-pruning-japanese-maples-7369697) as possible. Dead or broken branches should be cut off, and branches that begin to cross one another should be carefully pruned to avoid crowding. The bark and flesh of the tree is sensitive, so be careful not to expose too much with cutting, especially in summer when hot sun can burn the tree. Early in its life, you can determine the shape of the trunk (either one single trunk or multiple ones) with pruning. Because the Osakzuki cultivar is so tall and upright, a singular trunk works well, but multiple trunks can look very dramatic, so it's really a matter of taste.

species.description: A dwarf, slow-growing Japanese maple with unusually narrow, strap-like leaf lobes that give the whole plant a fine, linear texture. Foliage emerges deep purple-red, holds its colour well through summer in dappled light, then turns to orange and gold before dropping. Reaches only around 2-3m over many years with a low, spreading, layered branch structure. Ideal for a sheltered atrium or courtyard where the fine leaf and winter branch silhouette can be read at close range; also excellent as a long-term container specimen.
species.maintenance: Wants shelter from hot afternoon sun and drying wind - leaf edges scorch in exposed positions. Keep soil consistently moist but free-draining; mulch to protect the shallow root system. Prune only in late autumn or winter when dormant, and only to remove dead or crossing wood; the natural layered form is the feature. Slow to establish, so avoid disturbing the root zone.

species.description: Acer palmatum 'Sango Kaku' – Coral Bark Maple is an upright, deciduous ornamental tree known for its bright coral-red stems that intensify in winter. Soft green, finely lobed leaves provide contrast through spring and summer, shifting to golden-yellow with red tones in autumn. They look excellent in courtyards, Japanese-style gardens, or feature positions where winter interest and subtle structure are needed. The vivid bark colour adds strong seasonal contrast, especially when leafless, making it a valuable year-round design element.
species.maintenance: Drought tolerant once established they perform better given a cool moist root run.  Give soil well-rotted compost before planting and ensure good drainage. Liquid fertilise every two weeks until established.

species.description: Acer palmatum 'Shaina' is a dwarf, slow-growing deciduous Japanese maple known for its compact, rounded shape and vibrant deep red to maroon foliage, making it ideal for small gardens, containers, and patios. This cultivar is a popular choice for structured, colorful, and compact garden accents.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance; prune in late winter or early spring for shape, but avoid heavy pruning.

species.description: Renowned for its prolonged, radiant autumn show, Acer rubrum 'October Glory' is a standout variety of the Canadian Maple family. This tree is distinguished by its glossy green leaves that, come Autumn transition into dazzling shades of deep red and violet. The 'October Glory' offers not just vibrant fall colouration but also provides shade during the warmer months, making it a favourite for landscapes and urban settings alike.
species.maintenance: No Maintenance

species.blurb: Flat pale-yellow plates that fade to soft buff and hold their shape right through winter.
species.description: Clump forming plant with fethery grey-green leaves and flat umbels that produce fiery orange flowers that fade into yellow over a period of time. Achillea is commonly known as ‘Yarrow’. This is a long blooming variety which produces a stunning colour display for around four months of the year. In the garden, flat umbels create a nice layer of colour. Perfect as cut flowers for a floral arrangement. Attracts butterflies. Whether you grow yarrow as a decorative plant or an herb, you can be sure that it will add beauty to your garden. Since yarrow care is so easy, you have nothing to lose by giving this ancient herb a small place in one of your flower beds.
species.maintenance: Cut black after flowering to promote growth.

species.description: Yarrow Achillea millefolium is a perennial herb native to Europe, prized for its medicinal uses and garden benefits. Its fern-like foliage and clusters of white or pink flowers make it a delightful addition to any landscape. With proper care, yarrow can bloom abundantly year after year, attracting pollinators and adding charm to cottage gardens. Yarrow is a favourite flower among pollinators, making it ideal for pollinator gardens. Insect-repelling properties also make it an excellent companion plant in vegetable gardens. As a dynamic accumulator, yarrow enriches and helps break down compost. In biodynamic farming, yarrow enhances soil vitality and plant resilience.
species.maintenance: Very low maintenance. Water until established. Cut back hard for a second and even third flowering.

species.description: Flannel flowers (Actinotus helianthi) are delightful Australian natives that add softness to any garden with their velvety white flowers and silvery grey foliage.
species.maintenance: Regular tip pruning will encourage side branching and create a nice shaped plant with extra flowers. Remove spent flowers with secateurs to encourage more blooms. Some plants may develop yellow leaves at the base of the stems and these can be removed using secateurs.

species.description: The wonderful soft, velvet-like texture and the silver coloured foliage are the outstanding features of this species. From the south coast of Western Australia, this plant is best suited to areas of southern Australia that have a Mediterranean climate (ie dry summers) rather than the more humid climates of places like Sydney and Brisbane. It grows into a large shrub and so makes a great feature plant and is sometimes used as a Christmas tree if grown in a large container. It has a compact habit. The foliage can produce skin sensitivity or allergic reaction in some.
species.maintenance: Low Maintenance. Some additional water during dry periods

species.description: A sprawling, adaptable mat like plant which is useful as a soil binding and ground cover plant for erosion control. Seeds can stick to clothing. Adiantum aethiopicum or the Maidenhair Fern is one of the prettiest and most delicate ferns, with slender black stems with a mass of delicately rounded pale green leaflets about 8mm diameter. The stems emerge from underground rhizomes to unfold making a very good foliage display that fill well in shady plantings e.g. in amongst Bromeliads etc and around pools. They go well indoors anywhere providing they are kept moist with a fine leaf spray every few days, bathrooms make an ideal location due to the humidity.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance. Keep moist, removing dead bits. Prune down in winter to promote new growth. Blood and Bone during the warmer months.
Application of fertiliser or composted manure in Spring. Cut back spent flowerheads after bloom and mulch annually .

species.description: A fine flowering perennial with prominent violet-blue flower spikes which last for months. In addition to its aesthetic qualities, agastache has long been cultivated in Asia where the fragrant anise leaves are used for culinary purposes and infused in tea for use as a health tonic

Agave 'Sharkskin' is a striking hybrid agave with thick, leathery blue-grey leaves that have the smooth, almost rubbery texture of shark skin — quite unlike the typical bristly or toothed agave leaves. Forms a compact, symmetrical rosette to around 60–90cm tall and 1m wide, slow-growing and offsetting modestly. Highly architectural, drought-tolerant, and frost-hardy to light frosts. Performs equally well in coastal exposures, rockeries, contemporary courtyards, and large containers. Like all agaves, it is monocarpic — flowering once at the end of its long life with a dramatic tall flower spike before the parent rosette dies.
species.maintenance: Very low maintenance. Water sparingly, especially in winter — well-drained soil is essential. Remove any old dry outer leaves cleanly with a knife. Cut off offsets if you want to limit spread, or pot them up. Avoid waterlogged sites.

species.description: An attractive medium-sized tree with a pendular habit. It has clusters of small white flowers that grow on the branches in between the leaves in spring and summer. Has nice long thin shiny leaves that hang from the drooping branches giving it an all over similar appearance to a Willow tree.
species.maintenance: Agonis flexuosa is relatively low maintenance. For best results, opt for a slow release native fertiliser and feed during early spring.

species.description: Ajuga australis, commonly known as Austral Bugle, is a low-growing, mat-forming Australian native perennial herb. It produces rosettes of soft, hairy, oblong leaves and erect spikes of small blue-purple flowers in spring and summer. Native to grasslands and open forests across southeastern Australia, it makes an attractive groundcover for partly shaded areas in cottage and native gardens.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance. Water regularly during establishment and through dry spells. Remove spent flower spikes to keep tidy. Divide established clumps in autumn if needed.

species.blurb: Glossy bronze-purple rosettes with short blue spires in spring — already thriving here, and replanted.
species.description: Award-winning Ajuga reptans 'Catlin's Giant' (Carpet Bugle) is an evergreen perennial prized for its large, glossy purplish-bronze leaves, 6 in. long (15 cm), which quickly form a dense mat of attractive rosettes. Rising from the center of the rosettes are whorls of tiny blue-violet flowers arranged on spikes, 12 in. tall (30 cm), which create a striking display when in full bloom, from mid to late spring.
species.maintenance: Once established, ajuga plants requires little care. Unless it's really dry, ajuga can usually sustain itself with normal rainfall and there's no need to fertilise this plant. Of course, if it's located in the sun, you may need to water it more often.

species.description: Deciduous small tree with a wide, airy umbrella canopy of fine ferny leaves and fluffy pink summer flowers. Light dappled shade; winter sun through bare branches. Can self-seed.

Onions are a biennial plant that belongs to the Allium family. They produce a bulb that is typically used in cooking for its distinctive flavour. Onions can be grown from seed, sets or transplants. They come in various sizes and colours, ranging from white to red to yellow.
species.maintenance: Onions require a moderate amount of maintenance. They prefer well-draining soil and a position in full sun. Onions should be watered regularly, but not excessively, and should be fertilized with a balanced fertilizer during the growing season. They can be planted in fall or early spring, depending on the climate.

species.description: Allium christophii, also known as Star of Persia, is a bulbous perennial with striking, large, globe-shaped flowerheads composed of numerous star-shaped, silvery-lilac blooms.These flowerheads can reach up to 20cm (8 inches) in diameter and have a distinctive metallic sheen when in bloom. The plant typically grows to a height of 30-60cm (1-2 feet) with broad, grey-green leaves that may fade by the time the flowers appear. It's a popular choice for borders, containers, and dried flower arrangements due to its ornamental value.
species.maintenance: Ensure well-drained soil, adequate sunlight, and managing foliage and seedheads after flowering. These plants are relatively low-maintenance, tolerating drought once established and generally resisting pests.

species.description: Garlic (Allium sativum) is a popular and flavorful vegetable that is easy to grow in a home garden. It is a member of the Allium family, which also includes onions, shallots, and chives. It is a perennial bulb, but should be treated as an annual. Long thin foliage, wider at the base. Light gray-green.
species.maintenance: Garlic requires regular watering, especially during the early stages of growth. The soil should be kept moist but not waterlogged. Garlic benefits from a high-nitrogen fertiliser applied at planting, and a side dressing of fertiliser applied during the growing season. Mulch lightly with pea straw at planting them add a thicker layer as foliage developes.

species.description: Chives (Allium schoenoprasum) is an easy-to-grow, grass-like perennial herb in the same family as onion and garlic. It has a mild onion flavor that tastes great in salads or as a soup garnish. The attractive edible purple flowers also make it an interesting garden plant and garnish. Chives attracts bees and other pollinators at the same time it seems to repel other insects; it is sometimes planted among vegetables to discourage Japanese beetles and other damaging insects.
species.maintenance: Chives require relatively little maintenance. They prefer well-draining soil and a position in full sun to partial shade. Chives require regular watering and should be fertilized with a balanced fertilizer during the growing season. They can be propagated by dividing the clumps every few years.

species.description: Allocasuarina littoralis, the Black Sheoak, is a slender small tree of eastern Australian woodlands and dry forests, usually 4–8 m tall with an upright habit and dark, furrowed bark. Its fine, drooping grey-green branchlets carry leaves reduced to tiny teeth, giving a soft, open canopy. Male and female flowers are on separate trees: males carry rusty-brown flower spikes that tint the whole crown, while females bear small red flowers that ripen into woody cones. It fixes nitrogen through root nodules, its seed is eaten by cockatoos, and the fallen needle litter forms a soft mulch beneath. Hardy in dry, well-drained soils.
species.maintenance: Very low maintenance. Water until established, then drought tolerant. No fertiliser needed as it fixes its own nitrogen. Leave the needle litter in place as natural mulch. Lower branches can be removed to lift the canopy.

species.description: Allocasuarina verticillata, commonly known as the Drooping Sheoak, is a native Australian tree well-regarded for its distinctive weeping foliage and resilience in harsh environments, including coastal areas.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance.

species.description: Alocasia macrorrhizos, the Giant Taro or Elephant Ear, is a dramatic tropical foliage plant from the rainforests of Southeast Asia and tropical northern Australia. Forms a clumping rosette of enormous, glossy, arrow-shaped leaves held upright on thick stalks, reaching 2–3m tall in favourable conditions. Produces a cream-yellow spathe-and-spadix flower structure typical of the Araceae family. Brings a bold, jungle aesthetic to sheltered gardens, courtyards, and shaded poolside plantings; perfect for adding scale and tropical texture. All parts contain calcium oxalate crystals and are toxic if ingested raw — handle the sap with care.
species.maintenance: Provide consistent moisture and rich, organic soil. Mulch heavily and shelter from drying winds and direct hot sun. Remove old or damaged leaves at the base. Frost-tender — protect from frost in cooler regions or grow in a sheltered position. Lift and divide clumps every few years to manage spread.

species.description: In winter beautiful pasted red to cream bicoloured flowers adorn this grey green stemless ball-shaped perennial who’s size and form resemble that of the Echidna, Australia’s egg laying mammal. This wonderful little aloe hybrid has pointed leaves which are covered in prominent but soft and safe , white warty spines.
species.maintenance: -Water during Summer. Provide fertiliser/compost in Spring. Remove old spent flowers (not necessary). Remove old leaves (not necessary)

species.description: An evergreen succulent that forms a cluster of leaves rising almost straight up from the base.  Leaves are green to grey-green and sometime feature small white spots of upper and lower surfaces. Each leaf is thick and fleshy and has a run of short thorns along each side.
species.maintenance: Needs soil with excellent drainage. Feed occasionally with slow-release fertilizer. Minimum watering required.

species.description: Lemon verbena is a perennial shrub or subshrub growing to 2–3 metres high. The 8-centimetre-long, glossy, pointed leaves are slightly rough to the touch and emit a strong lemon scent when bruised (hence the Latin specific epithet citrodora—lemon-scented). Sprays of tiny purple or white flowers appear in late spring or early summer. Due to its many culinary uses, it is widely listed and marketed as a plant for the herb garden.
species.maintenance: Frequent watering. Tip prune to keep in shape. Pruning is recommended in spring to encourage a bushy form.

species.description: Alpinia nutans, commonly known as Dwarf Cardamom or Cinnamon Ginger, is a clumping evergreen ginger from Southeast Asia. Forms upright cane-like stems clothed in long, glossy green leaves that release a distinctive sweet, cinnamon-like aroma when crushed. Produces nodding clusters of small white shell-like flowers with pink markings in summer. Compact relative to other Alpinias — usually reaching around 1–1.5m — and well-suited to shaded courtyards, tropical-style plantings, and pots. Performs best in sheltered positions with consistent moisture and humidity.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance. Mulch well and keep moist during dry periods. Cut back old or damaged canes at ground level to refresh the clump. Tolerates light frost but appreciates a sheltered position; protect heavy foliage from strong winds.

species.description: Alyogyne huegelii, also known as the lilac or blue hibiscus, is a fast-growing, medium-sized evergreen shrub that can reach heights and widths of up to 2.5 meters. It is characterized by bright green, deeply lobed leaves and large, hibiscus-like flowers that are typically mauve to purple but also come in white, cream, or red forms. The plant flowers for a long period, often from late spring through summer and into fall, making it a popular choice for landscaping, hedging, and attracting pollinators.
species.maintenance: To maintain Alyogyne huegelii, ensure it's planted in a sunny spot with well-drained soil and prune after its main flowering period to encourage a dense, rounded shape. Water moderately once established, fertilize with a native-specific fertilizer in spring, and apply mulch to retain moisture and suppress weeds.  It responds well to a frequent light prune, which should be done after flowering, and it can be shaped to size.

species.description:
The Amanogawa cherry blossom tree, scientifically known as Prunus ‘Amanogawa’, is a stunning and unique variety of flowering cherry. With its slender, upright growth habit and abundant pink blooms, this tree is a favorite among gardeners and cherry blossom enthusiasts. One of the key features of the Amanogawa cherry tree is its distinctive form. Unlike other cherry trees that spread out horizontally, the Amanogawa grows in a narrow, columnar shape, reaching heights of up to 20 feet. This makes it an excellent choice for smaller gardens or limited spaces, as it can be planted in tight rows or even as a striking focal point in a container.
In terms of its flowers, the Amanogawa cherry tree truly shines. Its blossoms are a delicate shade of pink, and what sets them apart is their double petal structure. This means that each bloom has twice the number of petals, creating a fuller and more vibrant display. These double pink flowers add a touch of elegance and charm to any landscape, and their beauty is further enhanced when the tree is in full bloom.
Pruning is an important aspect of maintaining and shaping the Amanogawa cherry tree. The best time to prune this variety is immediately after flowering. This allows you to remove any dead or damaged branches, as well as shape the tree to your desired form. Early formative pruning is also recommended for upright cherry trees like the Amanogawa, as it helps establish a balanced branch framework and removes any unwanted shoots. The Amanogawa cherry blossom tree is a stunning addition to any garden or landscape. Its upright form, double pink blooms, and relatively fast growth rate make it a popular choice among cherry tree enthusiasts. Whether you’re looking to create a striking focal point or add a touch of elegance to your outdoor space, the Amanogawa cherry tree will not disappoint.
species.maintenance: Take care to plant the bud union above the soil level. Water in well and keep soil moist until tree is established. Fertilize when planting and again after new growth appears. Prune tree when planting to encourage new growth. Prune after flowering finishes each season to promote new seasons growth.

species.description: Commonly known as Wind plant or windflowers (because of the way its dainty blossoms sway in the breeze), Japanese Anemone, and Japanese Thimbleweed, Anemone hupehensis is a perennial in the buttercup family. Known for its tall, graceful stems and large, saucer-shaped flowers in shades of pink, white, or purple. Its late blooming period and elegant form make it a beautiful addition to the fall garden.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance. A layer of mulch will keep the soil cool and moist. Cut back in late Autumn. Liquid fertiliser in Spring and deadhead.

species.description: A highly aromatic annual with feathery leaves and umbles of tiny yellow flowers. The leaves
species.maintenance: Keep soil loose and well-draining. Thrives in a slightly acidic soil. Keep moist but don't allow to dry out. Does not need heavy fertiliser if planted in rich soil.

species.description: Kings Park Royale is such a vibrant colour, pairing purple buds with orange stems, and a surprise pop of emerald and lime inside The Australian native plant features dramatic flowers rising above neat clumps of strap-shaped, green leaves. The flowers attracts nectar-feeding birds and are a valuable cut flower.
species.maintenance: Prune flower stems back to ground level after flowering. Avoid watering the foliage and protect from snails and slugs.

species.description: Kangaroo paw (Anigozanthos) is a genus of 11 species and multiple subspecies of flowering plants that are native to Australia. These plants have long, slender, arching leaves similar to the foliage of daylilies or amaryllis plants. The unusual tubular flowers grow on stalks in fan-like rows and are covered in velvety fuzz, giving them the appearance of an animal’s paw. The blooms come in an array of shades, including red, orange, yellow, and purple.
species.maintenance: Kangaroo paw plants grow fairly quickly and don’t require much maintenance.

The unusual tubular flowers grow on stalks in fan-like rows and are covered in velvety fuzz, giving them the appearance of an animal’s paw. The blooms come in an array of shades, including red, orange, yellow, and purple.
species.maintenance: Kangaroo paw plants grow fairly quickly and don’t require much maintenance.

species.description: Anise Hyssop (Agastache foeniculum) is a delightful herbaceous perennial known for its aromatic leaves, showy flower spikes, and pollinator-attracting qualities. Anise Hyssop is a clump-forming perennial that typically reaches a height of 2 to 4 feet (60 to 120 cm) and spreads about 1 to 2 feet (30 to 60 cm). It features lance-shaped leaves that are gray-green and have a distinct anise or licorice fragrance when crushed. The most striking feature of Anise Hyssop is its flower spikes, which are composed of small tubular flowers tightly arranged along the spike. The flowers can vary in color, including shades of purple, lavender, and sometimes pink.
species.maintenance:
1. Pruning: After the initial bloom period, you can deadhead (remove spent flowers) to encourage more blooms and maintain a neat appearance. In late fall or early spring, you can cut back the stems to the base to promote new growth.
2. Watering: While Anise Hyssop is relatively drought-tolerant once established, regular watering during dry spells can help promote healthy growth and flowering.
3. Division: Every few years, you can divide mature clumps to rejuvenate the plant and prevent overcrowding. •Aromatic Foliage: The anise-scented leaves of Agastache foeniculum release a pleasant fragrance when touched, making it a sensory delight in the garden.
• Pollinator Magnet: Anise Hyssop's showy flower spikes are highly attractive to pollinators, making it a valuable plant for supporting biodiversity and ecosystem health.
• Culinary and Medicinal Uses: The leaves of Anise Hyssop can be used to flavor teas, desserts, and culinary dishes. Additionally, the plant has been used in traditional herbal medicine for its potential health benefits.

species.description: Small to medium deciduous tree. Can grow to 10m but should be maintained to less than 5m. Oval shaped leaves with a slight pointed tip. Dark green above but slightly grey fur beneath. Cultivated worldwide, it is valued for its crisp, edible fruit and can live for decades with proper care.
species.maintenance: Young trees need reliable moisture while establishing. Important to establish chill hours for the area as this is essential to develop flower buds and then fruit. Keep well mulched. Annual application of slow-release fertiliser. Pruning: Regular pruning in winter or early spring helps maintain the tree's shape (often an open vase shape) and encourages healthy growth and fruit production. Pests and Diseases: Trees can be susceptible to issues like codling moths, apple maggots, and fungal diseases such as black spot and powdery mildew. Netting the trees is important to protect the crop from birds and other animals.

species.blurb: Finely cut silver foliage, aromatic when brushed. Grown for the leaf rather than the flower.
species.description: Wormwood is Made famous by being one of the active ingredients in the spirit 'Absinthe'. This herbaceous perennial has many uses – Koreans use it in cooking, Moroccans in mint tea, companion planting and medicinal uses include aiding digestion, flatulence and a nerve tonic. An aromatic, herbaceous perennial growing from 80cm to 1.2 meters. Rarely, the tall branching stems will reach 1.5 meters. The stems extend from the perennial roots and can be quite woody at the base. The stems are quite strong and are also white-silver toned, due to the coverage of many small hairs. The leaves are up to 8cm by 3 cm, divided into segments and arranged in a spiral around the grooved stem. The deeply serrated leaves are greyish green above and white on the underside, with both sides covered in fine silky trichomes or oil producing hairs. The overall appearance is a generally grey or silvery toned plant. The flowers are small, globular and a yellow-green colour.
species.maintenance: Sprinkle slow-release fertiliser around the base of the plant annually in spring. Watering: dry tolerant. Young plants require watering as they establish. Established plants rarely need watering, except in extremely long dry periods.

species.description: New Zealand Rock Lily is a clump-forming perennial that features strap-like, arching leaves. The leaves are long, narrow, and deep green, providing an attractive foliage display throughout the year in Melbourne. The plant typically reaches a height of 1 to 2 feet (30 to 60 cm) with a similar spread. In summer, it produces tall stems adorned with delicate, star-shaped white flowers. The flowers are lightly fragrant, adding a touch of elegance to Melbourne gardens.
species.maintenance:
1. Summer Care: Provide regular watering during Melbourne's dry summers to keep the plant adequately hydrated. Mulching around the base of the plant can help conserve soil moisture.
2. Autumn Pruning: After the flowering period, trim back any spent flower stems and remove any dead or damaged leaves to maintain the plant's neat appearance.
3. Winter Protection: In colder regions of Melbourne, consider providing winter protection such as a layer of mulch or a protective cover to shield the plant from frost                                             Organic fertiliser application in Spring. Removal of spent flowers in summer. Removal of dead foliage. Mulch to retain moisture in the soil and suppress weeds. Watch out for snails as they like to eat the new growth.

species.blurb: An indigenous lily with fine purple flowers that genuinely smell of chocolate when warmed by the sun.
species.description: Arthropodium strictum or the Chocolate Lily is a native herbaceous perennial native to woodlands and forests in regions of Western Australia, South Australia, New South Wales, Victoria, Tasmania and Queensland. It produces purple blooms from spring to autumn that smell like chocolate when crushed.
species.maintenance: Regular watering is necessary, especially during dry spells or in the summer months. Apply a layer of mulch around the plant to help retain soil moisture and suppress weed growth. To promote healthy growth, consider dividing the clumps every few years in early spring.

species.description: Foxtail fern is a plush-looking perennial evergreen herb with luscious, fluffy stems of pine needle-like leaves. The common name comes from the fact that each narrow, bushy, plume-like stem resembles a foxtail. With its delicate foliage and unique appearance, it can transform any space into a verdant oasis. A member of the asparagus family, the foxtail fern is actually not a fern at all, as the plant uses seeds to reproduce, not spores. The feathery plant yields small white flowers that produce eye-catching red berries, a wonderful addition to both outside gardens and indoor houseplant collections. Foxtail fern is also used as greenery in flower arrangements, where it stays fresh for two to three weeks.
species.maintenance: As a low-maintenance plant, the foxtail fern is a fantastic option for both beginner and experienced gardeners alike, able to survive periods of neglect while continuing to grow happily. To promote dense plant growth, pinch back your asparagus fern's stem tips by about a third every few months. If the plant's shape becomes too sprawling, cut back the oldest stems close to the soil to encourage new growth.

species.description: The cast-iron plant (Aspidistra elatior) is native to Taiwan and the southern islands of Japan, where it grows in the understory of the forest. It features long, tapered leaves that are glossy green, sometimes with stripes or spots.  It produces strange-looking purple flowers that emerge out of the rhizome at ground level, but this rarely happens indoors. If it does, lean down close to the soil and give the flower a sniff. It smells kinda musty, a lot like a mushroom.If you’re wondering why on earth a plant would send a stinky flower out of the soil, this is because it’s trying to attract fungus gnats (Cordyla sixi and Bradysia spp.).
species.maintenance: Remove spent leaves. Minimal. Very low water requirements. Should be watered when top soil dries out.

species.description: Asplenium australasicum, commonly known as the 'Bird's nest fern', is native to Australia's east coast from Cape York in Queensland down to the south coast of New South Wales. The common name derives from its large, nest-shaped rosette of light-green, slightly leathery radiating fronds and its ability to grow on trees due to is shallow root system. In its natural habitat it's found in moist and sheltered forests where it grows on trees or rocks but is happy to grow in urban settings in protected gardens and also indoors. Bird's nest ferns have a striking upright vase shape which adds structural interest and with green fronds reaching up to 1.5 m long can create a wonderful garden focal point.
species.maintenance: Feed with half strength liquid fertiliser during warmer months. The plants enjoy warmth, humidity and moisture. Watering needs to be consistent and topsoil layer must never dry out. Do not water straight into the rosette centre. Cut away spoilt leaves to maintain size.

species.description: Asplenium nidus, commonly known as the Bird's Nest Fern, is a popular epiphytic fern native to tropical regions of Southeast Asia, Australia, and Africa. It is widely loved as a houseplant for its architectural, apple-green fronds that form a distinctive rosette resembling a bird's nest.
species.maintenance: Gently wipe the broad fronds with a damp soft cloth to remove dust, which helps with photosynthesis. Remove old, yellowing, or damaged outer fronds by cutting them at the base with sharp, sterilised scissors.

species.description: A profusion of lavender pink flowers cluster at the top of towering stems in autumn. Each is around 2-3cm across with a golden centre. Plant Tartarian Aster towards the back of garden beds where the tall stems can laud it over the rest of the garden. It rarely requires staking, but should be protected from strong winds. The lower leaves are dense and each can grow up to 60cm long but up top they are much smaller. In the language of flowers, Aster's denote love or daintiness. The word, Aster, is Latin for Star. Asters are commonly known as Easter Daisies or Michaelmas Daisies.In Korea this Aster is known as gaemichwi and is eaten. It has long been used in Chinese medicine. It is currently under investigation in modern medicine for its anti inflammatory properties on the nervous system.
species.maintenance: By dead heading the plants regularly you will promote more blooms, plus the flowers last well in a vase. Tougher than they look, once established the plants don't require a lot of water, even though they grow and flowers through the hotter times of the year. Grow in moderately fertile to humus rich, well drained soil. Divide this rhizomatous herbaceous perennial every three or four years to keep it looking good.

species.description: A small, spreading prostrate shrub or groundcover with blue-green, pine like leaves and tubular flowers. Flowers are followed by small, round berries that turn from green to red as they ripen in spring and summer. Cranberries are high in vitamin C and antioxidants. Ideal fir eating as sauces, juices and jams or as dried fruit.A great plant for borders and rockeries or as a groundcover.
species.maintenance: Responds well to pruning

species.description: Old Man Saltbush has attractive silver foliage, growth habit tends to be sprawling to around 3 metres high and can get to 5 metres wide. Naturally growing in arid areas in all states of Australia, this is a very useful plant to grow as it tolerates high levels of salinity, alkalinity, severe drought and is good for stock feed.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance, cut back if required for a compact shape.

species.description: Atriplex semibaccata, commonly known as Australian saltbush, berry saltbush, or creeping saltbush, is a species of flowering plant in the family Amaranthaceae and is endemic to Australia. It has dense foliage that covers the ground, acting as a green mulch that provides protection for both the soil and fauna. Flowers most of the year. The female flowers develop into succulent square/diamond shaped red berries. The seeds are an important food source of insects, birds and small marsupials.
species.maintenance: No Maintenance

species.description: Geranium solanderi, commonly known as Austral Cranesbill or Native Geranium, is a widespread, hairy, sprawling native perennial herb often used as a groundcover, growing to roughly 0.2 m tall and 1 m wide. It features pink flowers and is adaptable to various conditions, often rooting at nodes to form colonies. It is well-suited for gardens, providing foliage and bloom.
species.maintenance: No Maintenance

species.description: A slender to densely tufting perennial grass that is aquatic or semi aquatic.  It has arching flowering stems around 1m but often most are below the water. 6-10-flowered spikelets scattered along narrow flowerheads 5-15 cm long. Upper hairs on lower floral bract reduced to large marginal tufts, hairs long on lower row, tip elongated; lobes broad, contracting suddenly to long bristle. Central bristle long.
species.maintenance: Responds well to mowing.

species.description: Midyim berries (aka. midgen berry, sand berry) are among the most delicious of all the bush tucker plants, similar in taste and appearance to the blueberry. This shrub bears small white, purple-speckled berries in profusion throughout late Summer and early Autumn. Berries are sweet and tangy, and may be eaten fresh or used in pies and preserves.
species.maintenance: A light trim after harvesting will help keep the plant bushy and encourage new growth, rewarding you with another crop the following season.

species.description: A brilliant low grass with outstanding flowers and seedheads. Leaves with a hairless or rough sheath at the base.  Ligule a membrane without a fringe of hairs. Leaves 3-7.5cm long, 1-2mm wide, with the edges rolled inwards, surface hairless to rough.  Spikelets pink, grey or black, with long white hairs that often make the spikelets appear white, 7-12mm long, excluding the awn.
species.maintenance: No Maintenance and Low supplementary watering. Plant closely at 25cm for optimal results

species.description: Slender tussock with erect stems to 50 cm tall. Slender tufted grass with flower stems to 60 cm tall. Fine leaves strongly inrolled up to 30 cm long. Short hairy leaf-collar (ligule). Seedheads to 30 cm with base often hidden by a leaf-sheath. Seeds are purplish then golden brown on maturity and covered with white hairs. Bristle or awn sickle-shaped (falcate).
species.maintenance: Prune in early winter to encourage new growth. Tolerates drought conditions.

species.description: Spear grass (Heteropogon contortus is a tropical perennial grass. It grows to a height of 50 to 150 cm, is tufted and highly variable. Its stems are geniculated at the base, erect at their upper levels, often branched, particularly at flowering   The leaves are green or bluish green, usually glabrous or with few long hairs at the base. The leaf-blade is folded when young, then flat at maturity, 3-30 cm long,
species.maintenance: Very low Maintenance

species.description: Azaleas are flowering shrubs known for their vibrant and showy blooms. They typically have a compact and rounded growth habit, reaching heights of 3 to 6 feet (0.9 to 1.8 meters) and spreading about the same distance. The leaves are small and glossy, ranging in color from deep green to bronze, and some varieties exhibit beautiful fall foliage. Azalea flowers come in a wide array of colors, including shades of pink, red, white, purple, and orange. The blooms are often trumpet-shaped and grow in clusters, creating a stunning visual display.
species.maintenance: Full sun can burn leaves causing weak growth and poor blooms.  Lace bugs and caterpillars are common pests. Prune after flowering maintaining original shape. Blooms are on old wood.

species.description: Lemon Myrtle is sometimes referred to as the “Queen of the Lemon Herbs”. It boasts an intensely citrus fragrance and flavour, and has long been used in Aboriginal cuisine and medicine. This native offers a taller hedging option to screen a two-storey house or new development. The evergreen foliage is lemon-scented and the ivory clouds of flowers are handsome all summer long. Infuse the leaves in hot water for a refreshing lemon-scented tea, or in a hot bath to clear the head and promote relaxation. Indigenous Australian were the first to recognise the nutritional and healing benefits if this valuable native plant. Chewing on the leaves of the lemon myrtle provided a boost of vitamins and minerals while the antibacterial properties within helps ward off disease and infection. The glossy green leaves would also be ground into a paste and applied to sores and other skin afflictions.
species.maintenance: Low Maintenance. Lemon myrtle are usually easy to grow with few problems provided they have rich soil and enough moisture in Summer.

species.description: Backhousia myrtifolia, commonly known as Grey Myrtle or Cinnamon Myrtle, is an evergreen small tree from the rainforest margins and creek lines of eastern Australia. It grows naturally where soil stays cool and moist, making it one of the more forgiving natives in ground that drains slowly. Dense and well furnished to the base, it carries small, deep green leaves that release a warm cinnamon scent when crushed. Clusters of cream star-shaped flowers open through late spring, and the papery calyces persist well into summer, holding a soft haze of colour long after the petals have gone. Naturally multi-stemmed, though it can be grown on a single leader where a clear trunk is wanted. Slow to moderate growth suits restricted root volume and container planting.
species.maintenance: Low. Tip prune while young to build density, or remove lower stems progressively to form a single clear trunk. Responds well to pruning and holds shape without regular intervention. Prefers shelter from hot, drying wind. Keep moisture consistent through the first two summers.

species.description: A great favourite of bees when it flowers during mid-summer, this small-growing form was collected in Crete and makes a neat, rounded evergreen shrub, clothed from top to bottom with round, thickly-felted grey leaves.
species.maintenance: The removal of spent flower stems is all the care required.

species.description: Baloskion pallens, commonly known as 'Didgery Sticks' or Native Rush, is a graceful Australian native sedge characterized by its elegant, upright, reed-like stems that form dense clumping mounds. It is highly valued for adding architectural vertical accents to gardens and for its ability to thrive in wet, waterlogged conditions.
species.maintenance: Generally low-maintenance. You can thin out dead stalks or trim the plant by half every 2–3 years to rejuvenate its appearance.

species.description: A tidy upright bamboo with smooth clean culms and lush green foliage. Height around 6-7 metres.
species.maintenance: No major pests or diseases.

species.description: Goldstripe is a small narrow screening bamboo perfect for small garden beds or pots and troughs. Goldstripe will naturally grow between 3-4mtrs in height and can be easily trimmed down in height if need be. It has a naturally upright growth (most bamboo fan out wide) with attractive bushy green foliage and a golden stripe on the culm. It can also feature a lovely golden hue on the poles when planted in full sun. The natural footprint size of the clump is 1 metre.
species.maintenance: A barrier material can control spread if required however it should be at least 30cm deep.  Allow spent leaves to form mulch.  Grass is good for mulching as it adds nitrogen and silica. Tall varieties need to be staked or guyed with rope about 2/3 way up. Needs frequent watering.

species.description: A fantastic and versatile groundcover with reddish brown to orange flowers appearing in autumn-spring. It’s dense habit makes it a good weed suppressor and stabiliser on embankments. Ideally requires well-drained soils but is also suitable for heavier soils such as clay and gravel.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance.
Responds well to a tip prune after flowering •

species.description: An easy care groundcovering Banksia, growing to just under a metre high and 2 metres wide. With large yellow flowers borne for most of the year- from summer through to winter-they are bird attracting and make good cut flowers.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance

species.description: Banksia integrifolia 'Sentinel' is a compact variant of the classic Coast Banksia. A top pick for narrow spaces and smaller gardens, 'Sentinel' maintains the signature characteristics of its parent species – the captivating yellow flower spikes and the distinctive silvery-green leaves – but in a more contained form.
species.maintenance: Occasional pruning to maintain shape

species.height_raw: 2–8m h x 2–4m w in gardens (to 12m in the wild)
species.description: Banksia marginata, the Silver Banksia (also Honeysuckle), is a highly variable native of south-eastern Australia, ranging from a low shrub on exposed coasts to a tree of 12 m or more in sheltered forest; in gardens it usually grows 2–8 m. Its narrow, stiff leaves are dark green above and silver-white beneath. Cylindrical pale yellow flower spikes appear from late summer through winter, followed by grey woody cones. The nectar-rich flowers are a key cool-season food for honeyeaters, wattlebirds, possums and insects. Hardy in sun or part shade on well-drained soils, and tolerant of wind and light frost.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance. Water until established. Light prune after flowering to shape; lower branches can be lifted. Use only low-phosphorus native fertiliser, if any.

species.description: Banksia menziesii dwarf is a small showy evergreen shrub with thick woolly branches and dark green leaves. Produces a profusion of stunning pink/red flowers that appear from autumn to winter.
species.maintenance: Prune after flowering to maintain compact growth. Banksia menziesii dwarf will grow to a height and width of 1.5m.

species.description: This Banksia not only has beautiful flowers but also eye-catching bright red new growth that is covered in tiny hairs giving it a velvety texture, similar to the new growth on Banksia robur. Banksia plagiocarpa has great ornamental potential in the garden, as it can be grown a a large shrub or can be shaped into a small feature tree, being a Banksia it is very forgiving to pruning and will happily reshoot from the rhizome.
species.maintenance: Prune lightly after flowering to encourage shapeliness. Banksias are phosphorus sensitive, so a good native fertiliser is best when it comes to feeding time.

species.description: Banksia praemorsa, commonly known as the cut-leaf banksia, is a striking and hardy native shrub or small tree from Western Australia. Its name refers to the distinctive shape of its leaves, which appear as if they have been cut off or bitten at the end. A dense, upright plant, it is valued for its bold, cylindrical flower spikes and its ability to attract nectar-feeding birds.
species.maintenance: Fertilise sparingly once or twice a year in spring or autumn to encourage stronger growth and flowering. An annual application of mulch can also provide slow-release nutrients.

species.description: A dense and compact small shrub that is perfect for rockeries and smaller gardens, whether mass planted for dramatic effect, in small groups or in containers on the patio, verandah or deck. It is frost tolerant, and suits acid to alkaline soils. Likes well drained soil types, in heavier soils it is advisable to build raised beds and add some organic matter. Banksias are phosphorus sensitive, so a good native fertiliser is best when it comes to feeding time.
species.maintenance: Low Maintenance

species.description: A compact dwarf cultivar of Banksia spinulosa with dark green foliage and golden-orange flower spikes from autumn through winter. It generally reaches around 0.5m high and spreads to approximately 1m wide. The flowers provide nectar for birds, bees and other pollinators. Best in well-drained soil and suitable for borders, mass planting and low habitat layers.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance. Light tip pruning when the plant is young, once established a light prune after flowering.

species.description: A lovely lilac aroma is produced from large mauve coloured flower heads, giving this plant its common name of Purple torch or Blue mist flower. The flowers appear on purple stems above velvety textured rich green leaves. A tall growing evergreen shrub, the Blue Mist plant (Bartlettina sordida) is native to Mexico and will reach over 2 metres in height. Large foliage, mid to deep green and rosy red to purple flowers buds in spring are followed by large lilac flowers.
species.maintenance: Mulch well. Prune after flowering to maintain compact growth.

species.description: This plant produces beautiful red or pink flowers that are a favorite of bees and butterflies. It can tolerate some shade, but still needs plenty of sunlight to thrive.

Berberis 'Rosy Glow' is an eye catching, compact and colourful shrub. Young leaves emerge purple, with silver and pink patterns which mature to purple.
Planting Berberis 'Rosy Glow' is a great way to add colour to the garden. In spring, small yellow flowers open, adding a nice contrast to the foliage. The blooms are followed in summer and autumn by small, red, ornamental berries.
Berberis are compact shrubs with interesting foliage and stunning autumn colour. Berberis make lovely, dwarf, specimen trees or can be used for small hedges or in pots. They are super low maintenance, needing only a light prune after flowering every other year to maintain form. Plant Berberis in humus rich, well drained soil. Ideally plant in a morning sun to a lightly shaded position for best foliage colour. The branches have spiny shoots which is where it gets its common name, Japanese Barberry.
species.maintenance: Very low maintenance

species.description: Bergenia cordifolia, also known as Heartleaf Bergenia, is a clump-forming evergreen perennial that produces clusters of deep-pink flowers in winter and spring. The blooms rise above rosettes of leathery, shiny, heart-shaped leaves. The leaves provide year-round interest, with the foliage transforming from a purplish-bronze colour in winter to a deep green in summer. Bergenia cordifolia is excellent when used as a ground cover, in a garden bed or border or when mass planted across banks and slopes. The foliage also makes a great addition when used in cut floral arrangements. We have Bergenia planted in our office garden and our [Bayside Retreat](https://www.landscape.net.au/project/bayside/), providing a beautiful lush texture all year round.
species.maintenance: Key maintenance tasks include pruning spent flower stalks, removing any damaged or unsightly leaves, and occasional division to rejuvenate the plant.

species.description: Betonica officinalis syn. Stachy's officinalis commonly known as Purple Betony, Wood Betony, Hedgenettle or Bishop's Wort is a stunning perennial with bright pink to purple flower spikes which emerge from dark green, glossy foliage. Wood Betony is a tough and versatile plant that grows as a compact clump and works beautifully planted en mass or positioned in the front of a border. In the Middle Ages Wood Betony was believed to possess magical powers and was worn as a woven armband and planted in churchyards to ward off evil spirits and was even used as a cure for drunkenness. Betony is a lovely low spreading ground cover that, when in flower, provides nectar for bees, butterflies and beneficial insects.
species.maintenance: Remove spent flower stems

species.description: Deciduous bright green foliage which turns pale yellow in Autumn. Trunk starts out grey then turns white. It is a grafted form of Silver Birch.
species.maintenance: Relatively low maintenance. Prune only in summer or early autumn. Pruning in winter can cause bleeding of the sap.

species.description: The Birch Tree is the ‘lady of the forest’ with its silvery bark, elegant white boughs and delicate leaves. This attractive narrow upright growing tree, with an open habit, outer branches have pendulous tips with small bright green serrated leaves that become yellow in Autumn. The slender trunk has white bark with dark markings making it a striking feature for the garden. The short, slender branches rise to a pyramid-like crown on younger trees and become pendulous on older trees. The leaves are egg-shaped or triangular with toothed margins and hairy undersides. The tiny flowers are called catkins and they bear winged seeds.
species.maintenance: Mulch and water well for up to 12 weeks or until the plant is established, and in dry spells.

species.description: Bidgee widgee (Acaena novae-zelandiae) is a fast-growing, mat-forming perennial herb native to Australia and New Zealand, known for its distinctive spiky burrs. It provides a valuable food source for birds, and its dense growth offers excellent habitat and refuge for frogs and small lizards. Bidgee widgee is highly adaptable, thriving in both moist to dry, clay and sandy soils, and a wide range of light conditions from full sun to full shade.
species.maintenance: The Bidgee widgee plant (Acaena novae-zelandiae) is a low-maintenance, hardy ground cover once established. The main maintenance task is controlling its vigorous spread to prevent it from becoming invasive in garden settings.

species.description: Billardiera mutabilis, commonly known as Climbing Apple Berry or Sweet Apple Berry, is a slender, evergreen climbing plant native to southeastern Australia. It is a versatile and adaptable plant known for its ornamental flowers and edible fruit. A slender, twining climber or scrambler, growing to a height of 1–3 meters (3–10 feet), or forming a sprawling shrub in open areas. Bell-shaped, nodding, greenish-yellow flowers are produced primarily from spring to summer (June to January in its native range), often becoming tinged with navy blue or mauve as they age. These flowers attract pollinators like bees and butterflies, as well as nectar-eating birds.
species.maintenance: It is a low-maintenance, drought-tolerant plant once established and is also tolerant of frost.

species.description: Billardiera scandens, the Common Apple Berry or Apple Dumpling, is a member of the Pittosporaceae family. It is a slender climber or scrambling shrub with stems reaching 3 metres in length. Billardiera spp. have simple and alternate leaves. In this species, leaves are linear-lanceolate, up to 3 cm long and about 1 cm wide, mid to dark-green, dull in texture, with wavy margins with an overall oblanceolate to lanceolate or long-elliptic shape. Juvenile shoots are very hairy. The flowers are followed by berries about 2 cm long which resemble a minature green kiwi-fruit;  ripening to brown-purple and covered in fine hairs – giving a felt-texture. A nice plant to grow. It is a slender climber which can be used on small fences or supports. Out in the open, without support, it will form a sub-shrub and can make a useful groundcover, potentially to 1 metre tall.
species.maintenance: No Maintenance

species.description: Blechnum gibbum Silver Lady is a charming fern with a compact growth habit and delicate fronds that are silver-green in color. Its low maintenance needs and striking appearance make it an excellent choice for both indoor and outdoor spaces. The Silver Lady’s charm lies in its captivating combination of texture and form. Its fronds, known as pinnae in the botanical world, cascade outwards in a graceful arch, reminiscent of a feathered fan. Each pinnae boasts a vibrant lime-green hue, accentuated by a subtle silver shimmer that dances in the light. This unique coloration arises from tiny hairs on the underside of the fronds, giving the Silver Lady its distinctive name.
species.maintenance: Keep moist during dry periods. Water every second day during dry periods. Apply a slow release fertiliser during spring and a liquid based fertiliser every 4 weeks during the warmer months, take care to dilute your solution to half the recommended dose to avoid burn. Re-pot every 2 - 3 years to keep soil fresh and full of nutrients. The best time to pot is in the cooler months when the plant is dormant.

species.description: Indigenous fern with upright rosettes of bright-green fishbone fronds, often forming a short trunk with age. Strong repeating form for moist, shaded ground.

species.height_raw: Depending on the species and growing conditions, Blue Devil can reach a height of about 30 to 90 cm
species.description: Eryngium ovinum, commonly known as Blue Devil, is a herbaceous perennial plant native to Australia
species.maintenance:
1. Watering: Blue Devil prefers well-drained soil and is somewhat drought-tolerant once established. Water regularly, especially during dry spells, but avoid waterlogged conditions.
2. Pruning: While not strictly necessary, you can deadhead spent flowers to encourage more blooms and trim back any dead or damaged foliage to maintain a tidy appearance.
3. Fertilization: Blue Devil generally doesn't require heavy fertilization. A balanced, general-purpose fertilizer applied in spring can be sufficient.

species.description: Borage is a hardy, prolific self-seeding annual, well known for its striking blue star shaped flowers during the warmer months. The large green-grey leaves are oval shaped and may be quite bristly. The stems are a similar colour but the prickly, white hairs, along the stems, create an impression of a silver coloured plant. Borage is a great addition to the garden and is also known to be one of the best bee and wasp attractants. It was given the nickname ‘bee’s bread’ many years ago. Borage flowers are edible and can be used as a garnish for salads, dips and soups. You can make ice cubes by setting the flowers in water, then chill and decorate your summer drinks. Adding the flowers to herbal vinegar will create a delightful pale violet colour.
species.maintenance: Borage doesn’t need pruning, but can be cut by a third with no ill effects. You can cut off young leaves for use in cooking and flowers when they are new and fresh. For a continuous supply of young leaf matter, you should remember to sow more borage seeds every three weeks during the growing season.

species.description: Boronia megastigma, Brown Boronia, is a slender upright Western Australian shrub grown almost entirely for its scent - the most powerfully perfumed of all Australian natives. The nodding bell flowers are chocolate-brown on the outside and bright yellow within, appearing late winter into spring, and the fragrance carries several metres on still mornings. Fine, needle-like foliage gives it an airy, almost heath-like texture to around 1-1.5m. Best planted close to a path, doorway or seating area where the scent can be met at close range.
species.maintenance: Needs a cool, moist but perfectly drained root run - mulch generously and never let it dry out completely. Prefers dappled shade or morning sun with shelter from hot afternoon exposure. Tip prune lightly straight after flowering to keep it bushy. Naturally short-lived (3-6 years); plan to replace rather than rejuvenate.

species.description: This small evergreen shrub with its aromatic leaves and masses of sweetly perfumed lemon bell shaped flowers will make a great addition to garden beds, borders and pots. A wonderful cut flowers for its colour, shape and an unmistakable scent. The oils extracted are used in Aromatherapy.
species.maintenance: Prune after flowering

species.description: Bossiaea prostrata, commonly known as creeping bossiaea, is a prostrate, mat-forming subshrub that is a member of the pea family (Fabaceae). It is a widespread native Australian species valued for its use as a groundcover in native landscapes and for erosion control. It has a prostrate or procumbent (trailing) habit, forming a mat of low-spreading branches, typically growing up to 0.2 meters tall and 0.5 to 1.5 meters wide. The showy, pea-shaped flowers are borne singly or in pairs on long stalks (pedicels). The standard (main upper petal) is orange-yellow with pinkish-brown on the back, while the wings and keel (lower petals) are a striking purple-brown colour. This species is suitable for native gardens, rockeries, parks, and reserves. Its matting habit makes it useful for weed suppression and erosion control. It is known to attract native bees and hoverflies and serves as a larval food plant for the fringed heath-blue butterfly (Neolucia agricola).
species.maintenance: Low maintenance.

species.description: A tropical. shrub-like vine that has colourful flowers for 11 months of the year in warm climates. Height can grow up to 12m+. In cold climates it can be deciduous however it is an evergreen climber. Flowers are generally red, orange, pink and purple, although white and gold are also found. Dwarf varieties are available.
species.maintenance: Water sparingly although do not let it dry out., Fertilise every few months. Prune and train at the end of the season generally Autumn. Mainly pest and Disease free.

species.description: A mounding and compact perennial plant, great for pots and for borders. It is long flowering from mid Spring to Autumn, with sunny yellow flowers.
species.maintenance: A good easy care ground cover apart from needing some extra watering in drought, and a handful of slow release fertiliser in spring.

species.description: Hardy native ground cover with fine ferny foliage and an abundance of lilac daisy like flowers. It has a long flowering time, a compact and rounded growth habit and nice divided foliage, and will send out suckering growth which helps it to be a more robust plant. A great little plant for rockeries, pots and borders, does well in full sun to part shade. Tolerates frost, good for mild acid to alkaline soils. A proven performer over a number of years.
species.maintenance: Mulch and water well during dry season. Clip tyo deadhead and encourage new flowers. An annual feed of native fertiliser.

species.description: Hardy native ground cover with fine ferny foliage and an abundance of lsoft pink daisy like flowers. It has a long flowering time, a compact and rounded growth habit and nice divided foliage, and will send out suckering growth which helps it to be a more robust plant. A great little plant for rockeries, pots and borders, does well in full sun to part shade. Tolerates frost, good for mild acid to alkaline soils. A proven performer over a number of years.
species.maintenance: Mulch and water well during dry season. Clip tyo deadhead and encourage new flowers. An annual feed of native fertiliser.

species.description: Bromeliads are a diverse family of plants that belong to the Bromeliaceae family. They are known for their unique rosette-shaped foliage and vibrant, long-lasting flowers. Bromeliads come in various sizes, shapes, and colors, offering a wide range of options for gardeners.
species.maintenance: Bromeliads are generally low-maintenance plants. They prefer well-draining soil or growing media, such as a mix of peat moss and perlite. They should be watered regularly, keeping the central cup or "tank" filled with water while ensuring that the soil is not overly saturated. Bromeliads benefit from occasional misting to provide humidity. Fertilize them with a balanced, water-soluble fertilizer at half-strength during the growing season.

species.description: A small tree or large shrub with striking, pendulous trumpet-shaped flowers that can range in color from yellow and orange to pink and white. The flowers emit a strong, sweet fragrance, especially in the evening. Bred by Dr. Alistair Hay internationally renowned brugmansia breeder and Australia's leading expert on Brugmansia. The blossoms actively open and close during the day.
species.maintenance: Water regularly. Requires regular fertilizer during growing periods. Mulch to conserve water.

species.description: This lovely perennial plant is known for its unique and eye-catching blue flowers, produced mostly in Spring and appearing at times through Autumn. The unique charm of the flowers makes it a great feature in a container or garden, with each stem bearing masses of tiny blue flowers in a pincushion shape above a cluster of soft foliage. Great for borders and rockeries, it will grow in a range of conditions. Grows in full sun to partial shade and in most soil types if provided with good drainage. Grow from seed- smoke treatment to the seed will improve germination rates and time.
species.maintenance: Relatively low-maintenance native Australian plant once established, primarily needing well-drained soil and occasional pruning. It is a short-lived perennial, often lasting about 3 years in cultivation, so collecting seeds for replanting is recommended.

species.description: Buddleia is one plant that deserves its common name of butterfly bush, as it really does attract butterflies to its sweetly scented flowers. Quick growing and easy to maintain, it is a useful addition to most gardens. Buddleja davidii Buzz Magenta (Butterfly Bush) is a compact deciduous shrub with gracefully arching branches, studded with lance-shaped, gray-green leaves and sweetly scented, elongated panicles of magenta flowers. Borne at the tips of the current year’s growth, the flower spikes are freely produced from mid-summer through early fall and …
species.maintenance: Butterfly bush will tolerate some dryness but will need watering about once a week in really hot and dry weather. During the year trim back the older growth when flowers are showing signs of slowing off and getting smaller.

species.description: Buddleia is one plant that deserves its common name of butterfly bush, as it really does attract butterflies to its sweetly scented flowers. Quick growing and easy to maintain, it is a useful addition to most gardens.
species.maintenance: Butterfly bush will tolerate some dryness but will need watering about once a week in really hot and dry weather. During the year trim back the older growth when flowers are showing signs of slowing off and getting smaller.

species.blurb: Cones of scented ivory flowers right through the warm months, and the best butterfly plant in the garden.
species.description: Buddleja ‘Buzz Ivory’ is easy to grow and problem-free with a super long-flowering period. From June to September, masses of conical heads of scented white flowers are carried on the shrub, providing nectar for pollinators, especially butterflies. The flowers are small but numerous and appear in summer in a long, showy cone arrangement at the end of the growing tips. The flower colour depends on the variety, but can be white, pink or purple—or any shade in between. Buddleia Buzz Ivory is easy to grow; prune in early spring to keep it in shape.
species.maintenance: Low Maintenance

species.description: Native grass-like perennial shrub with long narrow foliage and small star-like flowers which sit on large spikes throughout Spring and Summer. A wonderful native substitute for daffodils, Bulbine Bright Star will fill your garden with aromatic, yellow, starry blooms from September to March. As a thickly-tufted perennial herb, Bulbine Bright Star is perfect for growing in clusters, and is ideal for a rockery, cottage garden or container. The plump, round edible corms or roots are sweet and full of calcium and iron, and are best enjoyed roasted. Bulbine Bright Star is happiest in full sun or part shade in a range of soils and is frost hardy.
species.maintenance: No maintenance. When the leaves of this plant die back in mid-Summer, the corm beneath is ready for harvest. Simply dig them up gently, careful not to disturb the surrounding plants that may still be growing. The Leaves are Not Edible.

species.description: A small shrub usually about 3 to 4m tall which produces abundant small white flowers through Summer. Native to the east coast, the form in the wild varies greatly depending on habitat — ranging from a prostrate shrub to a small tree — in cultivation it is usually grown as a small to medium shrub for garden and landscape settings. The flowers are sweetly perfumed, making this shrub a lovely feature plant, and it’s hardiness makes it a good choice for garden and landscape use. Low maintenance and fast-growing, it performs best in well drained soil and will thrive in conditions from full sun to partial shade. Yearly pruning will prevent it becoming leggy and sparse. Great for attracting wildlife as the dense prickly foliage offers a protective shelter for birds and the flowers also provide an important food source for butterflies and other insects.
species.maintenance: Yearly pruning will prevent it becoming leggy and sparse.

species.description: Dense growing shrub with small deep green foliage oval to oblong 5-6cm long. Small insignificant white flowers.
species.maintenance: Each spring mulch and apply slow release fertiliser and a little manure.  Water well before and after fertilising. After planting prune all plants to the same height. Pruning should be carried out in spring once new growth has darkened, Mulch around the root to maintain cool.

species.blurb: The upright line of the garden — narrow buff plumes that stand through wind and stay standing all winter.

species.description: Majestic ornamental grass with erect feathery flower plumes. Grows up to a height of 60-90cm with deep green arched narrow leaves topped with pinkish-purple flowers. It’s a grass that could easily be weeded out of a young planting, being mistaken for an invasive interloper from a nearby paddock.  But once it’s in flower, it’s another matter.  While only grown for its seed heads, the flowers, seen through the lens of a bonus, are exactly that.  They’re tiny, and held apart like a cloud of minuscule purple gnats.
species.maintenance: Very little maintenance. Cut clumps to ground in late winter.  Flower plumes can be dried.
