species.description: Evergreen woody native shrubs or small trees. Beautiful bottlebrush blooms attract birds and insects. Bottlebrush colours range from bright red to cream, yellow and pink.
species.maintenance: Regular watering and annual feeding with high potash feed. Water weekly in absence of rain saturating as deep as possible but drought tolerant once established. Prune flowers after flowering just behind the spent flower. Mulch around the drip line to retain moisture.

species.description: This native shrub or small tree is very hardy and adaptable to a wide range of locations and soils. It is generally trouble-free, growing to about 4m high and 2m across. The flowers appear as beautiful crimson spikes which are borne in spring and summer. Requiring little to no maintenance, this variety flowers over a lengthy period and the slender, green foliage forms a neat, rounded appearance.

Callistemon Red Rocket is a small and colourful Australian native shrub that produces red tipped new growth on dark green foliage. Great for a hedge or feature plant, coastal gardens, poolside and low maintenance gardens in a sunny or light shade position with well drained soil.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance. Apply a slow release fertiliser that is low in phospherous when planting and apply again in spring if required.

species.description: Callistemon sieberi, commonly known as the River Bottlebrush or Alpine Bottlebrush, is a resilient and adaptable Australian native shrub or small tree widely used in landscaping and revegetation programs. It is known for its attractive bottlebrush flowers that attract native birds and pollinators.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance.

species.description: Small compact versatile bottlebrush to under 1m with scarlet red flowers that give a spectacular massed display of colour that are attractive to birds. Very hardy low hedge.
species.maintenance: Mulch and water regularly until the plant is established, usually around 12 weeks. Prune tips while young to encourage dense growth and fertilise with a slow release native fertiliser in Spring.

species.description: From the Greek kalos = beautiful, kephale = head, referring to the colourful globular flowerheads. Provides nectar for butterflies. Threatened in Tasmania.  Grows up to 50 cm tall by 50 cm wide with many tufts of narrow, grass-like silver-grey leaves. Bright yellow round or oblong flowerheads at the top of slender upright stems.
species.maintenance: No Maintenance

species.description: Calocephalus lacteus is a perennial herb, growing 5–70 cm high and spreading by means of rhizomes to form a dense mat suitable for use as a ground cover. Green-grey foliage gives good texture to garden beds, while the white globular flower heads provide highlights of colour in the ground layer from late spring to early autumn.
species.maintenance: Keep moist all year round. Plants can die back in late Autumn, losing all leaves except those at the tips of the stems. In July or August they will resprout from the base of the plant, and at this time the dead stems can be cut off. Stems lying on the ground may put out roots. These can be pulled out, or dug up and transplanted.

species.description: Calytrix tetragona, commonly known as the Common Fringe-myrtle, is a hardy, widespread Australian native shrub appreciated for its mass of star-shaped flowers and aromatic foliage. It is a popular, low-maintenance garden plant. The flowers attract bees, butterflies, and other insects, serving as an important food source.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance.

species.description: Showing off perfectly shaped small to medium sized formal type flowers in silvery soft pink, Camellia Ave Maria (Camellia japonica) is an award winning rounded evergreen shrub with glossy dark green foliage and an upright growth habit. Camellias flower from late Winter to Spring, adding a touch of colour when the garden can be a little dull.
species.maintenance: Lightly prune every couple of years to create density and maintain shape.

species.description: Camellia Sasanqua Paradise Avalanche (also known as Slimline Avalanche) is a compact form of Sasanqua. With a mature width of 1 meter, making it an ideal choice for evergreen flowering hedges, narrow garden beds, fence and house line planting. Featuring layers of snowy white petals, Avalanche flowers during Autum and Winter, adding breath of fresh air to winter garden landscapes. Ideal for both in ground planting and feature planters, if selecting a container pot, allow adequate room for growth.
species.maintenance: Use a specialist complete fertilizer in spring and early summer. Apply a thick organic mulch annually in spring.

species.description: Camellia sinensis is a species of evergreen shrub or small tree in the flowering plant family Theaceae. Its leaves, leaf buds, and stems can be used to produce tea. The leaves are 4–15 cm long and 2–5 cm  broad. Fresh leaves contain about 4% caffeine, as well as related compounds including theobromine. The young, light-green leaves are preferably harvested for tea production when they have short, white hairs on the underside. Usually, the tip (bud) and the first two to three leaves are harvested for processing. This hand picking is repeated every one to two weeks. The Camellia Sinensis produces a rich display of dense foliage and small, single, white to cream flowers. It is a hardy, long living, spreading shrub that likes acidic soil. It looks great in a feature pot and also makes a wonderful hedge or espalier.
species.maintenance: Leaves need to be picked when young. Keep plants moist during the hot weather.

species.description: Tufting, silvery-green narrow leaved grass-like perennial with a cascading and mounding habit. Great mass planted around ponds and water features as it tolerates boggy sites. Very versatile as this carex is also drought tolerant and grows in sun and part shade. The leaves are as fine as hairs, the colour is a gentle balayage effect from green to golden brown, and each slender cascading blade curls into ringlets at the tip.
species.maintenance: None

species.description: Carex appressa, commonly known as Tall Sedge, is a hardy Australian native tufted perennial. It forms dense clumps of fine, arching, dark green foliage to around 1m, with greenish to reddish-brown flower spikes in spring and summer. Naturally found along creek lines, wet depressions, and floodplains across eastern and southern Australia, it is excellent for damp sites, rain gardens, swales, and erosion control along watercourses.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance. Cut back to 10–15cm every 2–3 years to refresh foliage. Tolerates wet feet and seasonal inundation; appreciates supplementary water in dry summers if not planted in a moist position.

species.description: Carex testacea is an evergreen bronze-orange sedge (which are grass-like plants, but not true grasses). It forms arching, domed mounds of fine foliage to about 60cm in height that shifts in colour with the seasons, and depending on its exposure to direct sun, from a very subtle bronze-olive in the warmer months, to a really lively (and sometimes quite startling) orange in the cold.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance and generally disease free. Divide in early summer and cut out dead leaves.

species.description: Carpobrotus glaucescens is an evergreen soft wooded perennial native to coastal regions of Eastern Australia. It has succulent stems and fleshy three angled leaves. It has a spreading and prostrate habit. From Spring to Autumn it produces deep purple flowers with satiny petals.
species.maintenance: Little to no maintenance.

species.description: Unusual and tough Australian native mounding groundcover great for rockeries or spilling down embankments and over the side of pots, and will flow over rocks and hillocks creating spectacular effects. A very easy care plant that does well in a wide range of soil types, and from cold temperate to subtropical areas. The dense foliage will deter weed growth, adding to the low maintenance aspect. Can take some salt, so is good for coastal gardens. Tolerant of dry spells once established, frost tolerant. Heavy frost may brown the top foliage, but new growth will shoot away in spring.
species.maintenance: Slow release fertiliser for natives in Spring.

species.description: Catananche caerulea 'Major', commonly known as Cupid's Dart 'Major', is a perennial plant known for its striking, dark-centered, lavender-blue daisy-like flowers and upright, grassy foliage. It's a popular choice for cottage gardens and is also favored for dried flower arrangements. The plant is relatively low-maintenance, thrives in sunny locations, and tolerates dry conditions.
species.maintenance: Deadheading spent flowers can encourage more blooms.

species.description: Highly attractive large shrub or small tree with glossy leaves and fragrant blue flowers in summer. This Californian Lilac is commonly grown as a wall shrub, a free-standing shrub or small tree.
species.maintenance: prune to shape after flowering

species.description: Cedrela is frost tolerant, heat and drought hardy and prefers part shade or full sun. As with all trees, they like well drained soil. These trees are native to China, Korea, and Mongolia. Being a narrow, tall and slender trunked deciduous tree, it is perfect for tight spots which is handy for home gardeners with limited space. At most, they are likely to reach around 8m tall and they do become slightly broader with age. The smooth, brownish grey bark becomes grooved as it ages. The twigs are a coppery green and have soft hair. As the season progresses those flamboyant pink pinnate leaves change to a cream colour before maturing to a mid green. In autumn they turn cream/yellow again before they drop off. They have a lot to offer.
species.maintenance: Nil

species.description: This easy to grow, perennial ground cover has been used for centuries as a medicinal ‘brain herb’ by traditional African, Ayurvedic and Chinese cultures and is believed to have anti-inflammation properties. This small, creeping plant enjoys moist soil in a partly shaded position and should grow to about 20cm high by 1m wide. It will help suppress weeds and is a great plant to have in the garden
species.maintenance: Low maintenance

species.description: Snow-in-summer is a perennial flowering ground cover that blooms profusely in the early summer, producing a blanket of notched pristine white flowers that suggest a fresh snowfall. Snow-in-summer grows best in full-sun areas with poor, slightly acidic, and well-draining soil. This drought-tolerant plant thrives and spreads quickly in cool, dry climates with moderate temperatures and will not grow well in humid regions.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance and water needs. Avoid rampant spreading by shearing the flower stems off before the seeds drop. Trimming can be done easily with a lawnmower that's set high or using a string trimmer. Then, carefully clean up the debris that's cut away to prevent it from reseeding. Some cultivars are more compact and less likely to spread uncontrollably.

species.description: This striking tree has beautiful, broad heart-shaped green leaves which turn yellow in autumn. Often multi-trunked, the branches have a distinctive zigzag growth habit. Blossom like flowers appear from late winter to early spring, starting off as deep red coloured buds and opening to pink. In summer, long, flat leguminous seedpods develop and can hang onto the tree until winter.
species.maintenance: After planting water in well and provide a complete fertiliser to the cultivated area. When young will benefit from an application of complete fertiliser each Spring. A little protection from hot afternoon sun and wind.

species.description: Low growing mat forming aromatic herb with finely divided green leaves and white daisy like flowers with yellow centre.
species.maintenance: Trim stems after first harvest of flowers down to 30cm. Do not fertilize. Deadhead old flowers. Water young plants however once established it is drought tolerant.

species.description: The profusion of long lasting waxy flowers on a spreading but dense shrub are the outstanding features of this iconic Australian plant. It is one of the world’s great cut flowers and is used extensively as a backing flower in arrangements. It makes a wonderful feature shrub or screen plant in the garden especially in areas with drier summers. The Chamelaucium flowers are open-petalled and glossy or waxy, hence, the common name waxflower. They also have a resemblance to the flowers of tea trees (Leptospermum). The plant is aromatic and fills the air with a wonderful scent when the oil glands in the leaves are crushed.
species.maintenance: Light trim after flowering

species.description: The profusion of long lasting waxy flowers on a spreading but dense shrub are the outstanding features of this iconic Australian plant. It is one of the world’s great cut flowers and is used extensively as a backing flower in arrangements. It makes a wonderful feature shrub or screen plant in the garden especially in areas with drier summers. The Chamelaucium flowers are open-petalled and glossy or waxy, hence, the common name waxflower. They also have a resemblance to the flowers of tea trees (Leptospermum). The plant is aromatic and fills the air with a wonderful scent when the oil glands in the leaves are crushed.
species.maintenance: Light trim after flowering

species.description: Mexican Orange Blossom (*Choisya ternata*) is a small compact evergreen shrub. It is part of the Rutaceae family and is native to Mexico. It is a round, bushy plant with an abundance of shiny, dark green leaves. Younger leaves start off as lime green before they mature into the dark green colour.  In Spring clusters of small white fragrant flowers appear at the tip of the branches.
species.maintenance: 1500mm x 1500mm can be trimmed. Water regularly until established. Allow to dry our in between.

species.description: Chorizema cordatum, or the heart-leaf flame pea is a dazzling ornamental beauty that grows into a scrambling, mounded shrub around 1 metre high and wide and flowers from late Winter with a dazzling display of hot pink and coral coloured flowers. It is best grown in well drained and light soils, it needs to be well mulched and given adequate moisture during dry periods. Beautifully suited to a rockery or shaded retaining wall where it can scramble along. A wonderful understory plant for layering in the garden.
species.maintenance: Tip pruning is beneficial after flowering to retain a compact growth.
Very low maintenance and fast growing.

species.description: An evergreen groundcovering perennial plant, with beautiful silvery grey foliage and a profusion of golden yellow button flowers from Spring to Autumn. The papery flowers can be picked and hung upside to dry, and can then be used for dried arrangements. A hardy, waterwise, low maintenance plant. Good for massed plantings, rockeries and containers. This plant is a food source for butterflies.
species.maintenance: Some pests have been noted on C. apiculatum. These are chiefly caterpillars which attack the flower buds and leaves. Aphids are also found on new shoots and the decumbent habit of this plant makes it an ideal hiding place for slugs and snails.

species.description: Chrysocephalum semipapposum, commonly known as Clustered Everlasting or Yellow Buttons, is a perennial Australian herb in the daisy family, Asteraceae. This adaptable and hardy plant is valued for its attractive grey-green foliage and clusters of long-lasting, bright yellow flowers. The flowers are small, bright yellow daisies that appear in dense, terminal clusters. They bloom most of the year but peak in spring and early summer. The yellow pappus bristles on the seeds give the flower heads a fluffy appearance as they mature.
species.maintenance: Chrysocephalum semipapposum maintenance is minimal, requiring a winter prune to the base for rejuvenation and to encourage dense growth. It is drought-tolerant but benefits from occasional watering, especially in dry conditions, to extend flowering. The plant is hardy and tolerates frost.

species.description: Compact patio or container shrub also ideal for beds and borders. Open bright pink crepe-paper summer blooms, sometimes with dark red spots; soft sage-green foliage. Good pest and disease resistance. Very free-flowering.
species.maintenance: Mulch and water well, lightly clip over after flowering, and apply a slow release fertiliser.

species.description: Spiney evergreen shrub with rounded fruit 4-6cm with juicy green pulp. Valued for its culinary use.  Bears slightly fragrant flowers have long white petals with purple tinge on the edges. Flowers and fruit appear throughout the year.
species.maintenance: Fertilize biannually with slow-release fertiliser. Needs regular watering but not wet feet.

species.description:
The Citrus × paradisi 'Ruby' is a variety of grapefruit known for its sweet and tangy flavor, vibrant pink to red flesh, and delicious juice. Here's some information about Citrus Grapefruit 'Ruby,' including its description, maintenance, growing conditions, fruit characteristics, and notable features:
Description:
• Citrus Grapefruit 'Ruby' is a subtropical evergreen tree that belongs to the Rutaceae family.
• It typically grows to a height of 15 to 20 feet (4.5 to 6 meters), forming a rounded canopy of dark green, glossy leaves.
• The tree produces fragrant white flowers, which are often followed by clusters of round to slightly flattened grapefruits.
Fruit Characteristics:
• 'Ruby' grapefruits are known for their exceptional flavor, which is sweet, tangy, and slightly bitter.
• The fruit is medium to large in size and has a thin, smooth, and pink to red-colored rind.
• Inside, the flesh is juicy and ranges from pink to deep red, depending on ripeness and growing conditions.
• 'Ruby' grapefruits are often seedless or contain few seeds.
species.maintenance:
1. Watering: Grapefruit trees prefer consistently moist soil. Water deeply but allow the soil to dry slightly between waterings to prevent waterlogged roots.
2. Pruning: Prune the tree as needed to remove dead or diseased branches and to maintain its shape. Pruning is typically done in late winter or early spring.
3. Fertilization: Apply a balanced citrus fertilizer in late winter, early summer, and late summer to provide essential nutrient
Plant shrubs in Spring once soil has warmed up. Leaves picked as required. Feed three times a year - Spring, summer and autumn. During fruiting feed weekly.

species.description: Kumquat (Citrus japonica) is a small to medium-sized, evergreen fruit-bearing tree or shrub in the citrus family, Rutaceae. Native to Southern China, it produces small, oval to round, brightly colored orange fruits that are both sweet and tangy. The fruits have a unique characteristic where the skin is sweet, and the flesh is sour.
species.maintenance: Once established they require very low maintenance. An occassional pruning will help keep their shape. Water deeply and regularly but allow to dry out in between.

species.description:
The Tahitian Lime Tree is a medium-sized, rather showy tree that can easily be trained to produce stunning specimens that really stand out on the patio! Easy to grow and care for, they can be grown either in a container or in the ground. They make great plants for hedging, espalier training or as specimen trees.
The Tahitian Lime Tree produces lime green citrus fruits also known as Persian or Bearss limes. The tree will produce fruit in its first year after planting and fruit production will increase every year. Proper maintenance is key to supporting and encouraging plant health for a productive citrus harvest.
The Tahitian Lime Tree is considered to be the best choice of Lime due to it being more cold-tolerant than other species. It is easy to grow, generally pest and disease free, and it has larger, seedless fruits that have a less acidic flavour than the Key Lime.
The glossy, evergreen foliage looks great all year round and provides a wonderful backdrop for the fragrant, white flowers and edible green fruits. As an ‘everbearing’ plant this tree can provide you with fruit and flowers throughout the year. The fruits can be left on the tree so there will always be a lime ready to pick and use in your drink! They have the strongest, classic lime flavour when green but they are at their juiciest when left to ripen to yellow.
species.maintenance: Maintain regular watering during establishment and through the warmer growing season. Drought tolerant once established and can handle light frost. Watch for pest and treat at the first sign of damage. The limes are ready to pick in winter before the fruit turns yellow.

species.description: Tall thorny attractive tree with evergreen deep green leaves, small scented white blossoms, Looks similar to the Eureka lemon with slightly pitted skin and an oblong shape. Tree height to 6m x Width 3m.
species.maintenance: Tree can be kept to size through pruning. Harvest fruit mainly in winter. Water well until established. Slow and deep watering. Bi-annual feeding of citrus specific fertiliser.

species.description: The world's most popular eating orange, the large fruit is sweet and seedless and easy to peel. Ripens during winter and holds well on the tree.
species.maintenance: Regular tip pruning throughout the year will help to reduce growth, otherwise prune to one arm’s length. A general rule of thumb for all citrus is that you should be able to reach the trunk in the middle of the tree without having to dive into the foliage.

species.description: The Imperial Mandarin is a popular citrus variety that originates in Australia. A large evergreen shrub to small tree that produces fragrant creamy-white flowers followed by medium-sized orange fruit with a fine, smooth, glossy golden-orange skin that tends to look “puffy”. Imperial Mandarin is a robust tree that gives a vigorous amount of mandarins that ripen from June onwards. The skin is easy to peel, and the flesh is very juicy and delightfully strong-scented. The fruits are medium in size, oblate to broadly obovate, with the apex depressed. The rind is very thin, leathery, smooth and glossy, yellowish to pale orange at maturity. There are 9 – 11 segments, with comparatively few seeds, easily separable. The easiness of peeling makes this a very popular fruit with children.
species.maintenance: Annual slow release fertiliser, Keep moist during dry periods, Liquid feed, Mulch well

species.description: Over 250 varieties some climbers and others shrub like. Cool temperature varieties are deciduous.
species.maintenance: Feed in spring with blood and bone or liquid fertiliser. Deep watering in spring maintain moist soil.

species.description: A woody vine that climbs over shrubs and trees up to 3m.  It is noticed as a whitish fluff mass hanging from trees, shrubs and fences. They have separate male and female plants with the female developing a beautiful seed pod.
species.maintenance: Drought and Frosty tolerant.  Prune in late Winter to approx 30-45cm from ground. Prune stems at different levels to create flowers that distribute more easily.

species.description: Strappy dark green leaves and highly coloured trumpet flowers high above on stalks.. Different varieties produce flowers red-orange, yellow and cream.
species.maintenance: Water well in Spring and Summer keep drier in winter to prevent root rot. Use complete fertiliser in Spring. Remove dead leaves as they occur.

species.description: The bush morning glory plant (Convolvulus cneorum) is a beautiful, silvery foliaged shrub that comes from the Mediterranean region of Europe. It has a neat, dense round shape and grows (61 cm. to 1 m.). This evergreen plant is also quite hardy. Its funnel-shaped, showy, (8 cm.) flowers are white with a pink tint. Bees and other nectar loving critters are drawn to these flowers. The bush morning glory plant is drought tolerant, although it does need some additional water in the desert. It requires very good drainage and lean soil, as it is susceptible to root rot and other fungal diseases. Fertilizing and overwatering this plant leads to feeble, floppy stems. The bush morning glory performs best in the sun. It can also survive in shady conditions but will form a looser, sprawling shape and its flowers will only partially open. The bush morning glory is not weedy, so it won't take over your garden like some other morning glories.
species.maintenance: Grows up to 60cm tall and has a spread of 60-120cm. Can attract aphids and spider mites with overwatering otherwise pest free. Cutback after flowering to maintain compact form. Can be propagated by semi-hardwood cuttings.

species.description: A lovely ground cover growing to 10cm tall and 60cm wide. It has bright green leaves and from spring through to autumn produces deep blue, funnel shaped flowers.
species.maintenance: Low water requirements however will benefit from occasional watering during dry weather. Slow release fertilizer in Spring will encourage profuse flowering.

species.description: Coprosma quadrifida is a species of a hardy, evergreen shrub commonly known as the Prickly Currant Bush or Native Currant. It is native to southeastern Australia and Tasmania and is known for its small, sweet, edible red berries. The plant is an erect, often intricate and thorny, open-to-dense shrub that typically grows 2–4 meters high. Its branches are slender and often end in fine, thorn-like spines. The flowers are small, insignificant, and greenish, appearing from September to December. Male and female flowers grow on separate plants (dioecious). Its dense, spiny growth provides excellent cover and a protected habitat for small birds and other native fauna.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance.

species.description: An evergreen shrub with long strappy or broad dark red leaves aging with silver tints. Stately and architecturally pleasing, great for the accent garden or in containers. Mass together for a splash of colour
species.maintenance: Cordylines are surprisingly hardy and worth a go in most protected areas but will prefer full sun to part shade.  Plant in a well drained soil, mulch and fertilise when planting. Feed annually with slow-release fertilizer. Once established only requires watering in hot conditions. Remove lower foliage as it starts to brown. Start from lower to upper.  Can suffer from root rot if drainage is not good. Takes to propagation. Snails, slugs and mealy bugs can be a problem.

species.description:
Coriander is a fast-growing annual herb. It is multi-stemmed, with the stems arising from a single growth point in a loose form. The stems tend to be quite weak, especially those bearing flowers, so as the plant ages the stems tend to flop down with new smaller side shots going upright. This can create the impression of the plant having multiple growth points. Leaves are distinctly fan shaped: however, the leaves along the flower stems tend to be fine and feathery. The regular leaves look like flat parsley, the finer leaves like fennel both of which are coriander’s close cousins.
The white-to-slightly-pink flowers are held in bunches on weak stems. Many pollinating and beneficial insects love these flowers. Seed quickly follows flowers. Technically, the seeds are a fruit, but dried seeds look like small woody nuts. Known as ‘cilantro’ in other countries, it’s easy to mistake coriander for a variety of parsley at first sight. (They are close cousins.) However, crush a leaf and you’ll instantly smell the difference: sharp, rich, pungent and unique. 
Today we tend to associate coriander with Asian cuisines (particularly Thai), but it is a cosmopolitan herb. It was used by the ancient Egyptians for both cooking and medicinal purposes and even rates a mention in the Old Testament.
species.maintenance: Add a controlled fertiliser at planting time. Requires consistent watering.

species.description: medium sized ornamental shrub
species.maintenance: cut stems by 2/3 at end of winter

species.description: A large elegant shrub or small deciduous tree with spectacular Spring and Autumn display. In late Spring open spreading horizontal branches are covered in large rosy pink, petal-like, pointed bracts. In Autumn the deep green foliage turns brilliant reddish purple to scarlet. Mature trees produce strawberry-like fruits.
species.maintenance: Plant in a well drained and well worked soil. Take care to plant the bud union above the soil level. Water in well and keep soil moist until tree is established. Fertilize when planting and again after new growth appears. Prune tree when planting to encourage new growth.

species.description: Native flowering evergreen shrub with small oval dark green leaves, small bell-shaped flowers from Spring to Autumn, peach pink with a cream yellow trim. Height 1.5-2m X 2-3m Width.
species.maintenance: Mulch after planting. A light prune after flowering to keep shape.

species.description: Correa alba, commonly known as White Correa, is a plant species native to Australia, particularly found in coastal regions and heathlands. Evergreen species of shrub with egg shaped leaves with erect white flowers arranged singly or in groups on short side branches. Flowers late autumn to winter. Correa alba provides habitat and food sources for various wildlife species, including birds, insects, and small mammals. Its flowers attract pollinators such as bees and butterflies, contributing to local biodiversity. The dense foliage of Correa alba helps to stabilize soils and prevent erosion, particularly in coastal areas and exposed environments. Its deep root system also aids in soil stabilisation. Like all plants, Correa alba sequesters carbon dioxide from the atmosphere through photosynthesis and stores carbon in its biomass and in the soil. This contributes to mitigating climate change by removing carbon from the atmosphere.
species.maintenance: Feed every six months with native plant food otherwise low maintenance. Plant tends to wilt when dry indicating when to water.

species.description: A useful small to medium sized shrub as it grows in sheltered half shady positions, where it will happily produce its interesting looking pendulous flowers mainly in winter, with spot flowering through the rest of the year.The flowers are used by smaller nectar loving birds for food. A hardy plant, tolerant of medium to higher frost levels and rarely troubled by pests. Naturally grows dense to the ground, occasional tip pruning will create an even more dense habit. Likes some mulch to create a cool moist root run.
species.maintenance: Occasional tip pruning will create an even more dense habit. Likes some mulch to create a cool moist root run.

species.description: A low mounded evergreen shrub with lovely pendulous flowers of orange-red.
species.maintenance: Correas are a great low maintenance plant.

species.description: This is a great low maintenance shrub, hardy enough to be used for council plantings, and attractive enough for the home garden. Upright and dense in growth, it has cream-lime flowers in autumn and winter. It attracts birds to the tubular pendulous flowers. Drought and frost hardy. Good for clay to well drained loams. Needs little attention, maybe a light trim to encourage a more dense habit from time to time.
species.maintenance: Low Maintenance

species.description: A small shrub, generally growing to about 0.5m - 1m in height and width, with small, deep green, oval-shaped leaves. The main feature is its pendulous, tubular flowers in shades of red, orange, or pink, often described as salmon-coloured. It thrives in full sun to semi-shade and prefers well-drained soil, but is adaptable to most soil types, including sandy or coastal locations. The flowers attract nectar-feeding birds, making it an excellent addition for wildlife gardens.
species.maintenance: It's relatively low maintenance. A light prune after flowering (at the end of winter/early spring) will help maintain its shape and encourage new growth.

species.description: Correa reflexa is a low growing, wonderfully hardy shrub that flowers through the year. There are many different forms, from near prostrate to more upright, and yellow cream to pink to red and yellow flowers. The flowers are long and tubular bell shaped, and are attractive to birds and other nectar lovers.
species.maintenance: Best growth and flowering are in a well drained soil with a good compost mulch, and regular watering. Will survive if neglected, and rarely troubled by pests or disease.

species.description: A dwarf shrub with round to oval leathery leaves, bearing a profusion of greenish white bell shaped flowers from autumn to spring.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance. Grow in moist but well-drained, neutral to acid soil in a sheltered, sunny site.

species.description: An old favourite dense mounding shrub with profuse flowering from autumn through winter and on to spring. Great shrubbery plant that is a great small bird attractor.Correa reflexa is a low growing, wonderfully hardy shrub that flowers through the year. There are many different forms, from near prostrate to more upright, and yellow cream to pink to red and yellow flowers. The flowers are long and tubular bell shaped, and are attractive to birds and other nectar lovers. Will survive if neglected, and rarely troubled by pests or disease.
species.maintenance: Prune straight after flowering to encourage new and more dense growth and feed with a good native fertiliser in spring.

species.description: A beautiful small tree with large glossy dark green leaves with a light green reverse with reddish new foliage during the warmer months of the year.  It has rough, fibrous bark on the trunk and branches, egg-shaped to broadly lance-shape adult leaves, flower buds in groups of seven, bright red, pink or orange flowers The outstanding terminal display of large flowers followed by decorative large gum nuts. Honey eating birds love the nectar of the Corymbias.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance.

species.description: An very showy deciduous small shrub / tree growing to around 2-4m tall. It has deep purple round leaves that are often used in the foliage/flower industry. Amazing plumes of flowers that have a 'smokey' effect in spring and summer. The autumn tones can range from orange, reds and yellows.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance. Cut back hard in late Winter or early Spring to promote the growth of new shoots.

species.description: This low-maintenance bountiful evergreen shrub has attractive tiny green leaves that decorate swooping stems, that are also adorned with dark red berries in fall that are attractive to birds. It blooms with small white to light pink flowers in late spring to early summer, which are loved by bees. Thyme leaf Cotoneaster is wonderfully versatile, as it can be used for ground cover, rock gardens, topiary, urban, hedges and even bonsai. It prefers sandy, well-draining soil, but can tolerate a range of soil types as long as they do not retain standing water. It will do best in full sun to partial shade. This is a good plant for providing changing character across all four seasons. It can grow to around 2' tall and 5' wide, and can be pruned as desired, although we think it looks best when it is allowed to grow to its natural form.
species.maintenance: No maintenance

species.description: Cotyledon silver waves is ideal for adding foliage & colour contrast to the garden, silver waves forms masses of large, rippling silver white leaves that are covered in a fine white powder. Pink flowers appear on a tall stem from late summer to late autumn. An ideal addition to rockeries, borders & large containers where it will add colour & form. Prefers a sunny position in well drained soil. A very hardy plant and will take extreme summer heat and winter cold. Cotyledon Silver Waves has low water requirements once established. Water well up until this point and occasionally through warmer summer months. Cotyledon Silver Waves will grow to a height of 30cm and a width of 70cm.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance

species.description:
Pig's Ears is a succulent plant that forms a rosette of thick, round to oblong leaves. The leaves are usually gray-green to bluish-gray and have a powdery or waxy coating, which helps reduce water loss.
The leaves are typically arranged in opposite pairs, and they can vary in size but are generally broad and flattened, resembling the shape of pig's ears.
In late winter to early spring, Pig's Ears produces tall, upright stems with clusters of tubular, pendant flowers. These flowers are typically red or orange, adding a splash of color to the plant.
species.maintenance: Pig's Ears are drought-tolerant succulents. Water sparingly, allowing the soil to dry out between waterings. Be cautious not to overwater, as this can lead to root rot. Remove any dead or damaged leaves to maintain the plant's appearance. You can also deadhead spent flowers to encourage more blooming.

species.description: Crassula ovata, the Jade Plant, is a slow-growing evergreen succulent shrub from southern Africa, prized for its plump, glossy, oval green leaves often tinged with red along the edges in bright sun. Develops a thick woody trunk and branching structure that reads like a miniature tree, eventually reaching 1–2m tall in landscape settings. Produces clusters of small white-to-pink star-shaped flowers in late winter and early spring on mature plants. Tough, drought-tolerant, and architectural — equally at home in pots, rockeries, and coastal-style succulent plantings. Long associated with prosperity and good fortune in many cultures.
species.maintenance: Very low maintenance. Allow soil to dry between waterings; overwatering is the main risk. Tolerates drought and neglect, but appreciates occasional deep watering in summer. Prune for shape any time of year. Frost-tender — protect from heavy frost in cooler climates.

species.description: The ornamental Crocosmia species are popular garden plants for their handsome foliage and vibrant flowers. The erect sword-shaped leaves can reach up to 40 in (100 cm) long in some species, and often feature distinct veining or pleating. Throughout the flowering season, tall arching stems carry sprays of usually 6-petalled funnel-shaped flowers in shades of bright orange and red, with cultivars extending the colour range to include yellows and browns.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance and should be divided when they become very overcrowded.

species.description: Cupressus sempervirens glauca, more commonly known as the Italian cypress or pencil pine, is an evergreen conifer native to the Mediterranean region. This species of tree is a popular garden and park choice due to its columnar growth habit, deep green foliage, and ability to be pruned into a variety of shapes. Let’s take a closer look at this versatile tree.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance. Keep well mulched and water well during dry season.

species.description: Cycnogeton procerum is an Australian native aquatic perennial plant commonly known as Water Ribbons. It is a robust herb with long, glossy, ribbon-like leaves that can be erect or float on the water's surface, growing up to 3.5 meters long.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance.

species.description: Quince, (Cydonia oblonga), a small tree or shrub of the rose family (Rosaceae), grown for its edible fruit. Quince is the only member of the genus Cydonia and is native to Iran, Turkey, and possibly Greece and the Crimean Peninsula. The fruit has a strong aroma and is astringent in the raw state but makes an excellent preserve and is often used to give flavour and sharpness to stewed or baked apples. The flesh takes on a pink colour when cooked, giving an attractive colour to jellies and conserves. Quince plants are much-branched shrubs or small trees and have entire leaves with small stipules (small leafy outgrowths on either side of the leafstalk). They bear large, solitary, white or pink flowers that are similar to those of the pear or apple but feature leafy calyx lobes and a many-celled ovary. The fruit is a golden yellow pome and may be round and flattened or somewhat pear-shaped.
species.maintenance: Quinces need regular water during their first season after planting, and become more drought tolerant after they are well rooted. Fertilize once a year during winter.

species.description: Lemongrass is a clump-forming perennial grass commonly grown for the strong citrus-like flavour in the swollen stem-base. Grown for its culinary attributes, lemongrass is also a valuable ornamental grass in gardens and pots. It is additionally a great mosquito repellent.
species.maintenance: Apply a fish-based liquid fertiliser in late Spring and again in early Autumn.

species.description: Cynara scolymus, commonly known as the globe artichoke, is a thistle-like perennial plant cultivated for its edible flower buds. It is a member of the Asteraceae family and is native to the Mediterranean region. The plant is characterized by its large, deeply lobed, silvery-green leaves and purple flower heads.  It is a member of the Asteraceae family and is native to the Mediterranean region. The plant is characterized by its large, deeply lobed, silvery-green leaves and purple flower heads. The edible part of the artichoke is the flower bud before it blooms, consisting of the fleshy lower portions of the bracts and the heart.
species.maintenance: Relatively low-maintenance perennial vegetable once established. Key to its care is providing full sun, well-draining soil, and consistent moisture, especially during bud formation. Regular fertilizstion, mulching, and occasional division are also important for optimal growth and yield.

species.description: The Dahlia Grandalia White, commonly known as Dahlia, is a stunning flowering plant that belongs to the Asteraceae family. It is known for its large, showy flowers and lush foliage. The plant typically grows to a height of around 2 to 3 feet (60 to 90 centimeters) and has a compact, bushy habit. The foliage consists of green, deeply lobed leaves that create an attractive backdrop for the vibrant blooms
species.maintenance: To ensure healthy growth and abundant flowering, Dahlia Grandalia White requires regular maintenance. This includes watering the plant regularly, especially during dry periods, and providing well-drained soil to prevent waterlogging. Deadheading, the process of removing spent flowers, promotes continuous blooming and prevents seed formation. Additionally, applying a balanced fertilizer during the growing season can enhance the plant's vigor and flower production.

species.description: A prostrate perennial with the brightest blue to purple-blue flowers in Spring and Summer, with contrasting pale centres. It comes from the south of Western Australia, and it can do well in a good range of conditions, but best performance is in well drained soil.
species.maintenance: Low Maintenance

species.description: A prostrate perennial with the brightest blue to purple-blue flowers in Spring and Summer, with contrasting pale centres. It grows from 25 centimetres to a metre across, and is a great groundcovering plant. It comes from the south of Western Australia, and it can do well in a good range of conditions, but best performance is in well drained soil.
species.maintenance: No maintenance.

species.description: A dwarf and compact form of Dampiera linearis, Cobalt Mound is a lovely low maintenance plant for containers and the flower garden, with gorgeous bright blue flowers from spring through to summer.
species.maintenance: Mulch around the plant to deter weeds and conserve moisture.

species.description: Dampiera stenophylla is a low spreading shrub with gorgeous greyish foliage and massed sky blue flowers Spring to Summer. Light frost and drought tolerant. Ideal for containers and hanging baskets.
species.maintenance: Occasional summer water required during periods of low rainfall.

species.description: A showy plant in flower, with lovely blue-purple flowers in spring to summer. Low growing to 1 metre wide, it needs well drained soil, sun to part shade. Withstands light frost, drought tolerant, a bit of extra care with watering will see better growth. Great for planting to spill over walls, in pots and hanging baskets. Most species will grow in light shade, however they do tend to get ‘leggy’ and do not flower as well as they do when grown in full sun. They also do not like humidity, so tropical climates do not suit.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance.

species.description: Daphne odora is an evergreen shrub known for its delightful fragrance and attractive appearance. It typically grows to a height of 3 to 4 feet (0.9 to 1.2 meters) with a slightly wider spread. The plant has a dense and rounded habit, with glossy, leathery leaves that are deep green in color. The leaves are lance-shaped and arranged alternately along the branches. During late winter to early spring, Daphne odora produces small clusters of fragrant flowers at the branch tips. The flowers are tubular and waxy, usually pink or white in color, and emit a sweet, citrus-like scent.
species.maintenance: Slow growing they need very little pruning, with light shaping and damaged stems removed. If repotting handle roots with care. Leaves yellow when overwatered.

species.description:
A must have plant! ‘Eternal Fragrance’ is an awarding winning Daphne suitable
for a variety of garden applications. You will be rewarded with sweetly fragrant
flowers on the deep green to fresh lime foliage on repeated occasions throughout the year. First flush in late Winter and then in early summer and again in Autumn.Unlike other Daphnes, ‘Eternal Fragrance’ will thrive in a full sun position but will also perform in semi shade. A truly outstanding garden and pot performer, proven by over 30 years of development with results that speak for themselves.
species.maintenance:
Low water requirements. Once established requires only occasional deep
watering during periods of extended heat. Plant in a well-drained position which is
critical for success with any Daphne. For optimum results, lightly trim and feed with a slow release fertiliser in summer to maintain shape and vigor. Tolerant of both acid and alkaline soil types.

species.description: Affectionately referred to as the queen of Australian rainforest ‘plums’ the fleshy purple blue fruit of the davidson plum tree or ooray is fast becoming one of Australia’s most sought after native superfoods.

Daviesia leptophylla, known as narrow-leaf bitter-pea or slender bitter-pea, is an erect shrub belonging to the family Fabaceae. It is found in south-eastern continental Australia. This multi-stemmed shrub typically grows up to 2 metres (6 ft 7 in) tall, with angular, ribbed branchlets. From August to December, it produces dense clusters of small, pea-shaped flowers. The standard petal is bright yellow with a maroon base, the wings are dark red with yellow edges, and the keel is dark red. It attracts birds and insects and provides suitable bird habitat.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance

species.blurb: Clouds of fine bronze and gold flowerheads that light up when the sun is behind them.
species.description: Tufted Hair Grass is a clump-forming, cool-season, semi-evergreen grass that makes a low dense tussock of narrow dark green leaves, over which vast airy panicles rise on fine arching stems in early summer. The flowerheads open purplish-green and age through tawny gold to bronze, holding their shape well into autumn and catching low light beautifully when backlit. It is one of the few ornamental grasses that performs genuinely well in part shade, and it prefers soils that stay moist rather than drying out hard. Note that Deschampsia cespitosa is also indigenous to Victoria, occurring in damp alpine and subalpine grasslands with disjunct lowland populations near Woodend, Colac and Dartmoor — though nursery stock is almost always European cultivar material rather than local provenance.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance. Comb dead blades out of the clump by hand in late winter, or cut back to 10cm before new growth starts. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring. Water through extended dry periods — it will brown off and thin if allowed to dry out repeatedly.

species.description: Tough, drought tolerant low maintenance plant for borders, pots or as an accent plant. Foliage is strappy, blade-like and fresh, glossy green in colour. It has attractive blue sprays of flowers followed by blue berries in summer. It is perennial and spreads outwards to form a good-sized clump.
species.maintenance: Very low maintenance.  Water as required until established, mulch well. Ensure crown is not below soil or mulch level. Liquid feed annually.

species.description: Compact, dense green strappy flax lily. Neat, tough and water-wise; small blue flowers. Good tight edging and repeated drifts.

Dianella longifolia, the Pale Flax-lily (also called Blueberry Lily or Smooth Flax-lily), is a tufted, rhizomatous perennial herb in the family Asphodelaceae, endemic to the non-arid areas of Australia. It has grass-like leaves and loose sprays of pale blue, white or greenish flowers with pale yellow anthers, followed by shiny pale blue to purple berries that are eaten by birds. The leaves are good for weaving baskets and making string.
species.maintenance: Thinning out of new growth as required.

species.description: Dianella revoluta, commonly known as the Blueberry Lily or Black-anther Flax-lily, is a hardy, tufted perennial herb native to Australia. Widely distributed across most states, this evergreen plant belongs to the family Asphodelaceae and is a staple in both home gardens and large-scale commercial landscaping due to its resilience. It has long, leathery, strap-like leaves that are dark green to blue-grey. The leaf margins roll downward and inward, which gives the species its name "*revoluta*". Delicate violet to deep blue starry flowers emerge from spring to summer. They feature distinctive bright yellow filament swellings contrasted against dark brown to black anthers.
species.maintenance: Apply a slow-release fertiliser once a year in spring. Pruning or cutting back the foliage to one-third of its height every 3 to 5 years keeps the clump looking compact and vibrant.

species.description: Compact blue-grey strappy cultivar of an indigenous flax lily. Tough, water-wise drift plant with small blue flowers and berries.

Dianella tasmanica, commonly known as the Tasman Flax-lily, is a robust, tufted perennial native to southeastern Australia. Grown for its hardy nature and attractive foliage, flowers, and berries, it is a popular plant for landscaping and container gardening.
species.maintenance: Water regularly until established. Add layer of mulch and fertilise in Spring with acid loving slow-release fertiliser. Remove dead leaves and trim.

species.description: Dianella tasmanica, commonly known as the Tasman Flax-lily, is a robust, tufted perennial native to southeastern Australia. Grown for its hardy nature and attractive foliage, flowers, and berries, it is a popular plant for landscaping and container gardening.
species.maintenance: Water regularly until established. Add layer of mulch and fertilise in Spring with acid loving slow-release fertiliser. Remove dead leaves and trim.

species.description: Dicentra plants typically have finely divided, fern-like foliage and graceful arching stems bearing unique heart-shaped flowers. The flowers hang in pendulous clusters and come in shades of pink, red, and white, depending on the species and cultivar. The foliage is often bluish-green and provides an attractive backdrop for the flowers.
species.maintenance:
1. Watering: Keep the soil consistently moist but not waterlogged, especially during the growing season. Mulching can help retain soil moisture and regulate temperatures.
2. Pruning: After the initial flowering period, you can deadhead spent flowers to encourage more blooms. In late fall or early spring, cut back the foliage to the ground to promote new growth.
3. Fertilization: Dicentra usually doesn't require heavy fertilization. Incorporate compost or a balanced slow-release fertilizer into the soil before planting to provide nutrients.

species.blurb: An indigenous grass with loose, feathery seedheads that catch the light through late spring and summer.
species.description: A tussock forming grass that has feathery flowers held on stems in late Spring, early Summer. Flat hairless leaves to 15 cm long with prominently ribbed upper surface and rough margins. Loose fluffy seedheads green or purplish to 25 cm long.
species.maintenance: Foliage should be cut back hard in Summer.

species.description: Dichondra 'Silver Falls' (Dichondra argentea) is a popular, fast-growing trailing plant famous for its shimmering, silver-grey, fan-shaped foliage. It is primarily grown for its stunning visual impact, creating a "waterfall" effect as it cascades over the edges of hanging baskets, tall pots, or retaining walls.
species.maintenance: Water well until plant is established. Easily propagated from cuttings or divisions.

species.description: A creeping plant that spreads widely from underground stolons, making it a good ground cover. It is also used as a soft lawn alternative which doesn’t need mowing, though it won’t stand up to hard traffic. It grows best in moist lightly shaded areas, preferring clay type soils, but will grow in sunny spots provided it gets some water in dry times. Naturally grows in all areas of Australia. It has insignificant green-yellow flowers at all times of the year.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance

species.description: A very tough tree fern with graceful fronds produced during the warmer months once the plant is established.
species.maintenance: Remove dead or dying fronds once or twice a year. Then feed with rotted manure.

species.description: An evergreen plant with iris like flowers that bloom in summer. Long sword shaped leaves that form clumps. Flowers are light purple to almost white.
species.maintenance: Hardy and low maintenance. Prune year around to control size removing spent flowers and spent leaves. Take care not to over water. Can be prone to spider mites.

species.description: Dodonaea viscosa, also known as sticky hop bush, is a hardy evergreen shrub with a cosmopolitan distribution. It is a highly variable species that is widely planted for its attractive foliage and ornamental winged seed capsules. This plant can range from a small shrub to a small tree, typically growing 2–4 meters tall. It has glossy, narrow, and often sticky leaves. The 'Purpurea' cultivar is especially popular for its rich copper-purple to burgundy foliage.
species.maintenance: Very hardy once established. Deep drink between allowing it to dry out in between. layer with organic Mulch. Prune regularly to retain shape and promote growth.

species.description: The Gymea lily is a stunning, architectural plant, with an upright, clumping growth habit and large sword shaped leaves. It makes an eye catching feature plant when in flower, with long stems which can reach from 2 to 4 metres tall, topped by a large, rich red flower head. The flowers are rich in nectar, often being visited by birds, bees and other insects.
species.maintenance: It is very easy to maintain by simply cutting off the old flower heads and removing any dead or dying foliage in autumn.

species.description: Doryanthes palmeri, the Spear Lily, is a striking Australian native from the rainforest fringes of northern NSW and southeast Queensland. Forms a massive evergreen rosette of long, sword-shaped, deep-green leaves up to 2.5m long, and produces a dramatic spear-like flower spike to 4–5m bearing dense clusters of deep red flowers rich in nectar. Slow-growing but exceptionally long-lived, this is a sculptural feature plant for large gardens and bold ecological design — attracting honeyeaters, lorikeets and other nectar feeders when in flower.
species.maintenance: Very low maintenance. Slow-growing — may take 5–10 years to flower from seed. Remove spent flower spikes after flowering. Tolerates drought once established but flowers better with consistent moisture. Frost-sensitive when young; mature plants handle light frost.

species.botanical_name: Drosera peltata ssp. auriculata Tall Sundew

species.description: Lomandra longifolia, the Spiny-headed Mat-rush, is a robust tussocking perennial forming dense clumps of long, flat, strap-like leaves to around 1 m. In spring it produces spiny-bracted spikes of cream to yellow flowers with a strong honey scent; male and female flowers are on separate plants. Widespread across eastern Australia, it tolerates drought, frost, shade, poor soils and periodic wet, and is valued for erosion control. The leaves were traditionally used for weaving, and the plant hosts the larvae of several skipper butterflies.

species.botanical_name: DUPLICATE — delete (use Eucalyptus radiata (Narrow leaf Peppermint))
DUPLICATE — delete (use Prostanthera ovalifolia (Native Mint Bush))

species.description: Easy care ground cover. Foliage is cylindrical and points upwards like little blue sticks of chalk. Height around 20-25cm. Small white flowers in Spring.
species.maintenance: Easy care with little or no pruning. Propagate from cuttings leaf and stem taken in late summer. Allow to dry in between waterings.

species.description: Echinacea purpurea, commonly known as Purple coneflower, is a perennial flowering plant that belongs to the Asteraceae family. It is native to central and eastern North America and is widely admired for its vibrant blooms and medicinal properties. This herbaceous plant typically grows to a height of 2 to 4 feet (60 to 120 cm) and forms a clump-like habit. The plant features sturdy, upright stems with coarse, dark green leaves that have a rough texture. Atop each stem, you'll find eye-catching, daisy-like flowers with prominent, cone-shaped, spiky centers, surrounded by drooping, ray-like petals.
species.maintenance: Echinacea purpurea is relatively low-maintenance and well-suited for gardeners of varying experience levels. Here are some maintenance tips: Watering: While it can tolerate drought once established, regular watering during dry spells is beneficial, especially in the early stages of growth. Pruning: Deadheading spent blooms promotes continuous flowering and prevents self-seeding. Prune the plant down to the basal foliage in late fall or early spring to encourage new growth. Division: Every few years, dividing the clumps in early spring helps maintain plant health and vigor

species.description: Echinops, commonly known as globe thistles, is a genus of about 120–218 species of flowering plants in the daisy family (*Asteraceae*), prized for their architectural, spherical flower heads. These hardy perennials feature spiny, deeply-divided, grey-green foliage and tall, stiff stems topped by "golf ball" sized flower heads. Blooms are typically metallic blue or violet, though white varieties like 'Arctic Glow' or 'Star Frost' also exist.
species.maintenance: Prune back to the ground in late autumn or after flowering. Divide every 3-4 years to maintain vigor. They thrive in poor, well-drained, or sandy soils. They dislike, and may die in, waterlogged conditions.

species.description: The pride of Madeira is named for its native area, the island of Madeira in the Canary Islands. This flowering shrub is well-loved for its colorful panicles of purple flowers, woody stems, and slender grey-green spiky leaves that appear in early spring. Pride of Madeira has a mounding, low-branching habit. Growing 8 feet tall and 10 feet wide, it makes a dramatic landscape addition. It is a biennial or short-lived perennial. The plant is a great pollinator, making it an ideal companion plant. The striking blooms of this drought-tolerant plant make it attractive to birds, butterflies, and bees.
species.maintenance: Can grow a bit scraggly after 3-5 years.  Drops seeds so can be self-propagating. Lightly prune after flowering cutting only into soft wood.

species.description: With beautiful silver green foliage and large silver pink flower spikes that rocket to the heavens. This Echium species is far more frost hardy than the traditional Blue Pride of Madeira or Echium candicans that is more commonly grown. Making it a wonderful shrub for gardens that may get some harsh frosts. Drought tolerant, it loves a sunny position. And starts its flowering  in late winter, continuing through spring and into summer. It makes a bold statement in the garden reaching 1.5-2m high when in flower. Its flowers attract all sorts of pollinating insects. And are particularly loved by bees, butterflies and nectar birds. An excellent addition for pollinator or bird attracting gardens.
species.maintenance: Can grow a bit scraggly after 3-5 years.  Drops seeds so can be self-propagating. Lightly prune after flowering cutting only into soft wood.

species.description: A hardy, low-growing shrub that produces small, greenish-white flowers in spring and summer, which are attractive to a variety of pollinators, including bees and butterflies. The plant's foliage is also a valuable source of food and habitat for native wildlife, including birds and insects. Tiny abundant fruit appear in Autumn, are yellow or red when ripe with a salty sweet taste. Snack on fruits in the garden or add to salads or fruit salads. Leaf tips can be eaten raw although are strong tasting. Leaves can be boiled and eaten as greens.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance / Draught tolerant

species.description: Silverberry shrubs vary in size and appearance depending on the specific species and cultivar. Generally, they have dense, rounded or spreading growth habits and can reach heights ranging from 6 to 15 feet (1.8 to 4.5 meters). The leaves are typically elongated, oval-shaped, and often have silver or gray undersides, giving the plant its common name. Some Silverberry species produce small, fragrant flowers in spring or summer, which are followed by edible fruits that resemble berries.
species.maintenance:
1. Pruning: Silverberry shrubs generally require minimal pruning. However, you can trim them in late winter or early spring to shape the plant, remove any dead or damaged branches, and promote overall health.
2. Watering: While Silverberry is drought-tolerant once established, it benefits from regular watering during its establishment phase. Afterward, it can thrive with less frequent watering, as it is adapted to various soil conditions.
3. Fertilization: Silverberry shrubs usually do not require heavy fertilization. However, you can apply a balanced, slow-release fertilizer in spring to provide some nutrients for optimal growth.

species.description: Blueberry Ash is a medium to large sized evergreen tree that can grow up to 30 feet (9 meters) in height. It has a dense, rounded canopy with glossy dark green leaves that are elliptical or lance-shaped. The name "Blueberry Ash" is derived from the small blue, berry-like fruits it produces. These fruits are not true blueberries but resemble them in appearance. In Spring, Blueberry Ash produces clusters of delicate, fringed white or pale pink flowers that dangle gracefully from the branches.
species.maintenance: This hardy tree is ideal as a specimen tree, informal hedge and with pruning can be kept as a large shrub.

species.description: Ruby Saltbush is a quaint succulent bearing small berries with a crisp, salty-sweet flavour. grows to 1m
species.maintenance: trim to shape as required

species.description: English Lavender (Lavandula angustifolia) is a fragrant, cold-hardy flowering shrub known for its beautiful purple blooms and silver-green foliage. It's a popular choice for cottage gardens, hedging, and rockeries due to its attractive appearance, strong fragrance, and ability to attract bees and butterflies. English Lavender is also known for its drought tolerance and ability to thrive in well-drained soil and full sun.
species.maintenance:
Remove faded flower stalks to promote continued bloom. You can prune to shape in spring after new stems and leaves appear. A light pruning again in late summer or early fall before the first frost encourages good air circulation, which guards against rot. So if you have the time, pruning twice a year can be beneficial for your plant. English lavender typically blooms only once per season, but some varieties might send up a second flush of blooms after pruning.
Once the plants are well established, in their second season and beyond, it's usually best to prune the new spring growth after the plants leaf out, cutting about one-third of the green stalks. Never cut into the old woody stems. Shearing the plants to about eight inches from the ground in early spring every three years or so helps to control the plants' size and promotes new growth.

species.description: An attractive medium sized open shrub that is worth growing for the showy masses of bell flowers produced from autumn to spring. Peak flowering is in winter, helping to brighten the garden and feed honey eating birds which love them. They are also great for floral work, and can range from deep pink to red and white forms.
species.maintenance: Prune and fertilise after flowering for best results.

species.description: Encourage nectar-loving birds and wildlife to your garden with this medium sized native shrub. Impressive swathes of white flowers appear from autumn to spring, giving life to winter gardens. Endemic to open forests and alpine regions of South East Australia, it prefers full sun to part shade in coarse, well-draining moist soil and is very frost tolerant once established. Prune and fertilise after flowering for best results. H- 1-3m W- 0.5-1.5m

Eremophila Blue Horizon is a low growing ground cover with tidy blue-grey foliage and produces yellow flowers in winter. Plant in a full sun to light shade position in free draining soil, but can handle heavier soils in dryer climates. Ideal ground cover for mass plantings and gardens, or as a low border.
species.maintenance: Use a slow release fertiliser in spring. For a more manicured look, prune in autumn or spring every couple of years.

species.description: A lovely ground cover shrub, with dense soft grey foliage and beautifully contrasting yellow-gold flowers. Main flowering is in spring and summer, with spot flowers in winter and autumn, and birds and other nectar feeders love them. It has a one to two metre spread, and is drought and frost tolerant. Needs a well drained soil and low phosphorus fertiliser, and dislikes excess humidity.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance

species.description: Eremophila White is a fast growing upright native shrub that shows off greenish foliage and gorgeous white to pale pink tubular flowers.
species.maintenance: Maintenance Free

species.description: Eremophila nivea is absolutely striking even when not in flower, nivea Latin *niveus *means snow or snow white, referring to the overall appearance of the shrub, this silver colour contrasts easily with other greens in the garden and make this a stunning feature shrub. This is a medium sized shrub which is native to Western Australia. This sun loving plant is quite hardy and will tolerate mild frosts and drought once established.
species.maintenance: This is a low maintenance plant. Mulch will help maintain moisture but avoid putting it too close to the trunk. Lightly prune to maintain a compact shape.

species.description: Erica melanthera is a compact, bushy, shrub to one metre with bright green, small, needle-like leaves and purple/pink flowers that dominate the plant in Autumn and Winter. When all else is dormant, the Ericas come out to dazzle us with their vibrant displays of colourful bell-shaped little flowers. They are profuse producers of blooms, going well in shruberies or in larger borders as well as in pots and planters on the patio. Excellent for cut flowers, they are generally frost hardy but they do need protection when young and still not fully established.
species.maintenance: No maintenance

species.blurb: Small white daisies ageing to pink, softening every edge and seeding gently into the brickwork.
species.description: Seaside daisy (Erigeron karvinskianus) other common names are beach asters and Mexican fleabane are hardy garden perennials belonging to the family Asteraceae. The plant is native to Mexico and highly resistant to wind and salty sprays. The foliage is greyish green and the plant blooms in large numbers of tiny little daisy flowers, that open pink and slowly fade to a white with age. There are plenty of fine daisy like petals arranged around the yellow coloured central disc. Giving a multi coloured shades of pinks with the two tone pink and white affect.
species.maintenance: A good cut back in Winter will keep this plant looking at its best. Needs regular watering until established.  Apply slow-release fertiliser once established.

species.description: This beautiful European sea holly forms clumps of heart-shaped leaves, over which a profusion of striking anodised blue thimbles appear on vibrant silvery-blue stems from Summer to Autumn. Tolerant of the toughest conditions, \`Blue Sea Holly' may require staking or support in rich soils. This spiky, architectural character adds interest to our sunny border with its colourful stems and spiny-toothed leaves surrounding the domed blue cones. It looks wonderful planted amongst agastache and coneflowers. Also a superb cut flower, beloved of florists.
species.maintenance: Cut back to the ground in late Winter to encourage fresh new growth in Spring and abundant flowering in early Summer

species.blurb: Steel-blue thimbles above spiny collars, keeping their colour and form as they dry.

species.description: Erysimum linifolium, commonly known as the Alpine Wallflower or Spanish Wallflower, is a vigorous, short-lived perennial sub-shrub prized for its exceptionally long flowering season. Native to Spain and Portugal, it forms a bushy mound of narrow, grey-green foliage topped with dense clusters of four-petalled flowers.
species.maintenance: Lightly trim after a flush of flowers to maintain a compact shape and prevent the plant from becoming woody or leggy.

species.description: The California poppy ‘Ivory Castle’ is a refined and distinctive variety, featuring clusters of creamy-white blooms with soft yellow centres that stand atop its fine grey-green foliage. These delicate, silk-like flowers unfurl from pale lemon buds into smooth ivory-white petals, each accented by cream-colored anthers. California Poppies are a hardy annual, growing to 40cm in height and flower extensively throughout Summer.
species.maintenance: Minimal watering and infrequent fertilization are usually sufficient, as it is drought-tolerant once established. Deadheading spent flowers encourages further blooming and prevents unwanted self-seeding

species.description: This graceful, weeping tree grows to 6 m high. Its young stems, leaves, buds and fruit are blue-green in colour and are covered in a showy white, waxy bloom, that is, they are glaucous. The mature trunk has decorative minni-ritchi bark—bark that peels in small curly flakes but does not detach. The trunk, bark, foliage, flowers and fruit are all very appealing attributes. The oils extracted from this tree have medicinal properties.
species.maintenance: This tree has a natural irregular and weeping form that forms part of its character and it is therefore difficult to prune. Some light pruning can be done once established if desired, including cutting stems for floral arrangements. It can be cut at the base and allowed to re-shoot.

species.description: The river red gum is an iconic tree species of the Australian landscape. For anyone who has grown up along our inland rivers, this majestic tree has provided the backdrop for a myriad of childhood memories. We have climbed its branches, collected leaves and gumnuts, played, and rested in its shade. River red gum forests and connected wetlands are biodiversity hotspots - home to a long list of native plants and animals. They provide important ecosystem services for surrounding landscapes, communities and farms.

Eucalyptus cephalocarpa, commonly known as Silver Stringybark or Mealy Stringybark, is an adaptable Australian native tree prized for its aromatic silver-grey foliage and robust nature. It is a medium-sized evergreen tree typically found in Victoria and southern New South Wales. Its striking silvery foliage and dense canopy make it a popular choice for gardens and parks.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance.

species.description: The Corymbia citriodora dwarf, often known by cultivars like 'Scentuous' or 'Lemon Essence', is a compact, grafted version of the classic Lemon-Scented Gum, ideal for smaller gardens, offering strong lemon-scented foliage, attractive smooth pink-white bark, and cream flowers, making it a versatile, hardy, and aromatic Australian native feature tree for sunny spots with well-drained soil, attracting birds and insects.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance, native fertiliser twice per year.

species.description: Eucalyptus leucoxylon 'Rosea' (Pink Flowering Yellow Gum) is a popular, fast-growing Australian native tree prized for its stunning pink to red flowers, blooming from autumn to spring. Typically growing 6–10 meters tall, this hardy, evergreen tree is ideal for attracting birds and pollinators to, gardens, parks, and streetscapes due to its high nectar production.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance.

species.description: This is the shrub-form of 'Baby Blue'. It is a small-growing eucalypt usually seen as a tall, spreading shrub that retains its juvenile foliage into maturity. Young leaves, stems and inflorescences have a powdery white bloom. Foliage is strikingly silvery-grey and round in form. Cream flowers are produced between May and November and the large fruits that follow are cup-shaped. We prune the shrub-form of 'Baby Blue' to force division on the branches making it grow shorter and with wider lateral branching.
species.maintenance: While it is drought-tolerant once established, Baby Blue Silver Dollar Gum benefits from regular watering during its establishment phase. Once mature, it can tolerate periods of dryness. Baby Blue Silver Dollar Gum typically does not require heavy fertilisation. A balanced, slow-release fertilizer applied in Spring can support healthy growth.

species.description: Eucalyptus radiata, commonly known as the Narrow-leaved Peppermint or Forth River Peppermint, is an Australian native tree known for its aromatic foliage and versatile uses, particularly in essential oil production. It produces profuse clusters of small, white to cream flowers from October to January. The fruits are small, cup-shaped or hemispherical, and arranged in radiating clusters, which gives the species its name radiata.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance.

species.description: Eucalyptus rubida, commonly known as candlebark, is a large, evergreen tree native to elevated regions of south-eastern Australia. It is prized for its attractive, smooth, pale bark that develops a red or pinkish hue before shedding in strips, especially in late summer. Typically grows as a medium to large tree, reaching a height of 10-30 metres, occasionally up to 40 metres.  Its striking bark and form make it a popular decorative tree for large gardens, parks, and avenue plantings, where ample space is available.
species.maintenance: Eucalyptus rubida is a low-maintenance tree once established in a suitable location. Key maintenance activities focus on correct planting, watering, and occasional pruning.

Pruning not required but cutback to base after flowering is recommended.  Low water requirement but do not let dry out. CAUTION: Wear gloves when handling as milky sap is an irritant to skin and eyes.  no known pests.

species.description: Euphorbia 'Wickstead' is a spreading herbaceous perennial with red/orange flushed olive green leaves that turn red in Autumn. It has clusters of similar coloured floral bracts in Summer.
species.maintenance: Prune old stems to the ground in late summer or autumn to encourage new growth.

species.description: A useful foliage and flowering plant. The spiralling leaves are so symmetrically formed, they look like they belong on a reptile rather than a plant. Flowers start acid green then fade to a dusty pink in late winter and spring. Cut old flowers off at the base to maintain habit and stop their incidental spread.
species.maintenance: Very low maintenance. Self seeding if not deadheaded. Fertiliser is best avoided. Gloves and Eye protection is required to protect against the saponin within the plant.

species.description: It blooms with a froth of lime-green heads over spring-summer, above a mound of neat emerald foliage. And the “flowers” are exceptionally durable in all weathers as they are actually bracts. So they remain unspoiled for ages no matter what the weather does.Then in autumn and winter it is the turn of the foliage to star, when it reacts to the cold by colouring up to vivid reds and purples.
species.maintenance: Minimal.

species.description: The Mediterranean spurge is a show-stopper during the late winter to early spring when the winter rains provide moisture for robust growth and flowering. The combination of blue-green foliage and chartreuse flower bracts achieve the appearance of giant puff-balls in the garden. No other plant achieves this unique color and character combination. This unusual dry-tolerant perennial flowers for a long time in sun or shade. Large lime-green flowers lift the winter garden, with blue-grey foliage creating a striking contrast among spring and summer flowering perennials.
species.maintenance: Water when dry for the first year. Prune back to ground after flowering. Can be subject to Mildew if circulation is poor.

species.description: Euphorbia x martinii, commonly known as Martin's spurge, is a dwarf, evergreen hybrid sub-shrub prized for its architectural form and colorful foliage and flowers. It is a natural cross between Euphorbia characias (Mediterranean spurge) and Euphorbia amygdaloides (wood spurge), discovered in southern France. The plant forms a dense, mounding rosette of narrow, dark grey-green leaves. New growth often has a reddish or burgundy flush, which can turn pink in cooler months.
species.maintenance: Cut back the spent flowering stems to ground level in late summer or fall to encourage new, vigorous growth and a bushier habit.

species.description: Wasabi is a lush evergreen perennial with large, heart-shaped leaves. The foliage makes a statement in the shade, while the rhizome can be harvested for cooking after two years. Wasabi plants are fragile, so avoid high-traffic areas, where breakages are more likely.
species.maintenance: Water daily in warm dry weather. Wasabi is a water plant in its natural habitat, so needs to be watered regularly. Annual applications of well-aged manure are ideal. In Spring a good layer of Mulch will keep the soil cool and moist.

species.description: Fatsia japonica, the Japanese Aralia, is an evergreen shrub from the coastal woodlands of southern Japan and Korea. Its signature is the leaf — large, glossy, deeply palmate with seven to nine lobes, often 30–40cm across, held on long stalks from upright multi-stemmed growth to 2–3m.
