Produces branched panicles of creamy-white spherical flowers in late autumn and winter, followed by small black berries. One of the best architectural shade shrubs available: it holds structure and gloss year-round and reads beautifully against fine-textured foliage.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance. Shelter from hot afternoon sun and drying wind — both cause leaf scorch and browning margins. Keep soil moist and mulched. Prune leggy stems back hard in spring to encourage branching from the base. Watch for scale and mealybug on the leaf undersides.

species.description: Fennel (Foeniculum vulgare) is a perennial herb with a distinctive aniseed or licorice-like flavour. It is characterised by its feathery, finely divided leaves, tall, erect, and hollow stems, and flat-topped clusters of small yellow flowers. Native to the Mediterranean region but widely naturalized elsewhere, often found near the coast and riverbanks. Fennel is used as a culinary herb for flavoring dishes, as a vegetable (Florence fennel bulb), and for its medicinal properties, with seeds and extracts used for various health benefits
species.maintenance: Fennel is generally a low-maintenance plant. Key maintenance tasks include watering, especially during dry periods, and weeding around young plants to reduce competition for resources. Fertilising may be needed in poor soil, and pest control (like snail bait) might be necessary.

species.description: The brightest colour fescue grass, Elijah Blue is an outstanding small ornamental grass with fine slender steel-blue foliage all year round. A neat compact rounded habit that tucks into all kinds of spaces.
species.maintenance: Divide every 2 -3 years to keeps plants healthy, otherwise the centre will die out over time. Remove old blades by combing your fingers through the tussock.

species.description: A versatile and hardy sedge grass, Knobby Club Rush is an upright to gently weeping sedge with evergreen deep green cylindrical foliage. It is ideal for coastal gardening as it can take total coastal exposure. Although it is native to the coast, Knobby Club Rush also grows well in inland gardens. Ficinia nodosa was formally known as Isolepis nodosa and is commonly called 'Knobby Club Rush' - after its knobby looking seed head. It makes a great contrast plant for other foliage grasses. Although native to the coastal zone, it grows well in protected inland climates and it can cope with light frost. It may yellow a little in cold inland winters but will green up again in spring.
species.maintenance: Trim back foliage to 20cm above the ground every second year to remove older foliage

species.description: Fast growing medium sized deciduous tree growing 3-5 metres tall. During summer masses of dark red fleshed fruit are produced. it is self pollinating and produces two crops a year.
species.maintenance: Fertilise at least twice a year especially if leaves are yellowing early spring and late summer. Granular slow release is best. Can be prone to Rust, Consistent moist soil is required when fruit is on the tree.
Fertilise in Spring with long term slow release.  Prune to shape and contain growth.

species.description: Ficus pumila, also known as Creeping/ Climbing Fig, is an evergreen climber with rich, green, ovate, heart-shaped leaves. It’s known for being a vigorous and fast-growing climber as it attaches itself to everything it encounters via adhesive aerial rootlets. Pear-shaped fruits can appear on plants throughout the year, and when this is the case, fruit-bearing stems may have foliage that is larger, thicker, shinier and elliptic in shape.
species.maintenance: Pruning is essential for controlling Ficus pumila – if you’re using it along fencelines/ walls, you ideally want to keep a thin profile rather than allowing it to become bushy. Ensure you are pruning when necessary to ensure the Ficus doesn’t grow where you don’t want it. In the first few years of growth, it will require minimal maintenance as it grows – especially if the idea is to cover a large wall.

species.description:
Stenocarpus sinuatus, commonly known as the Firewheel Tree, is a striking and ornamental tree native to the rainforests of eastern Australia.                                 • Foliage: The Firewheel Tree is an evergreen tree with glossy, dark green, pinnate leaves. Each leaf typically has several leaflets.
• Flowers: The most distinctive feature of the Firewheel Tree is its large, showy flowers. The inflorescence is a wheel-like cluster, and individual flowers within it are red to orange-red, resembling a fiery wheel, which gives the tree its common name.
• Fruit: The tree produces woody capsules that contain seeds.
species.maintenance:
1. Watering: While it prefers moist conditions, the tree is relatively adaptable to different moisture levels once established. Water regularly, especially during dry periods.
2. Pruning: Prune to maintain a desirable shape and remove dead or crowded branches. However, major pruning should be done after flowering to avoid removing potential flower buds.

species.blurb: Smoky bronze foliage and flat yellow heads, aniseed-scented, with seedheads that hold into winter.

species.description: Foxglove (Digitalis purpurea) is a striking biennial or short-lived perennial plant that is native to Europe and has naturalized in many other regions. It features a tall, erect stem that can reach heights of 3 to 6 feet (0.9 to 1.8 meters). The leaves are large, lance-shaped, and arranged in a basal rosette during the first year of growth. In the second year, the stem emerges and bears dense clusters of tubular-shaped flowers.
species.maintenance: Foxglove plants require moderate maintenance to thrive. They prefer well-drained soil that is rich in organic matter. Adequate moisture is essential, so regular watering is necessary, especially during dry periods. Deadheading spent blooms can encourage prolonged blooming and prevent self-seeding. In colder climates, applying a layer of mulch around the base of the plant in late fall can provide some protection during winter.

species.description: Alpine strawberries are much prettier than the beefy modern garden varieties, with small white flowers and fruit held high, often above the leaves.
species.maintenance: Pick and Eat. A complete fertiliser that’s boosted with extra fruit-encouraging potassium to help promote a great berry harvest.

species.description: Fritillaria persica, commonly known as the Persian Lily, is a striking perennial bulbous plant native to the Middle East, including regions like Turkey, Iran, and Syria. It is highly prized for its architectural form, featuring tall spikes that can reach up to 90–120 cm (3–4 feet) and carry up to 30 pendulous, bell-shaped flowers.
species.maintenance: Remove the faded flower spikes as soon as they wither. This prevents the plant from wasting energy on seed production and redirects it back into the bulb. Maintain consistent moisture while the plant is growing and blooming. Provide approximately one inch of water per week if there is no rainfall. Avoid waterlogging, as this is the primary cause of bulb rot.

species.description: The snowdrop’s Latin name is *Galanthus*, meaning milk-white flower. From a distance, all snowdrops look pretty much the same. But on closer inspection there are subtle variations in flower size, shape and markings. Each snowdrop bulb produces two or three long, narrow leaves and one stalk, topped with a snowy-white flower. The blossoms have three large outer petals (sepals) and three much smaller inner petals that overlap to form a tube that’s typically adorned with lime-green markings. The flowers dangle from arching, whisper-thin stems that allow them to bob to-and-fro in the lightest breeze. On sunny days, the outer petals rise and make the blossoms look like they’re ready to take off. Snowdrops are best planted en masse for a great display. They naturalised when left undisturbed. They grow well in borders, at the base of shrubs or deciduous trees, or part of a woodland setting.
species.maintenance: Water well to keep the soil lightly moist. They do not like to dry out except when dormant. Fertilise in Spring with a slow release fertiliser. They usually multiply quick but should not be disturbed for at least 3 years before they can be divided. They can be divided once the foliage has died back.

species.description: Large sweetly fragrant double white flowers, glossy dense rich green foliage to 1.5-2m. Ideal for hedging, and as a cut flower to enjoy the perfume indoors. One of our most popular Gardenias.
species.maintenance: Mulch and water well, prune after flowering if required. Feed with a fertiliser for acid-loving plants every 2-3 months. Water regularly with seaweed solution. Spray with Eco-Oil to kill aphids, scale, and other pests.

species.description: Gardenia jasminoides, commonly known as Gardenia, is an evergreen shrub with glossy, dark green leaves and beautiful, fragrant flowers. It typically grows to a height of 3 to 6 feet (0.9 to 1.8 meters) and spreads about 3 to 4 feet (0.9 to 1.2 meters) wide. The leaves are leathery, oval-shaped, and arranged opposite each other along the stem. The flowers are large, white or creamy white, and have a distinctive waxy texture. They usually appear in summer and emit a sweet, intoxicating fragrance that fills the air.
species.maintenance: Require weekly light watering. Fertilise with acid-loving fertiliser in spring and summer. Mulch with woodchip or sawdust. Aphids can be a problem. Yellow leaves could mean lack of water.

species.description:
Butterfly Bush is a bushy, hardy perennial shrub with long graceful stems that bloom with pink and white flowers in spring-summer. These stems grow up to 1m long, but can be clipped back shorter, and sway gracefully in the breeze.
The name of a popular variety, Whirling Butterflies, perfectly describes the way the plant resembles a cloud of butterflies when swaying in the breeze. This variety is predominantly white, with hints of pink in the flower buds.
species.maintenance: Prune as required.

species.description: Genista — commonly called broom–bears sweet pea shaped yellow flowers from spring into summer. Genista has arching branches; species range from almost prostrate shrubs that can be used as ground cover to large shrubs reaching to 15 feet (4.5m) tall. Genista is called broom; the branches were once used for making dust brooms. Genista is related to the genus Cytisus, also commonly called broom. Genista is less aggressive than Cytisus or Spartium (Spanish broom) and will not run wild or become invasive. Genista tolerates rocky and infertile soil and thrives in full sun.  Left to their own devices Genista are very good at self-seeding and colonising any bare ground nearby.
species.maintenance: Very low maintenance. Taller growing varieties will make exponential growth and some pruning back of this new growth after flowering may well be sensible to keep the plant under control. However, you must be careful not to prune back hard into the old wood as this will not so readily reshoot and you may end up with a lopsided or unsightly plant.

species.description: Garden strawberries are excellent for both covering the ground and for growing fruit.
species.maintenance: Keep strawberry beds mulched to reduce water needs and weed invasion. Any type of mulch—from black plastic to pine straw to shredded leaves—will keep the soil moist and the plants clean

species.description: Over 300 varieties and a big range of shapes and colours. Most are low spreading plants with hairy, hand shaped leaves,
species.maintenance: Only requires a light watering after establishment. prune in late autumn before frost to maintain bushy habit. Leave to dry between watering. Regular fertilizing should be regular with a slow-release fertilizer. Fungal rust can be treated with fungicide. Water plant base only.

species.description: Ginkgo is a hardy, pest-resistant, and attractive large tree. It has unusual fan-shaped leaves that turn vivid yellow in fall. Only male trees should be purchased, as the females produce seeds with a soft, fruitlike covering that can be messy and have a potent odor.
species.maintenance: Very low maintenance. Slow to establish — water regularly through the first two or three summers, then largely self-sufficient. Requires almost no pruning: the narrow upright form develops naturally and central-leader pruning only spoils it. Effectively pest and disease free. 'Princeton Sentry' is a male clone, so it produces none of the malodorous fruit of female Ginkgos. Sweep or collect the leaves after the fast, near-simultaneous autumn drop.

species.description: A medium size tree with a fast growth rate and an open, rounded pendulous habit. The new fern like foliage is golden at the tips of the branches and pale green throughout the rest of the tree. Autumn foliage is golden yellow.. Pendulous branches sweep to the ground creating a graceful, colourful effect. Frost and drought tolerant, this variety has minimal thorns.
species.maintenance: Fertilise after new growth appears and prune to shape if necessary.

species.description: Glycine clandestina is usually a wiry, twining plant whose thin stems twist around the stems of other plants. Its habit is inconspicuous and it is often not noticed until the flowers appear. It is not especially vigorous and does not overwhelm other plants. The leaves are arranged alternately on the stems and are 3-foliolate with the middle leaflet usually longer in length than the other two. The leaflets are linear to lanceolate in shape and up to 40mm long by 10mm wide. The flowers, which appear in winter and spring, are usually mauve to pale pink and white. They are the typical “pea” shape consisting of 4 petals; the “standard”, the “keel” and two “wings” as shown in the accompanying diagram. The flowers are followed by elongated pods up to 40 mm long. The flowers are a source of nectar and pollen for bees and wasps.
species.maintenance: No watering required once established except for long dry periods.

species.description: Fast-growing native sprawling shrub-groundcover with cheery little yellow flowers for a long season, ideal for naturalising and underplanting in garden borders, and wildlife gardens. Happy almost anywhere you grow it, and home to native butterflies.
species.maintenance: Continue to water regularly until the plant is established, usually around 12 weeks. Hard prune after flowering to keep it dense and flowery. Feed with a slow release native fertiliser during spring.

species.description: Goodia lotifolia, commonly known as Golden Tip, Clover Bush, or Clover Tree, is a fast-growing, vigorous Australian native shrub. It is widely celebrated for its striking spring display of fragrant, bright yellow flowers and its soft, clover-like foliage.
species.maintenance: Because of its vigorous, fast-growing nature, it requires light pruning directly after flowering to maintain a compact shape, promote fresh growth, and prevent it from becoming overly sparse or leggy.

species.description: Upright tufted herb to 30 cm long, sometimes creeping. Leaves clover-like with wedge-shaped leaflets to 15 mm long, held on stalks up to 40 mm long. Flowers and fruits are above the leaves

Fast growing, tough hardy old favourite, grow it as a shrub or tree for the bird-attracting bright yellow blossoms and fine ferny foliage.  A good feature or screening plant but needs to be pruned regularly and from a young age to keep a reasonably compact shape. Tolerates moderate frost levels and dry spells once established.
species.maintenance: Pruning as required, slow release fertiliser

species.description: A spreading medium sized shrub. Very similar to ‘Robyn Gordon’ but has greyish foliage with broader lobes. Flowers through the year with large red flowers. A great feature shrub or screen plant. Tolerates light frost and dry spells. A single glance is enough to appreciate ‘Molly’s’ captivating charm. With its delicate, fern-like foliage, it creates a backdrop for its mesmerizing flowers, showcasing a kaleidoscope of reds, pinks, and oranges. These flowers are unique, resembling spider-like structures, each petal a slender, graceful strand. This vibrant display adorns ‘Molly’ from late Spring to early Autumn, bringing joy and colour to the garden throughout the warmer months. Besides its aesthetic appeal, Grevillea ‘Molly’ plays a crucial role in supporting local ecosystems. Its vibrant flowers attract native pollinators, like bees and butterflies, making your garden come alive with buzzing activity.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance

species.description: A small plant growing to around 1-1.5 metres high and wide,  with eye catching large flowers in shades of pink, orange and yellow for most of the year. Bird attracting and great cut flowers. Fast growing and easy care, just a light trim after flowering and a handful of low phosphorus fertiliser in spring and summer is all that is needed. Likes a well drained soil, sun to light shade.
species.maintenance: Light trim after flowering and a handful of low phosphorus fertiliser in spring and summer.

species.description: Grevillea juncifolia, also known as the honeysuckle grevillea, is a bushy, drought-tolerant shrub or small tree native to the arid inland regions of Australia. It is prized for its showy, nectar-filled, yellow-to-orange flowers, which attract native birds and insects. Grevillea juncifolia grows to a height of 2 to 7 meters and has a distinctive greyish appearance. The foliage consists of long, linear, rush-like leaves that are grey and covered with fine hairs.
species.maintenance: Lightly prune the plant after the main flowering season to encourage a bushier habit and promote more flowers.

species.description: A great ground covering grevillea forming a thick spreading mat. It has dense foliage with close set small mid green leaves, giving a very attractive appearance even when not in flower. It has small pink spider type flowers in winter to spring. It is drought and frost tolerant, and is best in cooler areas, and dislikes humid conditions. The cooler weather sees the foliage change to a rich burgundy colour. Late spring to summer sees an abundance of rich red toothed flowers.
species.maintenance: Prune after flowering.  Take care not to disturb roots.

species.description: A great ground covering grevillea forming a thick spreading mat. The cooler weather sees the foliage change to a rich burgundy colour. Late spring to summer sees an abundance of rich red toothed flowers.
species.maintenance: Prune after flowering.  Take care not to disturb roots.

species.botanical_name: Grevillea leiophylla x Grevillea humilis subsi. maritima
species.description: A delightful dwarf shrub with pink spider flowers and fine, narrow foliage. Great feature plant for small gardens as well as for pots. Grevillea leiophylla is a weakly erect to low-lying shrub that typically grows to a height of 20–60 cm, and has ridged branchlets. Its leaves are often crowded, narrowly oblong, narrowly egg-shaped with the narrower end towards the base or more or less linear, 20–60 mm long and 1–3 mm wide. The flowers are arranged on the ends of branches in groups of 8 to 24 on one side of the rachis and pale to deep pink, the style pink turning red with age, and the pistil 6–10 mm long. Flowering mainly occurs from August to November, and the fruit is a follicle with small lumps and about 9 mm long.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance

species.description: Grevillea levis is a dense shrub that typically grows to a height of 1–2 m , its branchlets glabrous. The leaves are mostly 20–30 mm long and divided with three to five lobes, the end lobes linear, 5–20 mm long and 0.3–0.8 mm wide, the edges rolled under, the tip sharply-pointed. The flowers are arranged in more or less spherical or domed clusters on a glabrous rachis. The flowers are white to cream-coloured, sometimes tinged with pink, the pistil about 3.5 mm long. Flowering occurs from May to October and the fruit is an oval to oblong follicle 6–9 mm.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance and drought hardy. Requires little or no maintenance.

species.description: Grevillea 'Elegance' is a popular Australian native hybrid (a cross between Grevillea longistyla and Grevillea johnsonii) known for its rapid growth and bird-attracting floral display. It is a versatile choice for privacy screening or as an ornamental feature in native gardens.
species.maintenance: Lightly prune after the main flowering period to maintain a dense shape and prevent it from becoming "woody" or sparse. Use a low-phosphorus native-specific fertiliser (P ratio under 3%) during the growing season.

species.description: An attractive medium sized shrub that has a main flush of pendulous attractive red flowers in spring to summer, with spot flowering through the rest of the year. A great native bird and bee attractor that prefers well drained soil. Great for a low border or to plant in a container.
species.maintenance: It responds well to pruning to create a more dense plant.

species.description: Grevillea rosmarinifolia is a hardy, native, evergreen shrub. It has dense rosemary like foliage and will produce spidery like flowers that are red/pink with a touch of white on the end of the branches. Flowering from Winter through to early Summer, this tough shrub is tolerant of moderate frosts and drought once established. Prefers well drained but not too moist soils that are slightly acidic. Fantastic in beds or borders.
species.maintenance: No Maintenance

species.description: An attractive and easy care medium sized shrub which flowers over many months from autumn through winter and on into spring. The flowers are spider shaped and mauve in colour, and are attractive to bees. An adaptable plant for sun to part shade, prefers well drained soils. Can be left to grow on its own where it will form an attractive informal shape, but also responds well to regular pruning for a more compact habit.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance but responds to a light prune for a more compact habit.

species.description: Grevillea synapheae is a low, spreading, and ornamental shrub native known for its attractive cream or yellow flowers that bloom from winter to spring. It typically grows to a height of about 0.4 to 1.5 meters and is drought and frost tolerant, making it well-suited for ground cover or low hedges in sunny, well-drained spots.
species.maintenance: Grevillea synapheae does not require fertilizer. Like many Australian natives, it is sensitive to high levels of phosphorus and can be killed by general-purpose fertilizers.Water the plant regularly for the first few months until its root system is established. Once established, it is drought-hardy and requires very little water. In fact, it is important to let the soil dry out between waterings to prevent root rot. Some supplemental water in extremely dry summers may be beneficial.

species.description: Grevillea Moonlight is one of the best grevilleas….it is tough and adaptable and also flowers all year round. It is great as a feature plant due to its flower power but also makes an effective informal screen or hedge. Also a great cut flower and bird attracting. The flowers are produced in groups at the ends of the branches, so as each group of flowers finishes it is best to trim off that whole shoot behind the spent flower heads.
species.maintenance: Prune after flowering to maintain compact growth.

species.description: Grevillea Winparra Gold is a stunning fast growing, evergreen hardy shrub that features vibrant, golden-yellow flowers against dark green foliage. This Australian native plant attracts birds and butterflies to the garden with its abundant blooms, adding a splash of color and beauty. With a compact growth habit, Grevillea Winparra Gold is ideal for use as a focal point in borders, rockeries, or containers.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance, native slow release fertiliser twice per year.

species.description: The Lavender Star, or the Crossberry, is a beautiful evergreen that can utilised as a large shrub or a small tree. This beauty is fast growing with gorgeous oval shaped leaves and stunning lavender-purple star flowers that bloom during spring and summer, followed by brown berries. Growing 1.5 to 2 metres tall, try growing the Lavender Star in a tub to spectacular result. The flowers are very attractive to bird and insect life, but especially so to butterflies.

Hemp Bush is a fast growing evergreen flowering shrub in the Hibiscus family (Malvaceae). Produces masses of small white or cream flowers with yellow centres. The plant is dioecious (individual plant has either male flowers or female flowers but not both, so both male and female plants are required to produce seed). The leaves are bright green and elongated triangle shape.
species.maintenance: No Maintenance

species.description: Shrubs and are surrounded by bracts when in bud. or small trees with over 150 Species. Some have flat leaves while others have needle-like in which case they are divided with a grove on the lower surface. The flowers are arranged in groups and are surrounded by bracts when in bud. Flowers are borne on a short stalks
species.maintenance: Good drainage is essential, and fertilizer is rarely required. Drought tolerant once established.

species.description: A medium sized shrub with a graceful weeping habit, and sweetly perfumed multi-hued pink flowers. It provides a perfect habitat for many small native birds, including honeyeaters, wrens and thornbills. Great screen plant that provides excellent nesting and feeding habitat for many small native birds.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance.

species.height_raw: **Height:** 2 – 4 m typicalCan reach **5 m+** in ideal conditions**Width:** 2 – 3 m
species.description: Hakea francisiana, is more commonly known as the emu tree, grass-leaf hakea or bottlebrush hakea.  It is a shrub of the genus Hakea from the Proteaceae family and is native to West and South Australia. The long, slender blue-green foliage of the tree is dotted with bright pinky-red conical shaped flowers and it makes a wonderful feature shrub in the garden.  It’s also great to plant in repetition as a screen or windbreak.  Low maintenance and drought tolerant, it likes a nice well-drained sunny spot. It’s a perfect plant to attract nectar eating birds and butterflies into your outdoor space.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance, Drought resistant. A light trim is recommended after flowering to maintain a dense habit.

species.description: A large shrub to small tree with bluish foliage, and much admired for the stunning flowers.  Best flowering is in a sunny spot, and budding starts in late summer, with flowers opening from late autumn through winter. It can be grown in part shade, but this lessens the number of flowers and makes for a more sparse growth habit. Frost tolerant, but new growth can sustain some frost damage. A shallow rooted plant, so can be affected in windy weather. The Noongar name for this plant is kodjet.
species.maintenance: Light pruning after flowering to maintain a compact shape, watering only while establishing, and avoiding high-phosphorus fertilizers.

species.description: Hakea ulicina, commonly known as furze hakea, is a rigid, erect shrub in the protea family (Proteaceae), native to southeastern Australia. It is known for its narrow, sharp-pointed leaves and clusters of creamy-white flowers. The plant typically grows as a dense, erect shrub between 1 to 3 meters tall, but can occasionally be a small tree up to 5 meters. It has rigid branchlets that can be downy when young. Small, creamy-white flowers are produced in dense clusters of 6 to 18 in the leaf axils. Flowering generally occurs from late winter through to spring (August to September in Australia). It provides a good habitat and food source for birds and serves as a nectar source for butterflies and other insects.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance.

species.description: There are few grasses that perform well in the shade that also have ornamental value. One of the best is Japanese Forest Grass or Hakone Grass, *Hakonechloa macra*, particularly its distinctive variegated or colored-leaf cultivars. This slow-spreading perennial grass forms loose cascading mounds that provide dramatic textural contrasts with other shade-loving plants. Its arching form with the leaves tending to flow in the same direction makes it reminiscent of a cascading waterfall. Even though it is a creeper, it is never invasive, spreading by underground rhizomes. It is a relatively slow grower and may take a while to become established. Clumps can eventually get 2’ high and 3’ wide, although they often stay smaller than this.Slender, arching, linear green leaves grow 12-36” long on wiry stems, giving the effect of a tiny bamboo. Variegation in the cultivars is affected by the conditions the plant is grown under.
species.maintenance: This grass has almost no insect or disease problems. Divide clumps in spring just as new foliage emerges, every 2 to 3 years or as necessary to propagate. After transplanting, they tend to “sit” for several weeks as they root out before putting on much top growth. This grass requires little maintenance, other than cutting the dead leaves back in late winter or early spring.

species.description: Hardenbergia violacea commonly known as Purple Coral Pea, is a stunning and vigorous climbing plant ideal for Australian gardens. It features an abundance of vibrant purple flowers that bloom in late winter to early spring creating a sea of colour and attracting pollinators.
species.maintenance: Fertilize with controlled release low phosphorus in Spring and Summer.

species.description: Hardenbergia Meema (officially Hardenbergia violacea 'HB1' PBR) is a tough, long-lived Australian native shrubby ground cover. Known for its tidy green foliage and It features an abundance of vibrant purple flowers that bloom in late winter to early spring creating a sea of colour and attracting pollinators.
species.maintenance: Fertilize with controlled release low phosphorus in Spring and Summer.

species.description: Shrubs that can range in size from 1m to large tree like plants 2m. Most species feature four rows of leaves arranged perpendicularly that grow in opposite pairs.
species.maintenance: Very sensitive to overwatering/underwatering. Low mzintenance does not require pruning
Toxic: to Dogs. Susceptible to leaf spot and aphids.

species.description: A perennial plant which grows at least 2m high. a number of species exist that vary in size and growth. Flowers in Summer and Autumn with tall spike like cluster flowers in a variety of colours. Flowers are fragrant. Plant can be deciduous in colder areas.
species.maintenance: Once finished flowering remove the old spike of flowers down to the ground. Regular watering should be maintained. Can be prone to snails and slugs.

species.description: This striking perennial produces upright stems adorned with daisy-like flowers in rich golden-orange tones, each featuring a deep red eye that adds depth and vibrancy. Flowering in late summer, it creates a long-lasting display that draws the eye and encourages pollinators such as bees and butterflies.
species.maintenance: Deadhead after flowering

species.description: An annual growing to 100cm when grown in garden beds, or 80cm in containers. Tall plants on sturdy single stems with a medium sized rich orange flowerhead around a dark centre. Attracts birds, bees and butterflies to the garden. Fast growing and drought tolerant. Suited to growing in garden beds and borders, in large containers or for cut flowers. Sunflower plants should flower in approximately 70 days.
species.maintenance: Sunflower plants may need watering during the growing season. Water when the soil is dry about 5cm below the surface (test this by scratching away a little soil with your finger). Water deeply in the early morning or late afternoon. Avoid watering the leaves of plants to avoid fungal diseases.

species.description: Curry plant is a curious and interesting little herb it is an attractive foliage plant featuring fine silver-grey leaves, yellow flowers and an aroma similar to curry when crushed or in warm sunshine. Curry plant is often promoted as an aromatic herb. Its common name derives from its scent, which can smell like curry. (As most of you know, curry is actually a blend of a variety of different spices that can vary from country to country and region to region.) When placed along a walkway, the aroma can be unexpected and enticing. To some folks, curry plant doesn't smell as much like curry as something else -- maple syrup. Regardless of how you interpret the aroma, it has a somewhat sweet, spicy and flowery note that seems at home with both sweet and savory fare.
species.maintenance: Mulch on planting and water regularly until the plant is established, usually around 12 weeks. Trim as required to maintain compact growth.

species.description: Licorice Plant is valued for its soft, velvety, silver-gray leaves that have a woolly texture. It typically forms a dense mat or trail along the ground, reaching a height of about 6 to 12 inches (15 to 30 cm) and spreading up to 3 feet (90 cm). The leaves are small and oval-shaped, providing an excellent backdrop for other plants. While not primarily grown for its flowers, Licorice Plant may produce small clusters of insignificant yellow flowers in summer.
species.maintenance: Pruning: Licorice Plant is a fast-growing trailing plant, and occasional pruning can help maintain its shape and control its spread. Trim back any leggy or overgrown stems to encourage bushier growth.

species.description: Heliotrope's abundant flower clusters add a splash of colour to a container garden or a flower bed. The most common hue is a deep, rich purple, but when you look closely at the blooms, they have several shades of purple with tiny yellow centers.
species.maintenance: A heliotrope plant is easy to grow and will fill your garden with blooms and fragrance as long as its basic needs are met.

species.description: Helleborus orientlis 'Pink Lady' is a bushy, clump-forming, evergreen or semi-evergreen perennial with leathery, deeply lobed, dark green leaves and, in late winter and early spring, upright stems bearing nodding to outward-facing, cup-shaped, pink flowers with prominent yellow anthers.
species.maintenance: Hellebores are relatively low-maintenance plants. Key maintenance tasks include removing old foliage in late autumn or early winter to showcase emerging flowers, feeding with a balanced fertiliser in autumn, and ensuring adequate watering, especially during dry spells and around new plantings. Mulching helps retain soil moisture.

species.description: The delicate mauve flowers that are plentiful in spring and summer and its ground covering habit are the key features of this lovely little plant from the mint family. It is fantastic for pots & hanging baskets and also makes an excellent rockery plant.
species.maintenance: Give it a light trim at the end of Summer.

species.description: Heuchera Sugar Plum has gorgeous frosty plum/ purple leaves which develop a silvery sheen in winter. During summer Sugar Plum comes in their full flowering display with delicate pale pink spires of choral bells on long stems, creating a lovely sense of movement with the breeze. This perennial is ideal for garden beds, rockeries, mass planting and containers.
species.maintenance: Proper care involves ensuring well-draining soil, providing adequate sunlight (depending on the variety), and watering regularly, especially during dry periods. Deadheading spent flowers and removing any dead or damaged leaves helps maintain their appearance and encourages new growth. Dividing plants every few years can also help rejuvenate them.

species.description: Heuchera Peach Flambe features peach coloured foliage that glows through spring and summer, turning plum through winter. Stunning foliage colour Great for underplanting and adding a year round colourful interest to the garden.
species.maintenance: Proper care involves ensuring well-draining soil, providing adequate sunlight (depending on the variety), and watering regularly, especially during dry periods. Deadheading spent flowers and removing any dead or damaged leaves helps maintain their appearance and encourages new growth. Dividing plants every few years can also help rejuvenate them.

species.description: Heuchera Black Forest Cake features deep purple, almost black foliage that is topped with spikes of cherry-red flowers in late Spring to early Summer.
species.maintenance: Fertilise annually with a long term slow release fertiliser.

species.description: Heuchera 'Forever Purple' is a striking plant and is a terrific choice for adding a touch of colour to shady areas of the garden. This fast-growing selection forms a sturdy mound of maple-like leaves in purple with contrasting black veins. The leaf colour changes with the season from red-purple to silvered-purple and sprays of white bell shaped flowers appear during Spring and Summer. This fantastic plant is perfect for mixed containers in outdoor entertaining areas or in groups around the garden. It is a robust grower, and tolerant of heat and humidity.. Vigorous multi-crown habit.
species.maintenance: Fertilise in Spring.

species.description: A hardy and adaptable low to prostrate small shrub, with golden flowers mainly in Spring and Summer, spot flowers possible for the rest of the year. It has fine leaves and a naturally compact habit, light pruning after flowering will encourage a more dense habit. It likes sun to part shade, prefers well drained soil. Performs well in pots and raised beds, looks great as an edging plant. Drought and frost tolerant. Naturally grows in open forest from northern Victoria through to southern Queensland, more prostrate plants will root at the nodes which makes for a hardier plant.
species.maintenance: Light prune after flowering will promote more flowers.

species.description: Hibbertia scandens is a climber with large bright yellow flowers on dark green decorative foliage. Used in rockeries or as a groundcover, great for erosion control. These plant are often seen growing wild among sand dunes, so sandy soil is not a problem. Plant in a sunny position to enjoy maximum flowering.
species.maintenance: Low Maintenance

species.description: Rosella is a hardy plant, adapted to a range of Australian climates. It can survive dry spells, but for best results, plant in fertile, well-drained soil and water regularly.
This plant produces tall spikes of beautiful flowers that are very attractive to bees. It can tolerate partial shade and prefers moist soil.

Hovea acutifolia, commonly known as the Purple Pea Bush or Pointed-Leaf Hovea, is a slender Australian shrub reaching up to 4 meters tall, characterized by its narrow-elliptic leaves with a rust-colored underside and dense gray to rusty hairs on its stems. It produces a profusion of blue to purple pea-shaped flowers from late winter to early spring. The plant prefers well-drained soil, partial shade, and a humid, rainforest-like environment but adapts well to temperate and sub-tropical conditions.
species.maintenance: To maintain a Hovea acutifolia, provide well-draining soil and a position with full sun to partial shade. Water adequately, especially during dry spells, and mulch to retain soil moisture. Prune lightly after flowering to encourage new growth and a bushier shape. Avoid overwatering, as this can make the plant susceptible to root rot, and fertilization is typically not needed.

species.description: Symbols of peace, commitment and beauty Hyacinth Delft Blue *(Hyacinthus orientalis)* is a multi award winning traditional favourite, and for very good reason! Classic lilac blue blooms, and a very reliable growth habit makes this one as close to perfection as you can get. Enjoy these highly perfumed blooms in pots, containers or garden beds. As long lasting cut flower they perfume a whole room. Hyacinths are extraordinarily rewarding every spring warming our souls from the winter months.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance

species.description: Hydrangeas are some of the more beautiful garden shrubs, exhibiting big billowy blooms that come in various shades of pink, blue, purple, white and even green. With the proper growing conditions and care for hydrangeas, they can be grown in a wide range of regions. Hydrangea plants do have a few specific requirements that will keep them healthy and blooming year after year. This mophead Hydrangea hgas the unique ability to bloom consistently on both new and old growth providing beautiful flowers all Summer long. Encourage even more new flower growth by cutting blooms to display in a vase. This variety offers pink blooms in alkaline soils and blue blooms in acidic soils.
species.maintenance: Hydrangeas grow best in rich, loamy soil. If the soil is acidic it can absorb aluminum and produce beautiful blue blossoms. With less acidity, blossoms will generally be pink or whitish. Ideal sun, water and shade are extremely important to hydrangeas. But soil is also a primary consideration for raising them to grow as healthy as possible. Above all, the soil you choose for a hydrangea’s home must be well-draining. Hydrangeas need plenty of water, but will react negatively if their roots sit in water or become soggy.

species.description: Hydrangea paniculata is a hardy deciduous shrub producing large, conical panicles of flowers that open creamy-white or pale green and often age to soft pink or rose by autumn. Unlike mophead hydrangeas, panicle types tolerate more sun, are more cold-hardy, and bloom reliably on new wood, making them dependable summer-into-autumn performers. Forms a graceful, upright shrub of 2–3m, with flowers held above the foliage on strong stems. Excellent as a feature shrub, in mixed borders, or as a deciduous hedge.
species.maintenance: Prune in late winter, cutting last year's flowering stems back to 2–3 strong buds to encourage vigorous new growth and large flower heads. Mulch and water well in dry summers; tolerates more sun than other hydrangeas but appreciates afternoon shade in hot climates.

species.blurb: Domed heads that open dusky pink, turn rust, then stand as rich brown structure all winter.
Dark stems and grey-plum foliage under soft pink plates, handsome long before it flowers.
species.description: Sedum Matrona is a beautiful tall upright herbaceous perennial with dark red stems and grey-green to purple succulent leaves. From spring to autumn stunning broad clusters of mauve-pink flower heads appear on tall red-purple stems giving absolute contrast to the blue green leaves. Looks great when mass planted and used with contrasting colours and textures.
species.maintenance: Prune back after flowering. Very low maintenance.

species.description: Commonly known as the native Frangipani, although not related to the exotic form, this tree bears highly fragrant flower clusters that start out cream and turn to yellow. It is a rainforest tree native to Queensland and New South Wales and its large, glossy leaves give it a tropical look. Growing to 8 metres in ideal conditions, it is capable of providing a nice canopy and the flowers are great for attracting birds and native bees.
species.maintenance: Low Maintenance

species.description: ‘Lushious’ is a dwarf form of the lovely Hymenosporum flavum, and has dense glossy green foliage on a naturally rounded and compact shrub. It is suitable for both sun to quite shady spots, and is very low maintenance. It has perfumed flowers in summer, but a shady growing position will greatly reduce the number of flowers. It grows to around half a metre high and a metre and a half wide, and can be pruned to shape, making it good for low hedging. Good for clay to loam soils as long as it gets reasonable drainage. A handful of slow release fertiliser in spring is beneficial. Also makes a great potted plant. Frost tolerant.

Hypocalymma angustifolium is an erect, multi-stemmed shrub commonly known as White Myrtle or Pink-flowered Myrtle. It typically grows 0.3-1.5 meters tall and is distinguished by its fine, narrow leaves that have a sweet, spicy fragrance when bruised. It produces masses of delicate white or pink flowers along its stems in spring (June to October).
species.maintenance: Hypocalymma angustifolium maintenance involves pruning lightly after flowering to maintain a dense shape, and only watering during very dry periods once established. It thrives in well-drained, preferably acidic soil, in a spot with full sun to dappled shade and protection from strong winds. Fertilize with a low-phosphorus type after pruning, if needed, and protect young plants by mulching the base.

species.description: Hypocalymma robustum, commonly known as the Swan River myrtle, is a flowering shrub native to the southwest region of Western Australia. This evergreen species belongs to the myrtle family, Myrtaceae. A small to medium-sized, erect shrub that grows up to 1.5 meters high with numerous stems. It has thin, dark green, linear-shaped leaves that are aromatic when crushed. Produces a striking display of deep pink to mauve flowers that appear in clusters along the stems. The blossoms, which are sometimes flecked with mauve and tipped with gold, are often described as waxy.
species.maintenance: Pruning after flowering is recommended to encourage a dense, bushy shape.

species.description: An ornamental shrub which is good for wildlife and plenty of nectar for butterflies. Growing to around 2m it can take some frost and drought. It has an upright and spreading growth habit. Leaves are pinnate with up to 21 egg shaped to narrow leaflets which are slightly hairy. Flowers appear in clusters from the leaf axils It will flower through spring, with spires of pink to purple blooms. Growing to around 2 metres tall and wide, it can take neglect and some frost and drought. Given regular watering, a handful of slow release fertiliser each spring, and a light prune, it will grow into a lovely garden specimen. The leaves and stems can be used for natural dyes, and give a soft yellow colour.
species.maintenance: Water regularly and fertilise and prune each Spring. Avoid pruning into old wood.

species.description: Ipomoea nil is commonly called Japanese Morning Glory. It bewitches with its large, showy flowers in a myriad of colors and patterns, celebrated in Japanese culture for centuries as a symbol of beauty and resilience. An annual vine with emerald- green heart shaped leaves, and royal purple-blue trumpet shaped flowers. It opens in the morning and closes in the afternoon.
species.maintenance: Water deeply once a week during dry spells ensuring top inch of soil in-between. dries out. Liquid fertiliser every 3 weeks boosts blooming. Enrich the soil with compost or well-rotted manure.

species.description: Iris albicans is a rhizomatous perennial that typically grows to a height of 1 to 2 feet (30 to 60 centimeters). It features narrow, sword-shaped leaves that are grayish-green in color and can reach a length of around 12 inches (30 centimeters). The leaves are arranged in a fan-like pattern, creating an attractive and architectural look. The flowers of Iris albicans are large and showy, measuring approximately 3 to 4 inches (8 to 10 centimeters) in diameter. Each bloom features three upright, slightly overlapping petals known as "falls" and three erect, petal-like structures called "standards." The petals come in various shades of white, ranging from pure white to creamy white, with delicate veining patterns on the falls.
species.maintenance:
Iris albicans is generally a low-maintenance plant. Here are a few maintenance tips:
• Watering: Provide regular watering during the growing season, ensuring the soil remains evenly moist but not waterlogged.
• Fertilization: Apply a balanced, slow-release fertilizer in early spring to promote healthy growth and abundant blooms.
• Deadheading: Remove faded flowers to encourage prolonged blooming and prevent the plant from diverting energy into seed production.
• Dividing: Every few years, when the clumps become crowded, divide the rhizomes in late summer or early autumn to maintain plant vigor and promote better flowering. WEAR GLOVES WHEN HANDLING.

species.description: There is a lot to like about Isotoma axillaris (often called Laurentia or Solenopsis). It has attractively toothed, deep green leaves, forms bushy plants about 25cm high and wide and once it starts to bloom in Spring it just gets better until late Autumn. The flowers are delicate and starry, about 3cm across, held above the foliage, and lightly fragrant. They are usually pale, (lavender) blue but can be white and or pink.
species.maintenance: Grow Isotoma 'Blue Star' in loam-based compost or moist but well-drained soil. Pinch out the young growth to make it even bushier, and give it a fortnightly liquid feed in summer. Deadhead spent blooms to prolong flowering.

species.description:
This beautiful hellebore was selected by the breeder for its vigorous growth rate, uniform crop production, and compact, upright habit. Unlike hellebores from seed, at least 85% will bloom the first year after vernalization. From late winter through mid-spring, rich burgundy-pink buds open to beautiful ivory blossoms which take on rose and chartreuse tones as they age.  They are outward facing and open flat for best display. This selection has particularly attractive dark green foliage with silver veining which remains compact as it matures. 
Hellebores are the harbingers of spring, blooming for six weeks or more beginning in late winter. They are often flowering during the Christian season of Lent, from which they get their common name, Lenten Rose. This is the perfect plant for naturalizing in moist, woodland areas where its extensive root system will spread as far as it is allowed.
species.maintenance: Avoid soils that are prone to drying out or staying wet. Remove faded or damaged foliage when they appear. Can be a ski wear gloves when handling. irritant

Prune for best shape to show off blooms. Clip off vertical suckers keeping one main trunk with branches leading off from the middle.  Heavy carpet of flowers when they fall. Flowers must be raked up because they decompose into slime.It may take 2 to 14 years for first bloom. Do not overwater.

species.description: An elegant tree with a relatively short trunk and a broad, spreading canopy. It’s not unusual to a see a jacaranda wider than it is tall. Jacaranda will most often grow to less than 8m tall, although it can reach 12–15m under ideal conditions, taking 20+ years to do so. Jacaranda tree foliage is a lush green with a soft, almost fern-like appearance due to the dozens of tiny leaflets that make up each compound leaf. The leaves thin-out over winter before turning a buttery golden colour and falling completely in late winter to early spring. The leaves then reshoot at the same time as, or slightly after, flowering.
species.maintenance: Reliable moisture while young and establishing; quite dry-tolerant once established but may need additional watering in extended dry periods. Annual application of controlled-release fertiliser. As tree grows prune offside shoots. Once around 2m let it form naturally.

species.description: Juncus australis is a species of rush known by the common names austral rush, leafless rush and wīwī. It is a native ornamental grass for margins of waterways and ponds. Ideal grass for revegetation, and soil stabilisation of banks, and provides a natural habitat for native birds and frogs. It features densely tufted rush with dull, green to bluish-green stems. Flowers occur in close or distant almost globular clusters during October to February. It is useful for stabilising wet, sloping soils and acts as a water filter.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance and tolerant of harsh conditions, requires little care once established. Fertilise with a native slow release fertiliser once a year.

species.description: The juniper "Skyrocket" is probably the narrowest Juniper variety available. The foliage is bluish green, scale-like, and aromatic when crushed. Like most Junipers, it develops tiny, rounded, bluish gray cones that resemble berries. These can take up to two years to fully mature. Even the bark is attractive. It is reddish brown and has an interesting shredding appearance. In the landscape, Skyrocket juniper plants make a beautiful informal screen when planted en masse. They are also useful as specimen plants and their non-invasive roots mean they can even be used as foundation plantings.
species.maintenance: Regular watering until established. Rarely need pruning except for dead or damaged wood. USE GLOVES as Sap may cause a rash. Water regularly until established.

species.description: Kalanchoe beharensis, the Felt Bush, is a distinctive succulent shrub from southern Madagascar, prized for its enormous, triangular, deeply scalloped leaves covered in a dense felt of soft silver-bronze hairs that feel like velvet to the touch. Forms an upright, sparsely-branched architectural form, eventually reaching 2–3m with age. Produces clusters of small yellow-green flowers in winter to spring on mature plants. A bold sculptural choice for succulent gardens, dry borders, and large containers — its scale and texture create immediate presence. Frost-tender; protect from heavy frost or grow under cover in cooler regions.
species.maintenance: Very low maintenance. Drought-tolerant; water sparingly. Remove tatty lower leaves to expose the architectural trunk as the plant matures. Frost-tender — protect from heavy frost. Easy to propagate from leaf or stem cuttings.

species.description: Kalanchoe 'Silver Spoons' is a striking succulent shrub with distinctive silver, spoon-shaped leaves edged in a fine red line. Native to Madagascar, it forms an upright, branching plant to around 1m tall and produces small clusters of orange-yellow flowers in winter and early spring. The metallic-silver foliage provides year-round interest and reflects beautifully in evening light. Ideal as a feature plant in succulent gardens, dry borders, rockeries, and container compositions. Frost-tender — protect from heavy frost or grow in containers in cooler regions.
species.maintenance: Very low maintenance. Allow soil to dry between waterings. Tip-prune to maintain shape and encourage branching. Frost-tender — provide shelter or grow in containers in colder areas. Drought-tolerant once established.

species.description: A prostrate or twining shrub with red pea flowers, this plant makes a great ground cover or a restrained climber. Flowers from Winter to Summer. It has a spread to around 1.5 to 3 metres, and has leathery green leaves. Likes a moist but well drained soil in sun or half shade. Can be used for banks, hanging baskets, to spill over retaining walls, as well as on a trellis or fence. Best in temperate and subtropical areas.
species.maintenance: No Maintenance

species.description: Kniphofia also known as Red Hot Poker, is a striking perennial that produces tall spikes of fiery red flowers during winter, adding vibrant color to the garden when little else is in bloom. Its arching, grass-like foliage remains evergreen, providing year-round structure. This hardy plant attracts birds and pollinators, making it a great choice for wildlife-friendly gardens.
species.maintenance: Key maintenance tasks include regular watering during establishment, fertilising in spring, pruning spent flower stems, and dividing clumps every few years.

species.description: Kunzea leptospermoides, commonly known as Yarra burgan, is a flowering plant in Myrtaceae, the myrtle family, and is endemic to Victoria, Australia. It is an erect shrub or small tree with narrow leaves and white flowers crowded near the ends of the branches in spring. The wood was important to the Kulin people for making fighting implements and boomerangs.
species.maintenance: Very low maintenance

species.botanical_name: Lachnagrostis filiformis var. filiformis Common Blown-grass

species.description: Creating quite the visual impact over a lengthy period, this variety offers masses of intense, pink flowers over summer, followed by stunning, rich foliage colour in tones of yellow, red and orange through autumn, before shedding its leaves. When mature, the bark of this variety will peel, creating a mottled effect to reveal the beautiful caramel-pink colour of its underbark.
species.maintenance: Plant in a well drained and well worked soil. Take care to plant the bud union above the soil level. Water in well and keep soil moist until tree is established. Fertilise when planting and again after new growth appears. Prune tree when planting to encourage new growth.

species.description: The Zuni Crepe Myrtle (Lagerstroemia indica x fauriei 'Zuni') is a popular, hardy small tree or large shrub known for its intense violet-purple flowers, vibrant red-orange autumn foliage, and mottled, exfoliating bark. Masses of intense dark lavender or violet-purple flowers. The bark is highly ornamental, peeling to reveal a mottled or striped effect on the trunk as it matures.
species.maintenance: Lifespan around 25-100 years in ideal conditions. Seedpods do not stain so can be near concrete paths. Cut flowers immediately below the head. A light prune required in autumn to remove spent flowers.

species.description: Crepe Myrtle Lipan is a showy small tree with masses of delicate purple flowers in summer, highly ornamental bark and very good autumn colour. Lagerstroemia Lipan is an adaptable and disease resistant tree suitable for a range of situations growing to 4m tall and 3m wide. Lipan Crepe Myrtle is vase-shaped with an upright branching with a rounded canopy.  The dark  green leaves provide a lovely show in Autumn with shades of orange through to red.
species.maintenance: Requires minimal pruning. Perform light shaping in late winter or early spring (when dormant) to remove dead wood, thin out crossing branches, and improve airflow. Avoid "topping" (heavy cutting), which weakens the tree. Requires regular water during the first 12–24 months to establish. Once established, it is very drought-tolerant, needing only deep watering during long dry spells.

species.description: Summer-flowering large shrub or small tree with paper-like white blooms and small oval shaped leaves. Deciduous through winter, with autumn leaf colour before leaf-fall. Vigorous growing variety with smooth grey bark and a gently weeping habit.
species.maintenance: Water regularly during the first 8-12 weeks until the plant is established, then during dry periods until the plant develops a trunk. Drought tolerant. Prune in autumn following leaf drop for prolific summer flowering and a dense growth habit; or deadhead after first flowers to keep an elegant shape and encourage a second flower flush. Fertilise using a slow release fertiliser twice yearly, thrive in clay soils.

species.description: Bunny tail grass (Lagurus ovatus), also known as hare's-tail grass, is a popular ornamental annual grass prized for its soft, fluffy, ivory-white seed heads that resemble the cottony tails of rabbits. Native to the Mediterranean, it is widely used in both fresh and dried floral arrangements due to its unique tactile appeal and whimsical appearance.
species.maintenance: It requires regular watering during the growing season, but is otherwise quite drought-tolerant. It can be propagated by seed, which can be sown in spring or autumn.

species.description: Soft crinkled evergreen foliage and profuse clusters of light scented spidery tassle like flowers. Many varieties have deep purple leaves. Generally, blooms mid spring.
species.maintenance: Best left at natural shape it can be pruned after flowers have finished. Trim out dead and diseased branches.  Keep soil evenly moist but not soggy.

species.description: The Bay Tree is a large shrub or small tree with aromatic, dark green leaves known to many as one of the plants used in bay leaf seasoning. The leaves are 2-4 cm wide and 6-12 cm long with an entire, or un-toothed, slightly undulating margin. In cultivation it may grow from 10-20 meters, but this is not likely in most garden situations. The bay leaf plant is dioecious, with male and female flowers on different plants. The small flowers are a pale, yellow green and borne in pairs beside a leaf. The fruit is small, black, shiny and has a 1 cm diameter.
species.maintenance: Pinch out growing tips during warmer months when new growth forms.

species.description: French lavender is famous for its iconic purple blooms and its ruffled, serrated leaves. Though beautiful, French lavender is not often used for culinary purposes because of its poor flavour.
species.maintenance:
Occasional pruning will help keep this lavender clean and blooming. [Deadhead](https://www.thespruce.com/deadheading-garden-flowers-1402454)
spent flowers to encourage more flowering.

species.description: Silvery-green foliage, upright flower spikes and compact shrub like form. It is a form of mint plant with scented, colourful flowers. Can include annuals and short lived species. Flowers are contained in whorls held on spikes rising above the foliage. Flowers can be blue, violet or lilac. Depending on variety can be used in cooking and baking and buds used in teas. Flower spikes are used for dried flower arrangements and potpourris. The scent of lavender can trigger powerful memories and associations. It can bring memories of visiting grandma's garden or the old linen cupboard, the fresh smell of lavender wafting out from between the sheets and tablecloths. It evokes a clean, warm and comfortable feeling of home.
species.maintenance: Requires very little fertiliser but require good air circulation. In areas of humidity fungus may be a problem due to root rot. Gravelly mulch is best to prevent this. Hand harvest to maintain.

species.description: Lavandula x intermedia, commonly known as Lavandin, is a popular hybrid lavender species resulting from a cross between English lavender (Lavandula angustifolia) and Portuguese lavender (Lavandula latifolia). It is widely cultivated, particularly in the Provence region of France, for its high essential oil content and robust growth. It is an evergreen shrub that forms a dense, bushy, and rounded mound of narrow, grey-green, aromatic foliage. It typically grows larger than L. angustifolia.
species.maintenance: Annual pruning is critical to maintaining a compact, productive shape and extending the plant's 10–15 year lifespan. Post-Flowering (Mid-to-Late Summer): This is the most important prune. Cut back about one-third of the green growth, focusing on removing spent flower spikes and shaping the plant into a symmetrical dome. Early Spring: Perform a light prune to remove any winter damage or dead wood once new leaves sprout. Never cut back into the old wood (the brown, leafless parts at the base). Lavender rarely regrows from old wood, and doing so can kill the plant.

species.description: An upright, clump-forming rhizomatous perennial with loose sprays of lavender-pink flowers with hanging, yellow stamens produced in Summer. It is deciduous with a bushy habit.
species.maintenance: Cut down stems when flowering is complete. Generally, pest free but can be subject to powdery mildew in dry conditions.

species.description: Lechenaultia plants are typically small shrubs or herbs, often with spreading branches, and are known for their bright, five-petaled flowers in shades of blue, white, yellow, or red. They have narrow, fleshy leaves, and their flowers are often hairy inside the petals. These plants, which are endemic to Australia, are popular in horticulture due to their colourful displays.
species.maintenance: Lechenaultia maintenance requires excellent drainage and a sunny, well-ventilated spot to prevent root rot and fungal problems. Fertilize with a low-phosphorus native plant food in spring and autumn. Prune lightly after flowering to maintain a compact shape. Water when the soil is dry to the touch, but avoid overhead watering.

species.description: Leionema is a group of mostly small shrubs from eastern Australia, known for their scented foliage and clusters of star-shaped flowers. A great rewarding mid sized shrub for screening and hedging, especially for those difficult shady spots, as it will still grow dense and will flower in all positions. It has deep green fine leaves which are aromatic and the foliage grows dense to the ground. In spring to mid summer it is covered in masses of white flowers, and will flower well in shady spots as well as sun. It is butterfly attracting.
species.maintenance: If needed, lightly prune to shape after flowering.

species.description: This big bold bright herbaceous shrub is easily recognised by its distinctive flower arrangement, like cherry tomatoes on a kebab skewer. The colour sings out of a mixed garden border; and slender-beaked birds love to feed on its nectar. Have a stroke of the flowers too - soft and velvety!
species.maintenance: Prune as required to maintain a tidy appearance. Fertilise using a slow release fertiliser twice yearly. Deadhead after flowering to encourage a second flush of buds and prevent self seeding.

species.description: Leptorhynchos tenuifolius, commonly known as Wiry Buttons, is a native Australian perennial herb belonging to the daisy family (Asteraceae). It is known for its delicate appearance, with small, bright yellow button-like flowers held above fine, narrow foliage. It is locally common in grasslands, woodlands, and light forests in Victoria and South Australia. It is often found in well-drained soils and can tolerate a range of conditions from full sun to semi-shade, and sometimes seasonally moist areas. It is known to colonize disturbed soil or areas after fire.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance.

species.description: Leptospermum continentale, commonly known as the prickly tea-tree, is a dense, upright, evergreen shrub native to southeastern Australia. It is a hardy, adaptable plant known for its sharp-tipped leaves and profuse white or pale pink flowers that bloom from spring to early summer.
species.maintenance: Relatively easy to maintain once established. It is adaptable to various conditions and generally requires minimal intervention.

species.description: A gorgeous small shrub which will delight in spring when it is covered with a profusion of bright red/pink flowers. The branches are arched and sculptural and the plant grows to 80 centimetres high and a metre and a half wide. Grows in most soil types, but performs best in moist and well drained soil. Beautiful as a feature shrub and lovely planted on banks and walls where it can cascade over the edge. This plant is a pollinators delight, attracting butterflies, bees and all manner of interesting insects.
species.maintenance: Regular watering until established, annual pruning after spring flowering to maintain shape, and feeding with a slow-release, low-phosphorus native fertiliser.

species.description: A tall shrub with striking burgundy coloured new growth and white flowers. It is great for a fast growing screen or hedge. The bold coloured leaves are useful for cut foliage in flower arrangements.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance

species.description: A graceful pendulous shrub with soft, fine, dark purple foliage and purple-pink young stems. The flowers attract butterflies, and wrens, thornbills and other small birds love to forage amongst the blossom.  The dark foliage adds interest all year round, and acts as a great contrast plant in gardens and landscaping.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance

species.description: Native tea tree manuka is highly prized by beekeepers as well as gardeners. Frost hardy evergreen shrub with dainty white flowers and slender foliage typical of leptospermums. An attractive upright fast-growing shrub to around 2.5m tall. The dark foliage is a feature year-round, but the the plant really comes alive in spring with an eye-catching flush of dark pink to red flowers. The flowers are attractive to native bees and predatory wasps. Well suited to informal hedges, screens and fence lines. Adapts well to a variety of soils, grows best in moist to well drained heavier soils. Salt, wind and drought tolerant.
species.maintenance: Mulch and water regularly during the first 4-6 weeks or until the plant is established. Easily grown in acidic, fertile, well-drained soils in full sun or light shade. Young plants appreciate consistently moist soil, but established plants prefer moderate but even moisture. Tolerance for drought and poor soil makes this plant suitable for cultivation in dry Mediterranean climates.

species.description: A bushy evergreen shrub with leathery leaves that are oblong in shape and tulip or cup shaped flowers that are yellow shading to green. It is dioecious, meaning that there are separate male and female plants. Male ones are quite compact and yellow while the female plants are more open and greenish tinged.They make excellent cut flowers.
species.maintenance: Do not disturb the roots, feed with blood and bone annually. Water in dry periods. Remove spent flower heads late winter early spring.

species.description: Leucochrysum albicans is commonly known as the Hoary Sunray and is a member of the daisy family, Asteraceae. It is a small, spreading perennial herb with grey-green foliage, and an inflorescence of a single flower head with a yellow disc centre and papery yellow or white radiating bracts. After flowering, the plant dies back in summer, but its roots survive, allowing it to live up to 15 years.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance

species.description: Leucophyta brownii is a small, compact evergreen shrub that typically grows to a height of about 2 to 3 feet (60 to 90 cm) and spreads about the same width. It features dense, fine, silver-gray foliage that gives it a distinctive appearance. The leaves are narrow, linear, and covered in fine hairs, contributing to the plant's silver colouration. The shrub has a rounded and mounded growth habit, creating a neat and tidy appearance.
species.maintenance: Silverbush generally requires minimal pruning. However, you can lightly trim the plant in early spring to maintain its shape and remove any dead or damaged branches. Once established, Leucophyta brownii is highly drought-tolerant and prefers well-drained soil. Water it sparingly, only when the soil is dry, as excessive moisture can lead to root rot. Silverbush typically does not require heavy fertilisation. However, you can apply a slow-release, low-nitrogen fertiliser in spring to promote healthy growth if needed.

species.description: Leucopogon parviflorus is a medium, bushy shrub or small tree up to 5 metres high. The lance-shaped leaves up to 25 mm long and 6-7 mm wide. Flowering occurs in winter and spring and the small, white flowers are about 4 mm long, occurring in clusters of up to 13 flowers.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance, pruned by the wind.

species.description: Leucospermum is a spectacular evergreen shrub that produces a long display of brilliant shaded, pin cushion like flowers. The beautiful, pincushion-like blooms are brilliantly coloured in red, orange or yellow from spring to early summer, while the foliage takes the form of an evergreen, compact and attractive woody shrub with thick, leathery leaves. It is a good long lasting cut flower.
species.maintenance: Although Leucospermum is not an Australian native, it benefits from the same type of soil that native plants do. Soil should be rich in nutrients, well-draining and slightly acidic but low in phosphorous - digging in some well-rotted manure or organic matter will help to condition your soil.

species.description:
Aptly named, the Tractor Seat Plant has lush dark green, kidney shaped leaves that are perfect for adding some charm to your Cottage or Tropical garden, being a brilliant feature along paths or you can even bring it inside as a terrific showpiece. If you are looking for a great foliage plant for a shaded position, then Ligularia reniformis commonly called the ‘tractor seat plant’ is one to consider.
Also known as Farfugium japonicum Giganteum and widely seen as Ligularia ‘Designer Verde’, you could well describe this perennial as a feature plant or a designer plant, however it is really the texture of the large glossy leaves that best describe its attraction.
Native to China and Japan, the Tractor Seat Plant is clump forming perennial, overtime it will spread to form a good clump. It is evergreen in temperate climates, however in colder climates it will die back over winter.
This is a plant that can reach 70cm to 1 metre in height, it can be grown in a container in shaded courtyard if desired.
species.maintenance: Water regularly and keep moist.  Apply mulch around bases to retain moisture. Deadhead after flowering and cut dead or damaged leaves at the base. Prone to slug and snail attacks.

species.description: You know by the name that this makes a great coastal plant! It's a tough resilient low-maintenance perennial that shoots up domed flowerheads in shades of purple and white in warmer months; and gives you autumn leaf colour in cooler ones. Drought tolerant and comes through light frosts. The flowers are small but numerous and appear in summer in a long, showy cone arrangement at the end of the growing tips. The flower colour depends on the variety, but can be white, pink or purple—or any shade in between!
species.maintenance: Mulch and water regularly for the first 12 weeks until the plant establishes. Deadhead old flower stems to encourage new buds. Divide the plant every three years or so to retain its vigour.

species.description: Linum marginale, commonly known as native or wild flax, is a slender, perennial herb native to Australia. A member of the flax family (Linaceae), it is found across temperate regions of the continent, except the Northern Territory. It typically grows 10 to 60 cm tall but can reach up to 1 meter in some conditions. The plant has an upright, often unbranched, hairless stem and a thick, tuberous rootstock. The pale or sky-blue, star-shaped flowers have five petals and may have darker venation. They appear in loose clusters at the top of the stem and bloom from spring through summer.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance.

species.description: An evergreen perennial which forms clumps of grass like dark green leaves. It grows to a height of 40cm and produces showy dark purple bell shaped flowers from early spring until late autumn.
species.maintenance: Cut old foliage down to the ground in winter to promote new leaves in spring.

species.description: A hardy evergreen perennial that features dark green strappy foliage and white spikey flowers in Spring-Summer.
species.maintenance: Low to no maintenance.

species.description: Liriope Emerald Cascade is a stand out tough-as-nails garden performer, tolerating a broad range of adverse conditions. Not only will Emerald Cascade tolerate extended periods of dryness, but it also does well with minimal care inside the home or office. With dramatic emerald green foliage producing cobalt blue-berries in the spring and summer. A non-invasive form of Liriope, Emerald Cascade spreads slowly to form graceful thick mounds offoliage, and makes for a low-maintenance dense groundcover when planted en masse.
An evergreen perennial which forms clumps of grass like dark green leaves. It grows to a height of 40cm and produces showy dark purple bell shaped flowers from early spring until late autumn.
species.maintenance: Cut old foliage down to the ground in winter to promote new leaves in spring.

species.description: Livistona chinensis, the Chinese Fan Palm, is an elegant, slow-growing palm from southern Japan, Taiwan, and southern China. Forms a single trunk topped with a rounded crown of large, glossy fan-shaped leaves that droop gracefully at the tips, giving the palm a soft, fountain-like silhouette. Slow to develop a trunk in cooler climates but eventually reaches 6–9m. Produces inconspicuous cream flowers followed by clusters of small blue-black fruits. Highly adaptable — tolerates a wide range of conditions from sun to part shade, and is one of the more cold-tolerant fan palms, making it well-suited to temperate Melbourne gardens, courtyards, and as a feature in tropical-style plantings.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance once established. Remove old dead fronds as they brown off — wear gloves, the leaf bases have sharp teeth. Water regularly while young; mature palms are moderately drought-tolerant. Tolerates light frost; protect young plants from heavy frost.

species.description: Lomandra Frosty Tops is a hardy, fast-growing, grass. It has tough glossy, strappy green leaves and clusters of small perfumed, cream-to-yellow flowers appearing in Spring. The foliage is a distinct blue-green with silver-gray highlights, creating a frosty and shimmering effect. It is perfect for specimen or mass planting, a great choice for amongst rockeries, along medium strips or roadside spaces.
species.maintenance: Trim spent flower stems. Feed with phosphorous native fertiliser early Spring or late Summer.

species.description: Lomandra confertifolia 'Seascape' is a hardy, low-maintenance evergreen native with weeping, blue-grey foliage that forms dense 50-70cm clumps. Ideal for coastal gardens, it thrives in full sun to part shade and handles drought, frost, and diverse soils. It blooms with scented yellow flowers in summer, making it perfect for borders, mass plantings, and container gardening.
species.maintenance: Trim spent flower stems. Feed with phosphorous native fertiliser early Spring or late Summer.

species.description: A clumping grass-like perennial with bright green narrow foliage which is slightly weeping. Great as a border or pot plant. Good for coastal plantings, drought and frost tolerant. If the foliage gets damaged, it is easy to cut any unsightly top growth away to let the plant resprout with healthy new growth. Flowers are insignificant and hidden amongst the foliage.
species.maintenance: Water well until established. Slow release fertiliser in spring. Prune every 3 years.

species.description: Lomandra filiformis, the Wattle Mat-rush, is a slender, tufted Australian native perennial. It forms compact clumps of fine, wiry, dark green leaves to around 30–50cm, with small yellow flower spikes appearing in spring. Tough and very versatile, it tolerates a wide range of conditions and is well suited to mass planting, border edges, rockeries, and naturalistic restoration plantings.
species.maintenance: Very low maintenance. Drought tolerant once established. Cut back hard every few years if needed to refresh foliage. No fertilising required.

species.description: Lomandra 'Lime Tuff' is a compact, hardy Australian cultivar with bright lime-green, fine-textured foliage. Forms a tidy clumping mound to around 40–60cm and produces small yellow-cream flower spikes in spring. Highly versatile and reliable, it tolerates a wide range of conditions including coastal exposure, drought, and frost, making it an excellent choice for mass planting, container work, low formal borders, and contemporary native garden design.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance. Drought resistant and prefers a well-drained soil.

species.description: Native to Australia. This is an extremely versatile and hardy plants that will grow almost anywhere. On warm summer days the flower spikes produce a pleasant perfume.
