The leaves are strap-like forming tussocks. It will grow nicely in containers and as is also useful as an ornamental grass in native gardens or for use in borders along driveways, the blooms also look great in floral arrangements. It grows very well in almost all areas.
species.maintenance: Water well until established. Slow release fertiliser in spring. Prune every 3 years.

species.description: Lomandra 'Tanika' is one of the most popular Australian native cultivars, prized for its fine, weeping, lime-green foliage that forms a tidy, dome-shaped clump to around 60–75cm. Produces small yellow flower spikes in spring with a subtle honey scent. Tough, evergreen, and adaptable — it thrives in full sun to dappled shade, tolerates drought, frost, and coastal exposure, and stays compact without becoming bulky. Excellent for mass planting, contemporary borders, and structured native landscapes.
species.maintenance: Very low maintenance. Trim back hard every 2–3 years to rejuvenate. Otherwise just remove any tatty leaves as needed. Drought-tolerant once established; water moderately during establishment. Frost-hardy.

species.description: A colourful attractive large evergreen shrub with reddish-purple foliage bearing clusters of pretty hot pink tassel-like flowers in Spring. Loropetalum is a genus of four species of shrubs or small trees in the witch-hazel family, Hamamelidaceae, native to China, Japan, and south-eastern Asia. There are two main forms of Loropetalum, sometimes referred to as the Chinese Fringe Flower. It boasts the deepest, darkest plum-coloured foliage found amongst Loropetalums and retains this brilliant colour all year round.
species.maintenance: Water well until established. Do not allow to dry out.  Mulch annually to retain moisture. Slow-release fertiliser in Spring. Shape after flowering.

species.description: Loropetalum Little China Ruby is a true show stopper in any garden. This tidy and compact, evergreen perennial is in high demand with dense plum like foliage year round and bright magenta flowers that cover the shrub in both spring and autumn. Works great when planted en masse but also makes a bright feature plant or contrasting border plant.
species.maintenance: A good organic fertiliser should be applied after flowering to promote another flush of blooms.

species.description: Lotus Red Flash commonly known as Parrots beak is a unique sun-loving ground cover plant that flowers from late Spring to late Autumn. This dense ground cover is great for cascading over rockeries or retaining walls and its silvery/blue foliage is perfect for softening hardscapes. Originating from the Canary Islands, it has fine ferny grey-green foliage and abundant rich red flowers like little claws or beaks. Super little plant for hanging baskets and window boxes.
species.maintenance: Mulch and water well during extended dry periods. Pinch stem ends to promote branching. No pruning required.

species.description: Lunaria annua, commonly known as Honesty, Silver Dollar, or the Money Plant, is a popular biennial flowering plant in the Brassicaceae (mustard) family. It is widely cherished in cottage gardens for its vibrant spring blooms and its unique, translucent, coin-like seed pods. It is a biennial, meaning it typically grows foliage in its first year and flowers, sets seed, and dies in its second year. However, it self-seeds so prolifically that it often appears perennial in a garden setting.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance.

species.description: An evergreen large shrub or small tree growing 7-12m tall and a 3-5m width. Attractive deep green foliage with copper coloured new growth.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance. Not troubled by pests.

species.description: Lycopus australis is a leafy erect perennial semi-aquatic herb. The species is most easily identified when in flower from January to March, though it can be identified from its distinctive foliage until June before the stems die back for winter. The stems are 4-angular and grooved. Leaves are lance-shaped and arranged opposite each other along the stem, with successive pairs at right angles to each other. For use in wet areas.
species.maintenance: Dies off in Winter, remove dead foliage if desired.

species.description: Lysimachia nummularia 'Aurea' (Golden Creeping Jenny) is a vigorous, low-growing, evergreen perennial (3-6 in. tall) valued for its vibrant chartreuse to golden trailing stems, making it ideal for ground cover, hanging baskets, or pond edges. It produces bright yellow flowers in summer, loves moisture, and thrives in full sun to partial shade. Golden Creeping Jenny is hardy and brings a high-contrast, "wow" factor to garden designs, particularly when paired with dark-foliaged plants.
species.maintenance: No Maintenance

species.description: Lysiosepalum involucratum is a compact shrub up to 0.5 metres high by about 1 metre wide. The leaves are linear to slightly ovate in shape about 10 – 25 mm long, grey-green in colour and hairy. The flowers appear in spring and are pink to mauve. The petals are very small and the sepals provide the colourful parts of the flowers which are subtended by rusty, hairy bracteoles.
species.maintenance: Light pruning after flowering

species.description: Lythrum salicaria, commonly known as purple loosestrife, is a tall, hardy perennial herb known for its dense spikes of vibrant pink or purple flowers that bloom from summer into autumn. It is native to Europe, Asia, northern Africa, and parts of Australia, and is a popular plant for water gardens and boggy areas. The flowers are a valuable nectar source, attracting bees, butterflies, and other pollinators.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance.

species.description: An evergreen flowering tree with deep glossy green leaves, underside are a rusty brown with a slight furry feel. From spring to summer it bears large white perfumed flowers. At maturity the dwarf varieties grow to around 4m but can be contained through pruning.
species.maintenance: Annual feed of controlled release fertiliser. Mulch annually in Spring to retain moisture during summer. Ensure adequate moisture during warmer months. Few pest that can be contained with oil based products.

species.description: Commonly called the Yulan Magnolia, this is a revered small deciduous tree from eastern and southern China. M.denudata produces pure white fragrant goblet-shaped flowers just before the leaves emerge in late winter and early spring. The tree will grow to approximately 6-8m in Melbourne suburban gardens and is easily shaped with pruning. It prefers sun to part shade and some protection from strong northerly and westerly winds. The Yulan has no serious pest or disease problems
species.maintenance: Requires pruning for shape

species.description: A reliable upright growing variety of grandiflora with glossy green leaves and a conical growth habit. It is a hardy and versatile plant that will tolerate a range of conditions and is relatively pest and disease free. During the warmer months it produces beautiful, creamy-white, fragrant flowers and will flower from an early age.
species.maintenance: Use a slow release fertiliser during Spring.

species.description: Magnolia Kay Paris makes a most luxurious hedge. Large, glossy, deep green leaves with a brown backing gives these trees a unique point of interest in the landscape. Add to that their massive creamy white blooms that come on during the summer months and they are a real winner. Their upright habit makes them ideal for screening. They key to keeping this Magnolia happy is lots of nutrients and consistent water.
species.maintenance: Low Maintenance

species.description: Magnolia 'Elizabeth' is a deciduous, upright-pyramidal hybrid magnolia (M. acuminata x M. denudata) carrying primrose to soft butter-yellow, lightly fragrant goblet flowers on bare wood in early to mid spring, just ahead of the leaves. Large mid-green leaves follow and hold a clean canopy through summer. Reaches around 6-9m over time with a naturally shapely single-leader form, making it a strong deciduous feature tree for a front garden - bare architectural branching in winter, flower in spring, shade in summer.
species.maintenance: Plant in a sheltered position; the flowers bruise in wind and late frost. Wants a deep, humus-rich, slightly acidic and well-drained soil - mulch annually and keep moisture up over the first few summers. Prune only to remove dead or crossing wood, immediately after flowering; magnolias resent hard pruning. Surface roots are shallow, so avoid cultivating beneath the canopy.

species.description:
Spring flowering magnolia trees have their own special allure. Their gorgeous flowering display is like a joyful shout-out from nature, signalling that winter is behind us. There is one kind of tree that puts on the biggest, boldest and most breathtakingly beautiful display – the deciduous magnolia. Its flowers are made up of petals that are 12cm or more in length, making them nothing short of spectacular. The flowers are often described as tulip-like, as they start with an upright, slender form before opening to a near saucer-like shape. The colours are just divine. A regular Magnolia x soulangeana is mainly white with various levels of purple towards the petal base. There are also deciduous magnolias with pure white blooms and all manner of shades, including delicate, slightly fragrant yellows to very deep, luxuriant purples. The impact of this flowering display is amplified by the fact that it all happens on bare wood before the new season's foliage has started to open. The deciduous magnolia will generally have one central trunk with a number of solid lateral branches creating a spreading form. This can give the impression that the tree is multi-trunked. Its form is naturally quite neat and tidy, and the tree is often almost as wide as it is tall. The classic Magnolia x soulangeana can become large with age, up to 8m tall × 5m wide, but most magnolias are smaller than this, with 5 × 3 being more typical at 10 to 15 years. Many of the newer varieties have growth habits that are around half that of a typical deciduous magnolia.
Flower and leaf buds develop on the tree over winter and are protected by furry protective coverings. The flowers can take week to fully open. Flowering time and duration will depend on the variety and location. The new leaves will follow shortly after flowering, or may start appearing while flowers are still present.
The canopy of the tree is quite dense when it is healthy and happy. The leaves start very soft and bright green and then age to a slightly leathery or thick papery feel. This tough appearance is deceptive, as leaves will be easily damaged by hot or drying winds. In autumn the leaves will wither and brown before falling. As the older bark of the tree is a smooth silvery grey, the tree makes a beautiful specimen even when bare in winter.
species.maintenance: Can be attacked by bugs, snails and fungus. Prune mid-summer when in full leaf. Mulch and regular irrigation during warmer months. Feed annually with a quality controlled-release fertiliser that is balanced for acid-loving plants. Protect from strong winds, Reliable watering during dry periods and periods of flowering.

species.description: An evergreen climber with petite rounded dark green leaves on black stems.
species.maintenance: Trim to contain vigorous growth.

species.description: The Malus 'Evereste' is one of the best flowering crab apple trees. It is a small specimen with a compact, broadly rounded crown. In April the tree is covered in dark pink buds that open into a mass of white blossom; a beautiful eye-catching display, and popular with bees and other pollinators. The leaves are dark green and will remain on the tree until late autumn when they turn a yellow-orange-bronze colour. Masses of small, red and orange crab apples appear in autumn and can remain on the tree throughout winter. They are a great favourite with all wildlife and can be used to make crab apple jelly and jam. The Malus 'Evereste' will thrive in most well-drained soil, including clay and chalk, and does best in full sun. This variety is the most disease resistant and will tolerate pollution, making it a very versatile tree for many landscaping schemes.
species.maintenance: Low with average water needs.

species.description: Malus floribunda is a popular ornamental tree that provides seasonal interest throughout the year. Flowers: In mid-spring, the tree is covered in mildly fragrant, single flowers. The buds start as a striking crimson or reddish-pink and open into masses of pale pink or white blossoms, creating a multi-colored effect that is a key feature of the tree.
species.maintenance: It requires moderate, regular watering, especially during dry periods and while establishing. Once established, it is considered reasonably drought-tolerant. Minimal pruning is needed to maintain its shape, best done in late winter to encourage healthy growth.

species.description: ‘Wychwood Ruby’ is an easy to grow, hardy and rewarding small tree suitable for many applications. ‘Wychwood Ruby’ is famed for its tight upright growth habit, and stunning ruby-pink blooms which adorn the entire tree during early spring each year. Rich new ruby coloured foliage in early spring, changing foliage tones in autumn. Small claret coloured fruit in summer.
species.maintenance: Easy to grow. Take care to plant the bud union above the soil level, water in well. Dry tolerant once established.

species.description: Low growing annual
species.maintenance: Dead head flowers to encourage new flowers

species.description: German Chamomile adds charm and pretty flowers to the garden. They are suitable as edging plants for garden beds and also grow happily in the vegetable garden, attracting pollinators such as bees and butterflies. German Chamomile is an annual herb to about 60cm, originating from Temperate Europe and Asia. Plants are multi-branched with feathery foliage and daisy like flowers with yellow centers and white ray florets. Chamomile is a beneficial companion plant that can enhance the health and growth of various garden plants, particularly brassicas, onions, garlic, fruit trees, tomatoes, herbs, beans, and strawberries.  A herb infusion of chamomile can be used on young seedlings to help deter damping off.
species.maintenance: Flowers can be picked when first opened throughout the year. Prune to shape and spent flowers will self seed.

species.description: Melaleuca elliptica, commonly known as the Granite Honey Myrtle or Granite Bottlebrush, is a hardy, medium-to-large evergreen shrub native to Western Australia. It is known for its showy, red bottlebrush-shaped flowers and attractive gray-green foliage.
species.maintenance: To maintain a Melaleuca elliptica, provide full sun and well-drained soil, water moderately during dry spells, and prune after flowering to shape the shrub and encourage denser growth. This hardy plant is low-maintenance, tolerates drought and salt spray once established, and generally resists pests and diseases.

species.description: Melaleuca styphelioides, known as the prickly-leaved paperbark or prickly paperbark, is a plant native to eastern Australia. It is a tree with spongy bark, prickly leaves and spikes of creamy-white flowers. It is a small to medium-sized tree up to 10 m high with a dense, rounded canopy and drooping branchlets. The spongy bark is white or light brown and peels off in large strips. The leaves are sessile, 7–15 mm long and 2.5–6 mm wide. They are slightly twisted, have sharply-pointed tips, are arranged alternately on the branchlets and have between 15 and 30 veins.
species.maintenance: Prefers moisture. Under prune to raise crown.

species.description: Lemon balm is a clump-forming perennial with heart-shaped, deeply veined leaves covered with stiff hairs. It looks very similar to mint in appearance but is not as invasive and easier to control. The flowers appear in early summer are small and white, with a delicate appearance. They grow in clusters on upright stems above the plant's foliage. The flowers are attractive to bees and other pollinators. Its promotes consecration, creativity, inner balance, purification, protection.
species.maintenance: Keep the soil consistently moist but not waterlogged, especially during dry periods. Adequate moisture is essential for healthy growth. Trim the plant regularly to encourage bushier growth and to prevent it from becoming too leggy. Pinching off the flower buds before they fully bloom can also help maintain the plant's vigor. Lemon Balm usually doesn't require heavy fertilization. A balanced, all-purpose fertilizer can be applied in the spring to support growth.

species.description:
Native River Mint (aka. Wild Mint) is a smaller, more delicate relative of more well-known mints like peppermint and spearmint. It has long been used in Aboriginal culture as a flavoursome bushfood, insect repellant and medicinal herb. In the wild, you’ll find it growing in most regions of the country, often around rivers, bogs and other damp, shaded places. The River Mint is the perfect Aussie replacement or substitute for other types of mint, or a fantastic addition to a native herb garden. Use it liberally, fresh or dried, when making sauces, salads, dressing, dips, roasts, desserts, teas, cocktails and water infusions.
To harvest, pluck the leaves off the growing plant or prune whole stalks at a time. Leaves may be used fresh, or chopped and dried for later use. Just remember the aroma and flavour in harvested leaves will fade over time. Native River Mint loves moisture and shade, and does best in boggy soil. However, it can be grown in dry areas, in sun or shade, with extra watering and plenty of organic matter in the soil. Like other mints, it grows relatively fast and will need regular pruning to keep tidy. This species of mint grows about 30cm high and 100cm wide, but can expand much further if allowed to run wild. Though this species of mint is less rampant, it’s still easiest to control when grown in a pot.
species.maintenance: Hard cut back at start of Spring

species.description: Mint breeder James Westerfield introduced yet another winner with this compact, perennial herb. ‘Berries and Cream’ has a warm, soothing aroma and flavor that hints of berries and mint
species.maintenance: Trim as required.

species.description: Peppermint is a perennial spreading herb with dark green leaves and reddish stems. The true Peppermint is a sterile hybrid derived from a cross between Mentha aquatica and M. spicata. Seeds sold and labeled peppermint generally will not germinate into true peppermint, but often produce a less intensely scented spearmint-like plant. The leaves have a sharp, spicy taste hot at first but at the same time cooling, they can be used to flavour desserts, drinks, teas, sauces, salads, liqueurs and some vegetables.
species.maintenance: Avoid fertilizing. The flavour relies on oils in the flowers. Cannot tolerate soaking soil.

species.description: Fast growing medium size tree with lime green foliage. Highly fragrant orchid like white flowers appear from mid-Spring through to Autumn. Height 6-10m Width 4m. Some varieties take a while to bloom.
species.maintenance: Mulch well to keep roots cool. Water regularly during Summer.

species.description: evergreen tree that grows to 3-4 metres tall
species.maintenance: trim to shape after flowering
Requires heavy mulching to deter weeds.

species.description: Microlaena is a low growing grass that can be planted as a native lawn. Microlaena, commonly known as Weeping Grass, is a small, slender native grass with lime green leaves. Microlaena can be used to create a native lawn. To get the best results plant them about 10cm apart.
species.maintenance: Mow around 2-4 times a year. Very low maintenance once established.

species.description: Mints (Mentha) are a genus of highly aromatic perennial herbs known for their refreshing scent and vigorous growth. They are versatile plants used globally for culinary, medicinal, and aromatic purposes.
species.maintenance: Mint is a low-maintenance perennial, but because of its vigorous growth habit, it requires strategic pruning and water management to stay healthy and contained.

species.description: An evergreen shrub that gives good foliage colour in winter. The leaves are glossy and oval shaped, and very dense.
species.maintenance: Prune once a year just before new growth begins in Spring. Water through the first summer.  Not frost tolerant.

species.description: Miscanthus 'Flamingo' is a deciduous perennial grass that forms clumps of arching foliage. It typically reaches a height of 4 to 5 feet (120 to 150 cm) with a spread of 3 to 4 feet (90 to 120 cm). The narrow leaves are green with a prominent white midrib, adding a striking variegated effect to the plant. In late summer to early autumn, 'Flamingo' produces feathery plumes of pink flowers that rise above the foliage, creating an elegant and soft texture in the garden.
species.maintenance:
1. Pruning: In late winter or early spring, before new growth emerges, cut back the old foliage to ground level. This allows the plant to rejuvenate and promotes the development of fresh, vibrant foliage.
2. Division: Every few years, consider dividing the clumps of 'Flamingo' to control its size and rejuvenate the plant. This is typically done in early spring when new growth begins.
3. Watering: Once established, Miscanthus 'Flamingo' is relatively drought-tolerant. However, regular watering during prolonged dry periods helps maintain its health and vigor.

species.description: Miscanthus sinensis, known as Chinese Silver Grass or Maiden Grass, is a clump-forming ornamental grass from East Asia, widely planted for its strong vertical structure and dramatic late-season flowering. Forms an upright fountain of fine, arching green foliage to 1.5–2m, topped in late summer to autumn with feathery silver, cream, pink, or bronze plumes that catch the light and shimmer in the breeze. Foliage turns warm gold and copper through autumn before fading to straw colour in winter. A foundation grass in modern naturalistic and meadow-style plantings — works beautifully as a tall specimen, a soft screen, or in drifts among perennials. Note that some forms can self-seed in certain climates; choose sterile cultivars where this is a concern.
species.maintenance: Cut back to 10–15cm above the ground in late winter, before new growth emerges, to refresh the clump. Divide every 4–6 years to maintain vigour. Drought-tolerant once established but appreciates consistent moisture for best growth. Frost-hardy.

species.description: Bitter melon is a climbing plant that produces green, spiky fruit. It is a staple in many Asian cuisines and can be used in stir-fries, soups, and curries. Bitter melon is also believed to have health benefits, including lowering blood sugar levels.
species.maintenance: Give plants a boost one a month by feeding with comfrey tea or liquid fertiliser, add more compost around each plant.

species.description: A low to medium growing grass with green or blackish strappy leaves. around 10-15cm tall.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance. Annual top dressing with organic compost and slow-release fertiliser. Once established it is drought tolerant. Can be propagated by division. in early spring.

species.height_raw: 2–3m h x 2–3m w (climbing higher with support)
species.description: Monstera deliciosa is an evergreen climbing aroid from the rainforests of southern Mexico and Central America. Young leaves are entire; as the plant matures they develop the characteristic deep splits and oval perforations, reaching 60–90cm across. Climbs by thick aerial roots and will scale a trunk, post or wall given support. In Melbourne it needs a warm, sheltered, frost-free position — a shaded courtyard, a protected wall, or grown in a container. All parts contain calcium oxalate crystals and are toxic if ingested.
species.maintenance: Low to moderate. Provide a moss pole, trunk or trellis for the aerial roots to grip. Water when the top of the soil dries; avoid waterlogging. Wipe leaves to keep them glossy. Frost-tender — protect or move under cover in cold snaps. Remove yellowing leaves at the base.

species.description: low growing ground cover

Murnong produces gangly, milky, white tuberous roots that may be eaten raw or baked. They can be prepared warm with butter, included in salads, mixed with other vegetables, or turned into a paste for desserts. They taste sweet and slightly coconutty. The slightly bitter leaves are also edible and may be enjoyed in salads with a vinegar dressing.
The tubers start forming in midsummer beneath clumps of yellow dandelion-like daisy flowers. When the flowers blossom in Autumn, the tuber roots are ready for harvest. Simply dig them up and enjoy.
species.maintenance: Harvest after one year.

species.description: A beautiful shrub bearing masses of cream white perfumed flowers in Spring and Summer. Dark evergreen leaves and a tight compact habit.
species.maintenance: Water deeply 6-8 weeks until established. Lightly prune in the warmer months to retain shape and size.

species.description: Muscari ‘Valerie Finnis’ is a distinctive cultivar of Grape Hyacinth known for its densely packed, conical spikes of pale, powdery blue flowers. Named after the famous British plantswoman Valerie Finnis, this perennial bulb is celebrated for its soft, "Cambridge blue" hue and sweet fragrance. Features dainty, bell-shaped florets that often have a silvery or icy sheen. Unlike the more common deep-blue Muscari, this variety offers a pastel, airy aesthetic.
species.maintenance: Allow the foliage to die back naturally after flowering to store energy for the next season.

species.description: Mazus pumilio, commonly known as Blue Swamp Mazus, is a hardy evergreen ground cover native to wetland areas. This low-growing, mat-forming plant thrives in waterlogged soils, making it perfect for damp garden spots or as a ground cover around ponds. The plant features dense rosettes of green foliage that spread by rhizomes, creating a lush carpet. In spring and summer, delicate purple-blue flowers blanket the plant, offering a soft burst of color. Mazus pumilio is ideal for creating a vibrant, low-maintenance ground cover in both sun and shaded areas.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance

species.description: An attractive large shrub, with unusual weeping leaves on long arched branches. While it is attractive when not in flower, it becomes even more eye catching in mid spring to early summer when the branches are covered with profuse small white flowers, making it look like the branches are covered in snow. It can be grown in sun to part shade, it can get a bit leggy in full sun, more profuse with some shelter from taller plants  (it naturally grows in sheltered gullies). It is a magnet for all sorts of native insects when in flower, making it a great habitat plant.
species.maintenance: Weeping Myoporum is a fast-growing, low-maintenance evergreen shrub that thrives in full sun to part shade and requires well-drained soil. It is drought-tolerant once established but benefits from occasional deep watering in summer. Pruning is rarely needed except for shaping or maintaining its weeping form.

species.description: Myoporum parvifolium 'Fine Leaf', commonly known as Creeping Boobialla, is a vigorous, low-spreading Australian native groundcover with fine, narrow bright-green foliage that hugs the ground in dense mats. Produces small white star-shaped flowers from spring through summer, attracting bees and other pollinators. Excellent for stabilising slopes, covering large areas quickly, and softening hard edges; tough, drought-hardy, and well-suited to coastal, native, and contemporary landscapes.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance. Water moderately during establishment then largely drought-tolerant. Trim lightly to control spread or rejuvenate dense growth. Frost-hardy in most situations. Tolerates pruning back hard if needed.

species.description: Myoporum parvifolium 'Purpurea' (Purple Creeping Boobialla) is a fast-growing, hardy Australian native groundcover featuring dense, purple-toned foliage and small, white, star-shaped flowers in spring/summer. It reaches 10–30 cm in height and spreads up to 3 m, making it ideal for weed suppression, bank stabilization, and coastal gardens.
species.maintenance: Water regularly during the first 6–8 weeks to establish roots. Once established, it is drought-tolerant, needing only occasional deep watering during extended dry periods. Lightly prune once a year in late winter or early spring to maintain its shape, control spread, and promote fresher, denser growth.

species.description: This dark green sticky leaves forming a dense shrub. Flowering from June to December in white flowers with mauve to purple spots.
species.maintenance: No maintenance

species.description: compact, evergreen, with tight habit
species.maintenance: regular hedging to maintain shape

species.description: Slightly branched, canelike stems and delicate, handsome, glossy, compound leaves that are pink-bronze when unfurling, green in summer, and red-tinged in winter. Leaves are intricately divided into many 2.5-5cm, pointed, oval leaflets, creating a lacy pattern. Small white flowers form in loose, erect, 15-31cm clusters and if grouped, are followed by bright red fruits that last well into winter; however, single plants seldom fruit heavily. Some nandinas have beautiful foliage colour during autumn and others retain their bright colours year round.
species.maintenance: Best to thin out old canes otherwise very tough and drought tolerant.

species.description: Daffodils are a hardy perennials that come back year after year, spreading and often naturalising. There are thousands of daffodil varieties.  The traditional daffodil flower may be a showy yellow or white, with six petals and a trumpet-shape central corona, but many cultivated varieties (“cultivars”) exist today.
species.maintenance: Lift and divide the clumps when flowering becomes sparse or the clumps congested.

species.description: Catmint is a perennial shrub from the mint family that looks good with its characteristic, small, blue blossoms in the shrub bed. If you cut it back directly after the first bloom, it may bloom a second time within one season. It exudes a pleasant, minty citrus scent. Catmint owes its name to its popularity with cats. Of course, not all cats react equally but it's not rare that cats passionately roll around in the plant.  From the fresh weed, a pleasantly tasting, slightly relaxing tea can be made. The leaves can be mixed well with other herbs. The edible, aromatic blossoms are also suitable for the decoration of desserts and fruit salads. It's best to use all plant parts freshly as they lose a major part of their taste with drying. Catmint also unfolds another interesting effect with regard to insects - they are neither attracted nor calmed down but permanently deterred by the contained essential oils.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance and easy to grow.

species.description: A fern with upright or drooping fronds usually up to 50 cm long. This species often produces distinctive round tubers on its creeping underground stems. Its 'leaves' are divided into numerous alternatively arranged narrow 'leaflets' (10-35 mm long and 4-11 mm wide). The lower parts of the 'leaflets' are usually somewhat overlapped and slightly lobed on one side, while their tips are relatively broad and somewhat rounded. Its brown spores are produced is small clusters midway between the centre and the margin of the undersides of the 'leaflets'.
species.maintenance: Requires moist and humid conditions with a high water requirement and a light fertiliser.

species.description: Nicotiana suaveolens is a slender, short lived perennial or annual herb native to Australia. It produces clusters of tubular, white to pale pink flowers with a strong sweet fragrance, especially at night. Flowering mainly in Summer and Autumn it is found in open forests, grasslands and disturbed areas often in well drained sandy or loamy soils. The Austral tobacco attracted nocturnal pollinators such as moths and adds delicate beauty to native gardens, while also playing a role in ecological restoration projects.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance

species.description: An aromatic perennial plant in warmer climates or annual in colder ones. The stems are hairy and bear simple toothed or entire leaves oppositely along the stem. The fragrant leaves are green or purple. The flowers are borne in terminal spikes. Fruits are nutless and produce numerous seeds.
species.maintenance: Plenty of sunlight will ensure healthy leaves. Ideal soil is light and airy but rich. Good drainage is essential. Fertilise is not recommended.

species.blurb: White-to-pink flowers on wiry stems, moving constantly, like a cloud of small butterflies.

species.description: Generous and exuberant, evening primrose flowers all Summer, with soft white flowers in such profusion they provide months of colour.
species.maintenance: Fertilise lightly in spring. Trim to keep neat as required.

species.description: The olive is one of those brilliant landscape and garden trees that is beautiful, productive, hardy and very versatile. They're also very easy to grow! Olive Trees grow very fast in height, and thicken at the same time. This is a low-fruiting variety of olive tree that has an upright growth. Responds well to pruning and can be grown with a single leader or easily pruned into a hedge for screening. Foliage is silvery.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance, formative pruning as required. Mulch and water well during the first 12 weeks.

species.description:
Olea europaea or the Fruiting Olive is a long lived, evergreen tree with beautiful, silvery grey/green foliage and a naturally slight weeping habit.
Its leaves are elongated oval and leathery, being lighter underneath (discolour) and it produces creamy-white flowers in spring that mature to green fruits in summer.These fast-growing plants can be set in rows and allowed to fill out, or, for something different the branches can be pleached, or interlaced with its neighbour’s to create a striking connected look.
species.maintenance: Olives are great for large gardens and can tolerate dry areas. They do well when pruned and look great when they are planted in groups. Long lived and extremely resilient. Cross pollination increases yields.

species.description: Olearia Ghost Town is an Australian native shrub with ‘ghostly’ edible leaves with a unique and pungent flavour. The stunning silvery foliage borne on upright branches and the masses of white daisy flowers in spring are the key features of this lovely Australian shrub. It can be used as a feature plant for a shrubbery where the light coloured foliage will contrast with other plants to create a year round feature.
species.maintenance: A light trim after it finishes blooming in Spring.

species.description: Olearia lirata, the Snowy Daisy Bush, is an evergreen shrub of south-eastern Australia in the daisy family (Asteraceae), usually 2–4 m tall. Its narrow, lance-shaped leaves are dark green above and pale grey beneath. In spring it is covered in clusters of white daisy flowers with yellow centres. It grows in woodlands and forests, often along gullies and forest margins. The nectar-rich flowers support bees, butterflies and other insects, and the dense foliage gives shelter to small birds.
species.maintenance: Pruning can help maintain a compact and bushy shape. You can prune after flowering to shape the plant and remove spent flowers. While it is generally considered to be drought-tolerant once established, regular watering is beneficial, especially during dry periods or in the first few months after planting. Snowy Daisy Bush doesn't usually require heavy fertilization. However, a balanced, slow-release fertilizer applied in spring can support healthy growth

species.description: Erect Native shrub to 1.6 m tall with scattered to crowded leaves 2-8 mm long and 0.8-2.5 mm wide with a rounded apex. Underside of leaves grey-woolly. [Flower-heads ](https://vro.agriculture.vic.gov.au/dpi/vro/vrosite.nsf/pages/water_sss_glossary#flowerhead)on the ends of side branches or in the angles between stems and leaves. Composite flowers white, pale blue to mauve outer ‘petals’ (ray [florets](https://vro.agriculture.vic.gov.au/dpi/vro/vrosite.nsf/pages/water_sss_glossary#floret)) with yellow centers (disk florets). Fruit an achene. Attracts butterflies and Native insects.
species.maintenance: Tolerates some Drought and Moderate frost. Requires moderate supplemantary watering.  Responds well to pruning.

species.description: A plant of particular loveliness this charming, long lived perennial carries deep sky blue for-get-me-not flowers over clumps of evergreen heart shaped leaves. This native of Turkish woodlands is happy growing in any lightly shaded or even sunny spot which can be given some extra watering during dry periods. Omphalodes ‘Cherry Ingram’ is a has deeper blue flowers than the species.
species.maintenance: Key care involves keeping soil consistently moist, trimming spent flower stems for tidiness, and dividing congested clumps every few years in spring or autumn.

species.description: Ophiopogon planiscapus ‘Nigrescens’, commonly known as Black Mondo Grass, is a striking evergreen perennial prized for its unique jet-black, grass-like foliage. Although often grouped with Ophiopogon japonicus (standard Green Mondo Grass), the black variety is specifically a cultivar of the species planiscapus. It typically grows in dense, arching clumps reaching 15–20 cm in height and spreads slowly via underground rhizomes to form a weed-resistant mat.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance. Annual top dressing with organic compost and slow-release fertiliser. Once established it is drought tolerant. Can be propagated by division. in early spring.

species.description: Hopley’s Oregano is more of an ornamental oregano, but it can also be used as a culinary herb. It has a mild “oregano” flavor when compared to other types of Oregano. The herb may be harvested fresh and chopped for use in breads, pasta dishes, stuffing, as pizza toppings, or to make oregano butter. The flavour is strongest just before flowering and small branches may be collected and used immediately. Alternatively the branches may be bunched and hung to dry, withIn the garden, Hopley’s Oregano produces hundreds or even thousands of tiny purple or lavender color blooms. You can harvest the flowers when they are brightest and use them in fresh flower arrangements or dry by hanging upside down.
species.maintenance: Divide the plant in Spring or take cuttings to create new plants.

species.description: Ornamental grape vines, scientifically known as Vitis vinifera,are deciduous climbers prized for their vibrant autumn foliage rather than their fruit. These fast-growing vines feature large, grape-like leaves that turn brilliant shades of red, orange, and purple in the fall. They are relatively low-maintenance, hardy, and long-lived, making them a popular choice for arbors, pergolas, walls, and fences.
species.maintenance: They thrive in full sun with well-drained soil and need support like a trellis or pergola. Pruning is the primary maintenance task, best done in winter, removing old flaky bark and cutting new growth back to a few buds. Watering is important during warm, dry periods, and fertilizing can promote healthy growth.

species.description: This grass-like clumping variety is ideal for informal group plantings amongst other shrubs in your landscapes, borders and raised beds or mass plantings as a ground cover under trees and on banks. The ornamental flowers bring a rare ‘true blue’ into your colour scheme – and while the pretty starry blue flowers only last a single day, they bloom so profusely the plant is rarely out of flower during Spring and early Summer. It prefers a semi shaded position, but can tolerate full sun. Butterfly attracting.
species.maintenance: Mulch to keep soil moist.

species.description: Evergreen shrub with sweetly perfumed cream-white flowers traditionally used to flavour Chinese tea and sweets.
species.maintenance: In Spring and Autumn they’ll appreciate a layer of compost or manure around their base and a dose of gypsum (if in heavy soils). After flowering prune lightly to maintain shape if necessary. Osmanthus are relatively free from pest and diseases. Plants grown in shady positions may succumb to scale and sooty mould but a few sprays of a horticultural oil will quickly get this under control. Spray both sides of the leaf to run off. Caterpillars have been known to have a chomp on leaves from time to time. Spray with Eco Oil if this becomes a problem.

species.description: A compact small shrub that has aromatic curry-scented leaves and clusters of white flowers all year round that are pink in bud. Trim back after each flower flush to trigger a new burst of blooms. This is a great feature or pot plant , and would also make an eye catching low hedge. Ozothamnus make superb long lasting cut flowers, and cutting them for this use will help stimulate new flowering growth as well.
species.maintenance: Feed with a good native plant food in the warmer months, being sure to water in well after fertilizing to prevent leaf burn.

species.description: Great for growing on a fence or trellis, this vigorous climbing plant produces large, tubular, pale pink flowers with a dark pink throat followed by a large fruit. It has a long flowering period between Spring to late Summer. It prefers full sun to part shade and reasonable drained soil. Once established it’s waterwise.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance

species.description: A vigorous climber with dark green leaves and golden red flowers in spring and summer. This plant can be used as a ground cover but will also climb vigorously if given something to support it. It can climb to great heights, so prune to height if needed.
species.maintenance: Low

species.description: Although the flowers of the corn poppy are most often red, cultivars are also available in other colors, notably the Shirley poppy, which grows in shades of white and pink. Blooms have 4-6 flower petals perched on long peduncles. There is a notable black blotch at the bottom of each petal, creating a dynamic contrast that is one of the hallmarks of this plant type. The common poppy’s stem is covered in fine bristly hair and irregularly pinnate, toothed leaves that span roughly 6 inches in length.
species.maintenance: Very low maintenance with minimal water needs. Seeds are self-sowing.

species.description: Boston ivy is a vigorous vine, that grows up to 50 feet long and cloaks horizontal and vertical structures with lustrous green foliage that erupts in shades of red, orange, and yellow in fall. The colorful three-lobed leaves (each lobe is pointed) hang onto the vines for several weeks as if celebrating the end of the growing season. Birds frequently visit to eat the plant's purple-black berries in autumn. Boston ivy can be grown in a sunny position or even in part shade. However, the autumn colour will be enhanced when the plant is exposed to sunlight. Boston ivy is a popular plant that many gardeners use to cover fences or grow over walls on different structures around the garden.
species.maintenance: In the beginning plant should be well watered to help the roots establish in the soil. A layer of soil around the base will help to retain moisture however keep it away from main stem. Once established only weekly watering is required.

species.description: A deciduous plant, Virginia creeper bears palmately compound leaves with five toothed leaflets; its fall colour ranges from yellow to red-purple. It climbs by means of characteristic disk-tipped tendrils. The small greenish flowers are borne in inconspicuous clusters. The fruit is a purple to black berry and is attractive to birds.
species.maintenance: Virginia creeper needs a strong vertical support. Plant in full sun for best autumn foliage colour. Pruning is not necessary except to control size.

species.description: Passiflora edulis, commonly called purple passionfruit, is a shallow-rooted, tendril-climbing, evergreen vine that typically grows to 9-12m and produces extremely showy bowl-shaped fragrant purple-white passionflowers (each to 3” wide) followed by edible, ovoid, purple passionfruits (to 2" across). The passion fruit is a truly multi-purpose plant. It is a vigorous tendril climber—the tendrils are those little “springs” you’ll notice beside the leaves—that will cover all manner of problem surfaces such as wire fences or arbours with minimal input required. Then it bears an abundance of often fragrant and distinctive flowers that, if all goes well, will become a crop of incredibly delicious fruit. Each flower has 5 greenish-white sepals, 5 white petals and a decorative corona of white filaments which are showy purple at the bases. Each fruit has a rough rind with as many as 250 tiny seeds inside, each seed being surrounded by an orange sac containing juice. Ripe fruits are edible off the vine or incorporated into a variety of food products such as beverages, jellies, fruit salads and sherbets
species.maintenance: Regular applications of liquid seaweed and liquid fertiliser will improve growth, flowering and fruiting. Ensure your plant is adequately watered during flowering and fruit development. If it is allowed to become dry while fruit is forming, it will often drop the fruit. With young plants remove the tips of vines regularly to encourage multiple branching and guide the vines over the structure as required. Trim excessive growth any time throughout the growing season to contain rambling vines or expose flowers and make them more accessible to pollinating insects. More substantial pruning can be done once a year in late winter to early spring to remove bulk and set plants up for the growing season. Cut the crown back to a 1-2m diameter, leaving a few growing tips. This will quickly stimulate new growth on which flowers and fruit will form. Pinch out the growing tips a few times to again encourage multiple branching.

species.description: Pelargonium australe, commonly known as Austral Stork's-bill or native geranium, is a native Australian plant found in various habitats across southern Australia. It's a low, herbaceous plant, typically growing to around 0.5 meters tall, with hairy, oval-shaped, and lobed leaves. The plant produces clusters of pink or white flowers with darker veins, especially on the upper petals. It's a hardy plant, adaptable to different soil types and tolerating full sun to light shade and frost.
species.maintenance: Responds to hard pruning. Requires well draining soil.

species.blurb: A low indigenous geranium with vivid magenta flowers, at home in the sunny gaps between tussocks.
species.description: Low tufted native geranium with a tuberous rootstock and clusters of vivid magenta flowers through spring and summer. Suits sunny, well-drained grassy spaces between tussocks.

A compact, clumping perennial grass with broad arching leaves and showy, purple feathery flowers through the warmer months. Great for mass planting, accent planting for rockeries and borders. Plumes suitable for dried arrangements.
species.maintenance: Remove the flower heads before they go to seed to prevent it self seeding.

species.description: Graceful tassels of mushroom-pink arch over the deep burgundy foliage. This dramatic purple fountain grass makes an impressive pot specimen or feature in the garden when planted amongst other grasses, succulents and perennials. This sterile cultivar will never become a weed. Quick growing, clumping exotic grass ideal for screening and feature planting. Long narrow upright in colour from Spring and through Autumn.
species.maintenance: Early Spring trim back to 200mm to 400mm to remove previous season flower stalks. Apply controlled release fertiliser and water in well.

species.blurb: Soft burgundy buttons scattered on fine stems, deepening in colour as the season turns.
species.description: A shorter, tidier fountain grass than most, forming a compact upright clump of bright green linear foliage. From midsummer it throws up tightly formed, soft burgundy-red button flowerheads held well clear of the leaves on fine stems, gradually fading to buff as they age and persisting into winter. The foliage turns golden-tan in autumn. Long-lasting and excellent for cutting, fresh or dried. It needs sun and free drainage — it dislikes wet feet, especially over winter, and in cold or heavy sites is often treated as an annual or short-lived perennial.
species.maintenance: Cut back to the ground in late winter before new growth appears. Free drainage over winter is the main requirement; a dry mulch helps in frost-prone positions. Water moderately through summer. Deadhead or remove seedheads before they shed if self-seeding is a concern — see note on genus weed risk.

species.description: A loosely mounded, tall and spreading perennial, which has masses of fine green leaves. From midsummer to early or mid-autumn bright crimson flowers which have deep carmine penciling in the throat are borne. Great for Bees.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance with a long Flowering season. Deadhead after flowering.

species.description: Penstemon 'Firebird' is a bushy semi-evergreen perennial boasting incredibly pretty, bell-shaped, crimson flowers with a throat of white with pale pink stripes.
species.maintenance: Lightly prune at the start of each spring. Light watering.

species.blurb: A smoky haze of lavender-blue on white stems, holding its structure well into autumn.

species.description: A compact selection of Russian Sage, growing to roughly half the size of the species. Finely cut, aromatic silver-grey foliage on upright silvery stems is topped through summer and autumn by a long haze of small lavender-blue flowers, giving the loose, smoky, see-through quality that makes Perovskia such a useful transition plant between structured shrubs and grasses. Woody at the base and herbaceous above, it thrives on lean, sharply drained soil and full sun, resents wet feet, and is highly attractive to bees. The smaller frame of 'Silvery Blue' suits it to front-of-border and courtyard planting where the full species would sprawl.
species.maintenance: Very low maintenance. Cut back hard in late winter to around 15cm above the ground, leaving a few strong buds, to keep the habit compact and flowering vigorous. Avoid rich soil and heavy feeding — lean conditions produce sturdier stems. Drought tolerant once established; water only through prolonged dry spells in the first year.

species.description: Hass avocado trees are dense evergreens with glossy, leathery leaves that have a vein-like pattern. They can grow up to seven feet tall in a container and up to 30 feet when planted in the ground. On the tree, Hass avocados have green skin. Once harvested, these skins turn nubbly and dark purple-black. The fruits are heavy, weighing between 200-300 grams. This is the variety with the longest harvest time as the fruit will store on the tree for up to 10 months. Avocados contain a wide range of nutrients. Health benefits of avocado consumption may include improving digestion, lowering the risk of depression, and preventing bone loss.
species.maintenance: As the tree grows, increase the amount of fertiliser each year to cater for its needs. Ensure the tree receives plenty of water during the hottest months of the year. Give a deep watering once a week in preference to shallow watering every other day.

species.blurb: Slender crimson spikes over clean green foliage, flowering steadily through the warm months.

species.description: Persicaria affinis, known by several common names such as Lesser Knotweed, East Indian Knotweed and Himalayan Knotweed, this plant is a mat-forming, semi-evergreen perennial that produces charming spikes densely packed with tiny flowers. When they first bloom in mid-summer, you can expect to see a deep rose-red colour. As the seasons progress, they will fade to a pale pink before turning brown in autumn. The foliage has elliptic to lance-shaped, deep-green leaves that turn a shade of bronze in autumn. It’s a great plant that evolves throughout the year to provide interest and contrast in the garden
species.maintenance: While Persicaria affinis is considered a drought-tolerant plant, it prefers moist, fertile soils that won’t dry out – so keep that in mind when planting. Other than that, there is minimal maintenance required for this plant.

species.description: A bushy biennial forming a dense rosette of rich green triangular aromatic leaves divided into flat or curly leaflets. Bloom will appear in the second year with small yellow green flowers at the end of stalks. Mainly 3 types: Curly, Italian or Hamburg.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance. Prefers full sun and regular watering. Apply complete fertiliser in spring and autumn

species.description: A small pretty, bushy shrub with slender silvery foliage and clusters of bright yellow flowers in Spring. Naturally occurring along the east coast of Australia. Prefers moist well drained soils in a protected position so Summer watering required in hot dry summer conditions. Ideal for native and cottage gardens, pots, rockeries and borders.
species.maintenance: Grows well in full sun to part shade. Prefers dry, well drained soils. Once established it can withstand dry period and mild frosts.

species.description: Phillyrea angustifolia, the Narrow-Leaved Mock Privet, is a dense, evergreen shrub from the Mediterranean basin — often described as a more refined cousin of the olive. It forms a tidy, rounded silhouette with fine, dark-green willow-like foliage and produces small, fragrant cream-white flowers in spring followed by dark blue-black berries. Tough, slow-growing, and elegant, it is increasingly favoured in contemporary garden design as a low-allergen, deer-resistant alternative to box and privet — clipping beautifully into formal shapes or growing freely as an informal screen.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance once established. Drought-tolerant and slow-growing. Clip lightly in late winter to early spring to maintain shape or formal lines, or leave to develop a natural rounded form. Tolerates hard pruning if needed. Grows in poor soils but thrives in well-drained Mediterranean conditions.

species.description: Philotheca myoporoides, commonly known as Long-Leaf Waxflower or Long-Leaf Philotheca, is a delightful evergreen shrub native to Australia. It is known for its attractive foliage and clusters of fragrant flowers. Philotheca myoporoides typically grows to a height of 3 to 6 feet (1 to 2 meters), forming a dense and compact shrub. The leaves are narrow, linear, and dark green, with a glossy appearance. They are clustered along the stems. Fragrant white or pale pink flowers appear in clusters during the spring and sometimes into early summer. These flowers have a delicate, pleasant scent. The plant may occasionally produce flowers at other times of the year, providing intermittent blooms.
species.maintenance: Prune lightly after the main flowering period to maintain a compact shape and remove any dead or leggy growth. Philotheca myoporoides prefers well-drained soil and should be watered regularly during dry periods. Apply a balanced, slow-release fertilizer in spring to promote healthy growth and flowering.

species.description: Phlomis fruticosa is a member of the mint family (Lamiaceae) native to dry, rocky areas from Italy and Sardinia through to Turkey and the Middle East. Despite its common name, it is not a true sage (genus Salvia) and possesses no culinary aroma or taste. It has earned the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit for its reliable performance. It forms a dense, mounding shrub typically 1m x 1m, though some varieties can reach up to 1.8m in height. It features woolly, wrinkled grey-green leaves and tubular, hooded yellow flowers arranged in spherical clusters called verticillasters. Lemon Blush has masses of soft yellow-primrose hooded flowers, faintly blushed pink, are held in whorls along upright spires during spring.
species.maintenance: Cut the plant back by approximately half its size in autumn or spring to maintain a bushy shape and encourage fresh growth. Seed heads can be left on the plant through winter to provide ornamental silhouettes.

species.description: Phoenix roebelenii, the Pygmy Date Palm, is an elegant, slow-growing palm from Southeast Asia. Forms a slender single or multi-stemmed trunk topped with arching, finely-divided dark green fronds that drape gracefully. Reaches 2–3m in cultivation, making it one of the most popular small-scale feature palms for courtyards, pool surrounds, and container plantings. Produces small cream flowers in spring followed by edible (though small and seedy) date-like fruits on female plants. Tolerates a wide range of conditions from full sun to part shade and is moderately frost-tolerant once established.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance once established. Water regularly while young; mature palms tolerate moderate drought. Remove old browning fronds cleanly; wear gloves as the leaf bases have sharp spines. Feed with palm fertiliser in spring.
Water well until established and regularly during Summer. Slow release fertiliser in Spring.  Remove older leaves and cut back half way every 4-5 years.  Divide clumps in Spring.

species.description: Bright red new foliage and glossy green mature leaves. Produces small white flowers in large clusters in Spring.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance. Prune to promote new growth and maintain shape. Use slow-release fertiliser twice yearly.

species.description: Pimelea ferruginea, commonly known as pink rice flower or coastal banjine, is a dense, rounded, and compact evergreen shrub native. It is highly prized for its brilliant floral display in spring and its neat, low-maintenance habit. A great feature plant for rockeries, borders or pots. Attracts butterflies. It likes a well drained soil, and a sunny position to be at its best.
species.maintenance: Lightly prune after flowering to maintain a compact shape and encourage a bushier habit. You can also hard prune it to maintain its shape. Use sharp, clean tools for clean cuts. Avoid heavy pruning to keep the plant healthy. Use a slow-release, native-plant fertilizer low in phosphorus when planting. Fertilize in spring, watering it in well afterward to avoid burning leaves or roots.

species.description: Masses of bright pink pom pom like flower heads complement the glossy dark green foliage on a compact dwarf shrub. Use it as a feature plant for the front of a sunny shrubbery or rockery or as a low growing pot plant. It is perfectly suited to windy and salty conditions near the ocean.
species.maintenance: Trim back behind the spent flowers at the end of spring.

species.description: Upright, multi-stemmed shrub to 60 cm tall and 60 cm wide. Pointed leaves opposite, decussate, blue-green, up to 20 mm long. Small tubular white flowers in dense clusters at the top of stems.
species.maintenance: No Maintenance

species.description: Pimelea humilis, the Common Rice-flower, is a low, spreading native shrub, usually 10–50 cm tall and up to about 1 m wide, often suckering to form small colonies. It has small, opposite, oval leaves and, from spring into early summer, rounded heads of tubular white to cream (sometimes pink-tinged) flowers at the tips of the stems. Widespread in grasslands, grassy woodlands and dry forests of south-eastern Australia, it grows in well-drained soils in sun or dappled shade. The flowers attract butterflies, moths and native bees. Like other Pimeleas, the plant is toxic if eaten.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance. Water until established, then only in extended dry spells. Light tip prune after flowering keeps it compact. No fertiliser needed. Toxic if eaten — keep away from grazing animals.
Responds well to pruning and can be shaped. Feeding twice a year, Can be pruned to size and shape. Can be prone tyo Leaf spot and powdery mildew.

species.description: a vigorous grower that stays very compact and round branching freely from its base. it has bright mint-green glossy leaves with small chocolate-purple flowers in late spring and early summer. Height 80cm Width 80cm
species.maintenance: Very low maintenance that requires very little pruning.

species.description: Pittosporums make beautiful hedges and privacy screens. Their small neat leaves are glossy and bright, contrasting with dark stems; their habit is dense enough to shelter small native birds, but not thick and gloomy; and they respond very well to clipping, while staying neat when left alone. Silver Sheen has attractively silvery-green leaves year round. A fabulous bushy, evergreen tree making it ideal for hedging. Soft green foliage with a hint of silver.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance requiring trimming twice per year.

species.description: A spreading Australian native evergreen shrub with velvety broad silver leaves. A useful heat and dry tolerant ground cover or understory plant for shade or sun, thriving beneath trees in tough, competitive conditions. Spikes of white flowers on mauve stems rise above the foliage in autumn. An ideal plant for sprawling over challenging bare patches to outcompete weeds and as a silver highlight to dull, forgotten areas. One of the few silver-leafed plants that will grow in shade.
species.maintenance: Prune back after flowering, or in early spring in colder areas. It is frost sensitive, but if grown in the shade of taller shrubs and trees, this will provide some protection. All Plectranthus need to be replaced by new cuttings every so often as they get a bit straggly after a few years.

species.description: Plectranthus ecklonii 'White' (White Spurflower) is a vigorous, upright, soft-wooded shrub, growing up to 2.5–3m tall and 2m wide. It is highly valued for its massed, upright plumes of white flowers that bloom in shady, dry spots from late summer through autumn. It prefers shade and needs heavy pruning in late winter.
species.maintenance: Crucial for maintaining a neat shape. Cut the plant back severely (to roughly 30cm or to about 1/3-1/4 of its height) in early spring or immediately after flowering to prevent it from becoming too woody and leggy.

species.description: Plectranthus parviflorus, commonly known as cockspur flower or little spurflower, is an Australian native shrub known for its ornamental foliage, drought tolerance, and adaptability to a wide range of garden conditions. This herbaceous, non-aromatic shrub typically grows between 10 and 70 cm tall. The stems and toothed leaves are somewhat fleshy and hairy. The leaves can vary in shape from circular to ovate. Crushed leaves produce a faint, minty scent. The plant produces continuous spikes of small, sweet-smelling, pale blue to violet-blue flowers throughout the year.
species.maintenance: A light prune after flowering will help keep the plant tidy and encourage denser foliage. The species readily self-seeds and may need to be managed to prevent it from spreading to unwanted areas.

species.description: Internationally recognised with an 'Award of Garden Merit' from the prestigious Royal Horticultural Society in the UK, MONA® Lavender Plectranthus 'Plepalila' is a particularly attractive form of Plectranthus that does not spread like other members of the family, but rather forms a neat low shrub with an upright, erect habit. Numerous spikes of lavender coloured flowers begin to appear from late summer through autumn complimenting the ornamental foliage of deep green leaves with dark wine purple coloured undersides, typical of many of the Plectranthus species.
species.maintenance:
Water requirements are low and prefers a moist, well drained soil. Choose a shaded to semi-shaded protected location. Protect from frosts and very low
temperatures. A light pruning after flowering will help maintain a neat shape and encourage dense foliage growth.

species.description: A semi spreading Australian native evergreen shrub with velvety broad silver leaves. A useful heat and dry tolerant ground cover or understory plant for shade or sun, thriving beneath trees in tough, competitive conditions. Sweetly aromatic undershrub to c. 80 cm high; branches decumbent or suberect, densely covered with short white, retrorse hairs and many shorter gland-tipped hairs, sessile glands very few or absent. One of the few silver-leafed plants that will grow in shade.
species.maintenance: Prune back after flowering, or in early spring in colder areas. It is frost sensitive, but if grown in the shade of taller shrubs and trees, this will provide some protection. All Plectranthus need to be replaced by new cuttings every so often as they get a bit straggly after a few years.

species.description: Powdery blue flowers in abundance on a versatile plant. Shrub, hedge, climber, espaliered vine, trained rambler, topiary bush - this plant will make itself at home in almost any situation! The more you clip it the more it seems to flower - but happy to scramble over a pergola or arch without too much attention. Loves the sun.
species.maintenance: Requires regular watering especially when growing. Twice yearly application of all purpose fertiliser.

species.description: The most graceful of the tussock grasses forming a fine textured mound of shining light brown to light green foliage. Upright arching stalks support slender inflorescences. Grows on a wide range of soils and is drought tolerant. It produces delicate, feathery bronze or tawny flower panicles in summer that sway gracefully in the wind. The name Poa is Greek for "grass," and cita comes from the Latin citus, meaning "put in motion," referring to how the grass moves in the breeze.
species.maintenance: Requires very little care. It can be cut back hard in late winter or early spring to rejuvenate growth if it becomes untidy.

species.description: This attractive form tussock grass has blue-green foliage Poa clivicola is a perennial, tufted, tussock grass, growing up to 60cm tall. Leaf sheaths are bleached at the base, herbaceous, pallid, and glabrous. Leaves are tightly in-rolled, tough to the touch, and very fine at 0.2-0.4mm wide. Leaves are mostly basal. Leaf-sheaths can be smooth or scaberulous and glabrous on surface. Ligules are 0.5-1.5mm long, truncate and firm. Panicles are open and pyramidal. Lemmas are 3-4mm long, hairless or with sparse localized hairs. And displays viviparous after Summer flowering. A very hardy ornamental grass.
species.maintenance: No maintenance

species.description: Poa ensiformis, the Sword Tussock-grass, is a soft, dense, shade-tolerant Australian native perennial grass. It forms attractive arching tussocks of bright green, sword-shaped leaves, with airy branched flower heads in spring and summer. Native to moist forests and gully systems of southeastern Australia, it is one of the few Poa species that thrives in shade, making it an excellent choice for woodland understorey, fern gully, and shaded courtyard planting.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance. Cut back to one-third height every 2–3 years in late autumn to refresh foliage. Keep moist in dry periods; tolerates dry shade once established.

species.blurb: An indigenous tussock with blue-green leaves and delicate plumes held above the foliage.
species.description: Poa labillardierei is a dense coarsely tufted grasses and can reach a height of 120 cm. The greyish-green or blue-green leaves are long and slender with rolled or flat blades. Poa labillardierei flowers in Spring to Summer. The flower heads are like delicate plumes that extend above the highly ornamental foliage making the species very attractive for horticulture.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance. Trim back to half foliage height end of March/April.

species.description: Poa labillardierei ‘Eskdale’ (Common Tussock-Grass) is a hardy, fast-growing, evergreen native perennial grass known for its dense, finely textured, blue-grey foliage. Reaching roughly 0.6−1m in height and width, it produces delicate, feathery flower heads in summer. It is highly versatile, ideal for coastal gardens, erosion control, mass planting, and modern landscapes.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance. Trim back to half foliage height end of March/April.

species.description: Poa morrisii, the Soft Tussock-grass (also Velvet Tussock-grass), is a dense, fine-leaved perennial tussock grass of south-eastern Australia, usually 30–60 cm tall. Its narrow, soft, grey-green to blue-green leaves are covered in fine hairs, giving the tussock a velvety texture. Open, airy flower heads rise above the foliage in spring. It grows naturally in dry forests and woodlands on well-drained soils, tolerating dry conditions and dappled shade. The tussocks provide shelter and seed for small birds, lizards and invertebrates.
species.maintenance: Very low maintenance. Water until established. Comb out old leaves or cut back by half every few years in late autumn to refresh. No fertiliser needed.

species.description: Poa sieberiana is a dense tussock grass with green to greyish green leaves which grow to about 30 cm long, with seeds heads to 1 metre tall. It has a large natural range, growing in NSW, from near coastal areas, growing commonly on the tablelands and western slopes, to the western plains, extending into south-east Queensland and right through Victoria and Tasmania, into the east of South Australia.It is found often in dry sclerophyll woodland and forests, especially on high rocky slopes but also creeklines and cold valleys. This species has very attractive inflorescences (panicles) which rise well above the foliage and are flexible in nature, from spring through to summer with pale green to purple seed heads
species.maintenance: Very low maintenance once established. Remove spent seed heads late winter.

species.description: Perennial herb to 0.8 m high, arising annually from a thickened persistent rootstock. Stems woolly to almost hairless, unbranched. Leaves basal and alternating up the stems, 1-20 cm long, 2-20 mm wide, rough to becoming hairless, margins flat to rolled down, bases stem clasping. Basal leaves stalked, stem leaves stalkless. Flower heads with 20–50 yellow to orange 'petals' 10–30 mm long, deeply 3-5 toothed, and yellow centres with many florets. Flower heads mostly 20–40 mm in diameter below the 'petals', hemispherical to bell-shaped, Flower heads usually single, rarely 2-8 per stem.
species.maintenance: No Maintenance

species.description: Polystichum polyblepharum, the Tassel Fern, is an evergreen fern from Japan and southern Korea. Forms a symmetrical shuttlecock rosette of glossy, dark green, twice-divided fronds to around 60–80cm. New croziers unfurl clothed in golden-bronze hairs and arch backwards before settling — the habit that gives the plant its common name. Tougher and glossier than most ferns, it holds its form through winter and provides a reliable dark-green base layer in shaded planting.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance. Prefers humus-rich, free-draining soil with consistent moisture — mulch well. Cut old and damaged fronds back to the base in late winter, before the new croziers emerge. Shelter from wind and direct hot sun.

species.description: Indigenous ground fern with glossy, finely divided dark-green fronds that form plantlets at the tips. Local equivalent of the Japanese tassel fern for shaded beds.

A Shrub or small tree with dark brown, fairly smooth bark with some fissures and longitudinal irregularities. Branches are covered with rust coloured star shaped hairs when young. Leaves are egg shaped 40-120mm long and 20-60mm wide with tooth shaped edges.
species.maintenance: Prune to shape and for denser foilage. Give water in dry hot times

species.description: Pomaderris racemosa, commonly known as slender pomaderris or cluster pomaderris, is an Australian native shrub or small tree in the family Rhamnaceae. It is endemic to south-eastern Australia, specifically South Australia, Victoria, and Tasmania. It is suitable as a taller screening plant for beneath trees or in areas where space is limited due to its erect habit. It tolerates dappled to semi-shade conditions. Its dense foliage and attractive flowers provide habitat for local wildlife.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance.

species.description: Prunus lusitanica, or Portugal Laurel as it’s more commonly known, is an evergreen shrub or small tree with glossy, leathery dark green leaves with dark brown bark. In late spring or early summer, it produces tiny white, fragrant flowers followed by small red cherries that ripen to a dark-purple shade by autumn. While the berries are not suitable for human consumption, once ripe, birds love them. An average Portuguese laurel growth rate is 18 inches per year, although good soil and irrigation can add an extra 6 inches of growth. This makes it among the fastest growing hedge varieties with only Cherry laurel and Leylandii growing at a faster pace (of the popular hedge types).
species.maintenance: Responds well to pruning. Fertilise in early Spring with a complete fertiliser.

species.description: A low growing trailing habit with a spread of around 30-40cm and height around 20cm. Leaves are succulent like small small and fleshy.  Plant produces jewel-like, multi-petalled blooms around 2.5cm wide.
species.maintenance: Very minimal care. Trim off spent flowers to keep plants tidy and rotate containers to maximise sun. Flowers close if in the shade. Apply liquid fertiliser every few weeks. Whole plant can die in winter but likely will self seed to sprout once weather warms up.

species.description: One of the oldest cultivated trees with beautiful silver foliage, bearing plump delicious green fruit which turn black if left. Can be picked by hand or by shaking the tree with a sheet underneath.
species.maintenance: Top up pot with fresh soil every couple of years and water lightly but regularly. In ground fertilise in early spring and late summer. Prune out suckers and low branches during winter. Can be prone to olive lace bug. Eco-oil to prevent.

species.blurb: A flat indigenous mat studded with pale star flowers, knitting the shadier pockets together.
species.description: Alpine Pratia is a mat forming perennial with tiny, dark green serrated leaves. This thick mat of foliage can be almost completely covered by a mass of blue star like flowers in late Spring through to Autumn. A flat grower that is a great weed suppressor and is also helpful with erosion control.
species.maintenance: Cutting back. Keep well-watered in Summer.

species.description: Prostanthera lasianthos, the Victorian Christmas Bush, is a large aromatic shrub or small tree, usually 2–6 m in gardens. It has lance-shaped, finely toothed leaves and, from late spring into summer, masses of white flowers tinged with lilac and spotted purple and orange in the throat. It occurs naturally in moist gullies and forest margins of eastern Australia, and prefers part shade with moist, well-drained soil. The flowers are visited by native bees and other insects. Can be lightly pruned after flowering to keep it dense.
species.maintenance: Water regularly through dry periods, especially in its first summers. Mulch to keep the roots cool and moist. Prune lightly after flowering to keep it dense; avoid cutting into old wood.

species.description: *Prostanthera melissifolia*, commonly known as Balm Mint-bush, is an aromatic native Australian shrub known for its fragrant foliage and profuse spring flowers. The plant produces abundant flowers in loose terminal sprays, primarily during spring (October to December). The flowers are typically mauve, purple, or pink. It is an excellent choice for borders, hedging, or as a background shrub in a garden setting. Its aromatic qualities make it ideal for planting near pathways or windows where the scent can be appreciated. Plant in a position that receives full sun to part shade and is sheltered from hot, drying winds. Positioning it near a pathway allows you to enjoy the minty aroma when brushing past the foliage.
species.maintenance: Maintaining Prostanthera melissifolia (Balm Mint-bush) is relatively simple, focusing primarily on correct watering, annual pruning, and appropriate feeding to ensure it thrives in a well-drained spot.

species.description: Prostanthera ovalifolia, the Oval-leaf Mint Bush, is a fast-growing evergreen Australian shrub smothered in mauve-purple tubular flowers through spring. The small oval leaves are strongly aromatic when crushed, releasing a sharp mint scent that carries on warm days. Reaches 2-3m in cultivation with an open, slightly arching habit. Excellent as a mid-layer scent plant, informal screen or cut flower, and highly attractive to native bees and small nectar-feeding birds. Prefers good drainage and appreciates a cool root run.
species.maintenance: Prune hard immediately after flowering to keep dense and prolong life - mint bushes are naturally short-lived (5-8 years) and go woody if left untrimmed. Needs well-drained soil; avoid wet feet. Mulch to keep roots cool. Light native fertiliser in spring.

species.description: Prostanthera porcata is a species of flowering plant in the family Lamiaceae and is endemic to the Budawang Range in south-eastern New South Wales. It is a small, erect shrub with glabrous branches, elliptic leaves and deep pink or pink and cream-coloured flowers.
species.maintenance: Regular, light pruning after flowering to maintain a bushy shape, ensuring it doesn't get waterlogged to avoid root rot.

species.description: A small to medium dense shrub with highly aromatic foliage continuously releasing a mint essence into the atmosphere. A lavish display of violet flowers all but hides the soft leaves throughout spring and early summer, attracting butterflies and small insect-eating birds. Positioning of prostantheras as border plants or near pathways is recommended as the mint odour is released when brushed against. Oil from the leaves of some species is distilled for use in cosmetics and as soap additives.
species.maintenance: Easily trimmed to contain height.  Mint fragrant blooms can be picked and taken indoors. This plant is highly drought-tolerant, requiring minimal water once established. Its resilience makes it ideal for water-wise gardens, offering beauty without excessive maintenance.

species.description: Medium evergreen native shrub with small round aromatic leaves and clusters of purple flowers during Spring. This hardy Mint Bush has a mild minty aroma when crushed or brushed past. Ideal for hedging, containers and borders. Will attract native bees and beneficial insects into the garden.
species.maintenance: Prune by one-third after spring flowering to maintain shape and prevent woodiness. Water during dry spells, but avoid waterlogged soil to prevent root rot.

species.description: There is no comparison to tree ripened apricots with their delicious flavour, sweet juicy flesh and unique aroma.
species.maintenance: A low maintenance tree ideal for backyards, pots, or tubs because of its dwarfing tree size.

species.description: Prunus cerasifera ‘Oakville Crimson Spire’ is a stunning and versatile deciduous tree that adds a touch of elegance to any landscape.
