An ideal specimen for narrow areas, courtyards or borders where space is limited. Will provide a profuse show of blossom in spring and highly contrasting dark purple foliage in summer. This is a deciduous tree.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance.

species.description: Prunus incisa 'Kojo-no-mai' is a compact deciduous Fuji Cherry selection from Japan, whose name translates roughly as 'dance of the little butterflies'. The structure is the feature: fine zig-zagging twiggy branches that hold their character through winter. Pale pink buds open to small single white-pink blossoms along bare wood in late winter and early spring, before the small serrated green leaves emerge, which colour orange and red in autumn. Slow-growing to around 2–2.5m, making it one of the few genuinely small-garden flowering cherries.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance. Prune lightly and only immediately after flowering — the zig-zag branch structure is the point, so avoid heading cuts. Mulch and keep moist through summer. Watch for aphids on new growth. Needs free-draining soil; will sulk in heavy wet clay.

species.description: Peaches (Prunus persica) are small fruit with a fuzzy peel and a sweet white or yellow flesh. They are thought to have originated in China more than 8,000 years ago. Peaches are related to plums, apricots, cherries, and almonds. They’re considered drupes or stone fruit because their flesh surrounds a shell that houses an edible seed. ‘No Bubble No Trouble’ peach has shown a high degree of resistance to leaf curl, making it an easy tree to establish and maintain in the home garden. This new cultivar bears prolific white fleshed freestone peaches, ready to harvest in late February and is self fertile.
species.maintenance: Fertilise during the growing season. Water well during Summer. To ensure large fruit, keep up water during fruit development and thin fruit to maximise fruit size and avoid brown rot. Mulch to retain soil moisture and control weeds. Prune to vase shape in late Summer or Autumn after harvesting. Be sure to spray with copper prior to budburst to avoid leaf curl.

species.description: Produces large plums with golden flesh, they are chin-dribblingly juicy when the skin turns from bright red to purple indicating plums are fully ripe.
species.maintenance: Easy to grow fruit trees, plums are high yielding and best trained to an open vase shape for maximum fruiting. Improve soil with aged compost and manure prior to planting.

species.description: A true blood plum with dark-red mid-sized rounded fruits, borne on vigorous upright branches that develop a willowy habit. The fruit is sweet with a hint of tart making it both a fresh eater as well as the perfect plum for jams and preserves.
species.maintenance: Easy to grow fruit trees, plums are high yielding and best trained to an open vase shape for maximum fruiting. Improve soil with aged compost and manure prior to planting.

species.description: The variety of Pteris cretica ferns that are cultivated display different shaped and colored fronds, but share very similar characteristics and care requirements. The P.cretica albolineata also called the variegated table fern is one of the most common that has broad green leaflets and a pale center. The P.cretica has slimmer green leaflets with serrated edges. The growth habit (clump-forming) of this species is to produce wiry thread-like stalks from small rhizomes in the soil and the stalks produce pinnate leaflets in rows. In a way, they kind of resemble a palm to me in looks, although they do not have a main stem.
species.maintenance: A need for High humidity and misting is essential. Pruning is good for keeping the plant in good shape and looking healthy and will encourage new growth. Just cut back any dying or untidy fronds when needed by cutting with a sharp knife or secateurs as close to the bottom of the stalk as possible.

species.description: A graceful native fern that grows well throughout most of Australia, Pteris Tender Brake Fern (Pteris tremula) is an attractive Fern for ferneries, moist shaded garden positions and container gardens. Tolerating semi shade to full sun, this beautiful Fern is a medium sized erect growing plant that features fine lacy foliage in delicate shades of pale green and reddish brown stems.

Ptilotus spathulatus, commonly known as Pussy Tails or Sprawling Mulla Mulla, is a small, prostrate perennial herb native to a wide range of habitats across southern Australia, including Victoria, South Australia, Western Australia, New South Wales, and Tasmania. It is known for its distinctive, fluffy, cylindrical flower heads. The flowers grow in dense, upright, cone-shaped or cylindrical spikes at the end of long stems. The flower heads are typically greenish, yellow, or cream-colored, often with pink tips, and have a soft, fluffy or "feathered" appearance due to long hairs on the flowers. This unique plant provides a valuable food source for ground-dwelling creatures and attracts native bees.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance.

species.description: Pultenaea daphnoides, commonly known as the Large-leaf Bush-pea, is a hardy, upright Australian native shrub belonging to the pea family (Fabaceae). It is highly celebrated for its brilliant, prolific spring floral display and unique foliage that resembles a Daphne plant. It has prolific, dense terminal clusters of bright golden-yellow pea flowers with contrasting reddish-brown or purple centres, blooming primarily from August to November.
species.maintenance: Cut back lightly right after spring flowering. This prevents woodiness and encourages dense growth. Avoid cutting into old wood without leaves. Water regularly during the first summer. Once established, it survives on natural rainfall and has high drought tolerance. Apply a low-phosphorus, native-specific fertilizer in early spring. Avoid standard fertilizers, as phosphorus damages its roots.

species.description: Pycnosorus globosus (billy buttons), member of the Asteraceae (Daisy) family, is a dense ground cover with a spread of at least 50 centimetres. Soft leaves are grey, long and narrow. Golden globular flower heads are carried above the foliage on long stems. A large number of flowers appear in Spring and Summer. Mature plants may carry dozens of flower heads. The foliage provides a background to the flowers.
species.maintenance: Deadhead to encourage further flushes of flowers. Keep well watered. Use a slow release, low phosphorus fertiliser. Do not mulch too heavily.

species.description: An upright ornamental pear with dense habit and attractive foliage. It isa deciduous tree with glossy green leaves that turn orange during autumn and produce soft white blossoms in Spring. Produces small pears not suitable for eating.
species.maintenance: Water well until established then deep once a week. Mulch with bark or Sugarcane. Prune to achieve balance shape during autumn Fertilise twice a year.

species.description: Graceful and small deciduous pear with fine, silvery grey willow-like leaves becoming glossy green with maturity. Known as a 'weeper' it forms a dense rounded head with branches that are fine and pendulous but irregular creating a slightly wild flowing specimen. Spring blossom is delicate creamy white. Fruit is pear-shaped, grey green but inedible. Brief period of yellow autumn foliage. 'Salix' is the Latin word for 'willow'. A great feature tree for smaller gardens.
species.maintenance: Prune in late autumn to keep the canopy compact. Remove branches below the canopy to make sure the rootstock is not going to overtake, and to keep a 'clean' stem.

species.description: Small hardy evergreen shrub with dark green foliage that has a copper tone on new foliage. Bears pinky white flowers in the summer.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance, minimum water once established. Prune lightly to encourage dense compact growth.

species.description: Raphiolepis 'Oriental Pearl', commonly known as Indian Hawthorn, is a compact evergreen shrub that displays a neat, rounded form. It typically reaches a height of 3 to 4 feet (0.9 to 1.2 meters) and spreads to about the same width. The glossy, leathery leaves are dark green, adding a touch of elegance to the overall appearance of the plant. The foliage forms a dense canopy, making it ideal for creating hedges or borders in gardens.
species.maintenance: Indian Hawthorn is relatively low-maintenance, making it a popular choice for both novice and experienced gardeners. It thrives in well-drained soils and requires regular watering, especially during hot and dry periods. Pruning is recommended after the blooming period to maintain a tidy shape and promote new growth. This shrub is generally disease-resistant and tolerates a variety of environmental condition

species.botanical_name: Rhagodia candolleana ssp. candolleana Seaberry Saltbush

species.description: A dwarf form of Rhaphiolepis that has stunning shiny dark leathery green leaves with red tipped fresh growth. Masses of beautiful dainty, fragrant white and pink flowers appear in spring and summer. Grows in full sun to part shade but produces more flowers when planted in full sun. A fantastic addition to the landscape making a great formal or informal hedge as well as a stand alone shrub.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance. Low watering requirements.

species.description: Clumping palm with fans of glossy dark-green leaves on slender canes. Elegant vertical screen for shade and sheltered corners; scorches in hot sun.

Tall, evergreen shrub with vigorous growth habit and large, leathery dark-green foliage that has thin, brown indumentum. In Spring, large conical trusses of bold, pink flowers make a stunning display.
species.maintenance: Deadhead flowers.

species.description: Rhododendron racemosum CGG#14035 Compact and small-leaved evergreen shrubs with white to pale or deep pink flowers in mid-spring. The attractive foliage is often blue-green on the upper surface with a glaucous white coating on the lower. Grown from seed collected in the wild in a newly explored region far to the east of where this species has ever been recorded. Bright red stems and wavy-margined leaves. Easy and tough in sun or light shade and drought tolerant once established.
species.maintenance: Regular even moisture.

species.description: Red currant (Ribes *nigrum*) is an upright small sized deciduous shrub that fruits mid Summer.
species.maintenance: Red currants like to be fed. Sprinkle with general fertiliser each Spring and top dress with well broken down animal manure or compost. Pruning should be done in Winter. Leave between eight and ten healthy, strong main branches each year. The ideal bush shape is an open ‘goblet’ with a single main stem and an open space inside the bush to allow light in and to aid air circulation.

species.description: Roses are a diverse genus of flowering plants known for their beauty, fragrance, and symbolism of love and affection. They are popular ornamental plants in gardens worldwide and are used commercially for cut flowers, perfume (rose oil and water), and food products like rose hips and syrups. A broad and hardy category with a wide range of sizes and forms. They are known for their resilience, disease resistance, and natural, informal look, perfect for hedges or mass plantings.
species.maintenance: Mulch annually with well rotted organic matter.  Prune annually after flowering to control shape and encourage flowering.

species.description: A white floribunda rose which features ruffled, double white blooms which can be light pink.  The flowers have a light fragrance and are around 7cm across in size. Flowering generally right through summer.
species.maintenance: Water generously until well established. WEAR TOUGH GLOVES: prune late winter or early Spring. Remove any dead, damaged plants and open up centre to allow air and prevent disease. Mulch annually with well rotted manure,

species.description: Rosmarinus Blue Lagoon is an attractive, small shrub. It has scented green foliage with a bushy habit. Blue flowers will appear from winter to spring. Ideal for rockeries, borders and flat groundcovers, it is a low maintenance plant and can also be used in home cooking.
species.maintenance: Rosemary "Blue Lagoon" is a relatively low-maintenance plant, but it still requires some care to thrive. It prefers full sun and well-drained soil, so ensure it's planted in a spot that receives at least six hours of sunlight daily and that excess water can drain away. Regular, but not excessive, watering is important, especially when the plant is young or during hot, dry periods. Pruning after flowering helps maintain its shape and encourage bushiness.

species.description: Low growing and spreading evergreen shrub with strong aromatic, needle like leaves about 5cm long. Clusters of pale blue flowers in Spring and Summer. Used extensively for culinary purposes. Very fragrant.  When crushed it releases fragrant oils These oils are used for perfumes, herbal remedies and aromatherapy, as well as uncrushed leaves in cooking (great sprinkled on a lamb roast).
species.maintenance: Only prune to shape by cutting when required.

species.description: A beautiful, thicket-forming deciduous shrub adorned with a dense foliage of maple like green leaves. Fragrant white flowers appear in showy clusters. They are followed by vibrant scarlet berries which mature in mid to late summer, The stems are thornless and the fruit is edible and can be used to make jam. In autumn the leaves turn brillant orange to maroon.
species.maintenance: Remove canes immediately after fruit has been harvested. In winter remove any damaged canes and leave only well spaced canes. Keep moist.

species.description: Rudbeckia fulgida plants make a deep-green, bushy clump to around 70cm tall and 40 to 50cm across. A profuse display of brown-eyed, golden-orange daisies are produced from midsummer through Autumn. Seedheads also have good winter interest. A great choice for mass planting, combining especially well with ornamental grasses. Excellent for cutting. Removing faded flowers regularly will greatly increase the blooming time. Plants may be easily divided in early spring. Attractive to butterflies.
species.maintenance: Once Rudbeckia is established in the landscape, dead foliage and stems can be removed in the fall, winter, or early spring. Deadheading old flowers will encourage re-blooming and keep the plants looking their best. Black-eyed Susans typically bloom in late spring through early fall. Annual Rudbeckia are planted in spring after the last chance of frost.

species.description: Salvia 'Santa Barbara' is a dwarf form of the common Mexican Sage. It is widely known for it's tough garden performance making it an exceptional selection for use in both domestic and commercial landscapes. Showy long stems of velvety purple flowers crown the silvery green foliage over summer through autumn. Compact habit and drought resistance make this Salvia a great addition to any garden.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance. It requires minimal watering once established and can tolerate drought conditions.Pruning is essential for maintaining its shape and encouraging new growth, typically done in early spring by cutting back old stems to the base once new growth appears.

species.blurb: Clear sky-blue flowers on an open, airy frame.

species.description: Salvia apiana is a perennial evergreen that can grow to heights of up to 1.5 metres  tall and spread as far as 1.3 metres wide. Sacred White Sage enjoys full sun and once established, doesn’t require much watering. The whitish, silvery leaves can grow to almost 10cm (4 inches) and are opposite with crenulate margins. Each leaf is covered in hairs that trigger oil glands which when rubbed release a strong aroma. The white almost lavender coloured flowers grow on stalks beyond the foliage and are very attractive to bees and butterflies. Sacred White Sage prefers a low-nutrient soil so it does not require fertiliser, just a soil that drains well and is located in a sunny position with good air circulation.
species.maintenance: Pinch back regularly to maintain a compact Bush.

species.description: One of the smallest of the Salvia family, 'Mystic Spires' produce broad, green leaves with blooms of dark blue atop long stems. 'Mystic Blue Spires' is a tender perennial that is typically grown as a summer season bedding plant. This striking salvia bears a close resemblance to lavender and features dark flower spikes that unfurl to reveal stunning deep blue flowers that tower above its slender, verdant foliage. This variety is compact and has multiple branches that produce a profusion of blooms from late spring until the first frost. It is an effortless plant to grow, requiring minimal maintenance and deadheading, and is a favourite among butterflies. It is also ideal for cut flower arrangements, and similar to other salvias, it is highly resistant to deer and rabbit damage.
species.maintenance: Remove spent flowers regularly to promote repeat flowering. Prune back by half after flowering has finished to maintain a compact growth habit. Low maintenance with low water requirements.

species.description: With vibrant color and an alluring, fruity scent, there is much to love about pineapple sage (Salvia elegans). While this plant is mainly known for its aromatic leaves that smell like pineapple when crushed, both the leaves and flowers are edible, and they can be used as garnishes or brewed into a refreshing herbal tea. Pineapple sage has showy, chartreuse green leaves and bright red flowers that are highly attractive to butterflies and hummingbirds
species.maintenance: Pineapple sage is a drought resistant plant. When you first plant your sage plant, you’ll want to water a few times a week. After a few weeks, you can taper off watering. Observe your plant – if it begins to wilt or its leaves start to curl, increasing the amount of water provided each week. Avoid overwatering your pineapple sage once established.

species.description: Indigo Spires is a garden classic that grows up to 1.3 meters with a sprawling habit. The leaves are dark green, ovate with a medium texture and they are approximately 7.5 cm long. The plant can become very heavy under its own weight and the branches may arch as they strain with the long blooming period. The flowers are a delightful blue-violet colour, with deeper purple calyces. The long inflorescences may reach 30 cm or more above the foliage. Each carries whorls of flowers, with individual flowers measuring up to 1.3 cm.
species.maintenance: It is a sprawling plant and has been described as growing and growing until it falls over under its own weight. Support from stakes and other garden plants may help in this regard. If you would like to have a tidier plant and prevent the branches from falling over, then prune constantly as you go about your regular gardening. However, cutting the plant back to ground level in late winter will work well to encourage the new spring growth.

species.description: Small leaved shrubby perennial sage with aromatic foliage and small red blooms with prominent lower petals in Spring and again in Autumn.
species.maintenance: Clip over after flowering to encourage fresh growth and more flowers. Cut it hard back in Summer

species.blurb: Deep violet-blue spikes, the strongest colour note in the planting.
Dense violet spikes early in the season — cut it back after flowering and it comes again.
species.description: This perennial stands out with its rich, velvety violet-blue flowers that bloom from spring through autumn offering a long season of vibrant color. The aromatic, dark green foliage provides a lush backdrop, enhancing the plant’s refined and elegant appearance. Growing to about 70 cm tall with a spread of 60 cm, it fits beautifully into borders, containers, and mixed garden beds. The flowers attract a variety of pollinators, including bees and butterflies, supporting biodiversity in the garden. This plant’s upright habit and sturdy stems make it a reliable performer that holds its blooms well, even in windy conditions. Its combination of striking color, texture, and resilience adds charm and structure to sunny garden spots, creating a welcoming and lively atmosphere. Perfect for adding a sophisticated splash of colour, it complements both modern and traditional garden designs.
species.maintenance: Key maintenance includes deadheading spent flower spikes to encourage reblooming, cutting back by half to a mound after flowering to refresh foliage, and shearing to the ground in late winter or early spring.

species.description: Noted for its compact form, long lasting blooming season , purple stems and rich, violet-purple flowers against pink bracts appearing in early Summer and lasting throughout the Summer.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance, remove spent flowers spikes to promote further blooms.

species.description:
Sage (Salvia officinalis) is a sensational herb renowned for its healing and antiseptic properties that has many uses. You’ll find it in toiletries such as perfumes, soap and even pot pourri. In cooking it is a lovely addition to stuffing for chicken and meats as well as in egg and vegetable dishes.
Sage is a hardy perennial with greyish leaves and unusual square stems (a characteristic of all salvias). Flowers are usually lilac or purple but can be also pink or white.  Plant it on the edge of your veggie patch to help attract bees or simply use it to jazz up a hot, dry spot in the garden.
species.maintenance: Sage will grow in very poor soils but improving the soil with compost and manure beforehand will enhance its growth. Boost calcium levels by applying dolomite or lime to mimic Mediterranean soil conditions. Pick individual leaves throughout the growing season as you need them.  These can be used fresh or allowed to dry and stored for later use.

species.description: Beautiful evergreen shrub with strongly aromatic, needle like leaves and clusters of pale blue to white whites that appear in Winter and Spring. Rosemary has been traditionally associated with Remembrance, fidelity and friendship and is known for its medicinal properties particularly in treating digestive issues, respiratory ailments and memory loss.
species.maintenance: Pruning helps maintain a bushier plant. Do not take more than 1/3 of the plant and make cuts just above a leaf joint. Thoroughly water but let plant dry out in-between. Cuttings can be dried upside down in bunches.

species.description: Salvia sinaloensis is a low growing plant with a prostrate habit, reaching about 30cm high with a 60cm spread. The spear, or lance shaped leaves are pointed at both ends. They are an attractive deep green with purple tones throughout when the plant is grown in the sun. The 2 cm electric blue flowers are held on an upright stalk extending about 10cm above the leaves. The flowers have been descried as being a true blue and the bluest of all salvias. The rich, bright blue flower has white spots or lines on the lower lip of the flower. The stems and calyces are both hairy and are a lovely deep purple, wine colour that looks almost black. They provide an elegant contrast to the blue flowers which bloom from summer to autumn. The wine coloured calyces stay on the plant after the flower petals fall off.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance

species.blurb: Soft white and pale lilac spires, the gentlest of the four salvias and the longest flowering.
species.description: The origins of ‘Waverly’ are unknown but it is thought to be a hybrid.  This salvia is worth being in every garden.     It is a very useful salvia as it stays around a metre in height.  Foliage is dark green and the flowers pale mauve.   It flowers most of the year but could vary depending on when it was pruned.  If grown in the shade the flowers will be a lot paler.   The flowers can be pale in hot weather and darkest in winter…
species.maintenance: Apply a slow release fertiliser in spring. Prune by half after main flowering period to tidy and again in early spring to remove old stems revealing new growth.

species.description: As well as forming part of the edible garden, it can also be used as a feature plant in the garden. It grows 3 - 4m high. The dark green, compound leaves are pinnate or bipinnate with leaflets arranged oppositely around the stem, creating an overall length of up to 30 cm or more. Each leaflet has serrate edges, is quite large and may measure 3-12cm long by 2-6cm wide. The fragrant white flowers are large and bloom in inflorescences or clusters, about 30 cm in width. These are followed by the blue berry like fruits, but the plant may have both flowers and fruit for several weeks.
species.maintenance: No maintenance

species.description: Sansevieria trifasciata (now correctly Dracaena trifasciata), Mother-in-Law's Tongue, is a rhizomatous succulent perennial from tropical West Africa. Forms tight upright clumps of stiff, sword-shaped leaves to around 60cm–1m, dark green with paler grey-green horizontal banding and, in some forms, a yellow margin. Exceptionally tough and architectural — the strong vertical line makes it a useful counterpoint to mounding and strappy foliage. Frost-tender and intolerant of wet feet. Toxic if ingested.
species.maintenance: Very low maintenance. Water sparingly and allow the soil to dry fully between waterings — rot from overwatering is the only real way to kill it. Requires free-draining mix. Frost-tender; keep under cover or in a warm sheltered position. Divide congested clumps to propagate.

species.description: Santolina ‘Cotton Lavender’ is an extremely hardy shrub, which once established requires very little water and trimming. To maintain a dense shrub, trim after flowering to shape. The beautiful silver / grey foliage covered with bright yellow button flowers will be a vibrant addition to any garden as a hedge or specimen plant.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance. Once established required very little water or trimming.

species.blurb: Deep maroon pincushions, almost black at dusk — the darkest note in the garden.

species.description: Scabiosa atropurpurea 'Black Knight' has fully double, pin cushion flower heads which are as near to black as can be. They make good cut flowers and will no doubt cause interest because of their haunting colour. Scabiosa atropurpurea 'Black Knight' is an excellent filler for the mixed border, flowering in summer. Scabiosa ‘Black Knight’ is known for attracting bees, beneficial insects, birds, butterflies/moths and other pollinators. It has nectar/pollen rich flowers and has seeds for birds. Whilst the species is perennial it is best treated as an annual to obtain the best display. Self sows readily.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance. Cut back faded flower stems in autumn to maintain plant health, or prune in late spring for a bushier habit.

species.description: Vibrant flowering native ground cover, plant in a sunny spot to enjoy the abundant small purple-blue flowers. Lovely in a hanging basket where it will trail over the sides, or mass plant around shrubs for a natural wildflower look. This is a lovely blue ground cover. It flowers during late autumn, spring and summer. It has wedge shaped foliage. Lots of flowers between spring and summer. It loves hot sunny positions.
species.maintenance: Mulch and water regularly and gently until the plant is established, usually around 12 weeks. Prune as required to maintain tidy growth. Tolerates dry conditions.

species.description: Scaevola albida is a fast-growing Australian native perennial ground cover. Endemic to eastern Australia, it is highly valued for its dense, mat-forming green foliage and profuse show of fan-shaped white, mauve, or pale blue flowers.
species.maintenance: Give the plant a light haircut after a major flush of flowers. This keeps the foliage tight and bushy while encouraging another round of fresh blooms.

species.description: Vibrant flowering native ground cover, plant in a sunny spot to enjoy the abundant small purple-blue flowers. Lovely in a hanging basket where it will trail over the sides, or mass plant around shrubs for a natural wildflower look.
species.maintenance: Mulch and water regularly until the plant is established, usually around 12 weeks. Prune as required to maintain tidy growth. Tolerates dry conditions.

species.height_raw: 2–3m h x 1.5m w (can be kept smaller)
species.description: Glossy radiating leaflets in umbrella-like whorls. Layered, lush mid-storey for shade; prune to shape. Best in a sheltered spot.

A fantastic grass for Autumn colour as its name implies, the colours in Autumn range from pink, bronze, rusty red and orange. The Summer foliage is a complete contrast of grey-green. Upright inflorescence stay standing above the foliage for months and contain lovely fluffy seed heads. 'Blaze' adapts to difficult conditions, poor soils and drought. As long as the soil doesn't become too wet
species.maintenance: Cut the foliage back to roughly 3–4 inches above the ground in late winter or early spring (before new green growth appears) to refresh the plant and maintain its upright, clumping form.
A little slow release low phosphorous native plant fertiliser in Spring. Nom pruning generally required. Fungal diseases can appear in humidity, provide good air flow to avoid.

species.description: Scutellaria humilis, commonly known as dwarf skullcap or Australian skullcap, is a slender, spreading, perennial herb native to Eastern Australia. It is part of the mint family (Lamiaceae) and is popular as a low-growing groundcover in gardens.
species.maintenance: No Maintenance

species.description: Skullcap is a perennial herb which is native to North America. It grows to about 80cm in height and spreads by running roots. It has many erect branches with opposite pairs of oblong leave sand lots of small blue flowers on the upper parts of the stems. Medicinally, Skullcap was traditionally used as a nerve tonic and sedative. Today it is used mainly for nervous conditions including insomnia, tension headaches and nervous exhaustion.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance. Skullcap dies back completely in Winter before re-sprouting again in Spring. Harvest in Autumn and dry for later use.

species.description: Sedum 'Autumn Joy' is a clump-forming succulent perennial that typically grows to a height of 1 to 2 feet (30 to 60 cm) and spreads up to 2 feet (60 cm) in Melbourne. It features fleshy, gray-green leaves that are thick and succulent in texture. The foliage forms a mound-like habit, providing a lovely backdrop for the plant's main attraction—the flower heads. In late summer to early fall, 'Autumn Joy' produces large, flat clusters of tiny flowers that start off pink and gradually mature to a coppery or rusty red color, adding a burst of vibrant color to the garden.
species.maintenance:
1. Pruning: In late winter or early spring, before new growth emerges, trim back the old flower heads and any damaged or leggy stems. This helps promote a tidy appearance and encourages strong, compact growth.
2. Watering: Once established, 'Autumn Joy' is quite drought-tolerant and only requires occasional watering during prolonged dry periods. Avoid overwatering, as Sedums are susceptible to root rot in waterlogged soil.
3. Division: Over time, 'Autumn Joy' may develop a dense clump. To maintain its vigor and prevent overcrowding, divide the plant every few years in spring or early summer.

species.description: Sempervivum, meaning "always alive," forms dense mats of rosettes in a breathtaking array of colors, from lush greens and fiery reds to mysterious, almost-black hues. Low-Maintenance Marvels: These succulents thrive in well-draining soil and sunlight, requiring minimal watering and no fertilization once established. Their drought-tolerant nature makes them a perfect fit for water-wise gardens. Sempervivum's compact growth habit makes it an ideal choice for creating vibrant ground cover in sunny, dry areas where other plants struggle. The captivating rosette shapes and colorful variations of Sempervivum make them a favorite for container gardening, adding a touch of whimsy and texture to pots, planters, and unique arrangements.
species.maintenance: Very low maintenance.

species.description: Senecio cineraria 'Silver Dust' is a tender shrub, usually grown as a half-hardy annual foliage plant. Its young leaves are slightly lobed, a bit like oak leaves, but as the plants mature they become deeply cut, much paler in colour and are covered in a silvery grey fleece. It's perfect for growing at the front of a border, and also as part of a container display. It works particularly well with bold-coloured plants, with which its foliage contrasts well.
species.maintenance: Water regularly until established, then avoid drying out. Mulch well.

species.description:
Senecio minimus, commonly known as Shrubby Fireweed, is a short-lived annual or perennial herb native to southeastern Australia and New Zealand. It's a weedy species found in disturbed areas, forest margins,pen_spark and along tracks.
[ Opens in a new window commons.wikimedia.org](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Senecio_minimus_(Shrubby_Fireweed)_(24368197034).jpg) Senecio minimus Shrubby Fireweed 
Here are some key characteristics of Senecio minimus:
• Habit: Erect to spreading aromatic annual herb, sometimes branching at the base.
• Leaves:  Alternate, elliptic to lance-shaped, 6-25 cm long and 1-4 cm wide, with toothed margins and clasping stems.
• Flowers:  Small, rayless, yellow flowerheads in large terminal clusters.
• Flowering: Flowers throughout the year, with peak blooms in spring and summer.
Senecio minimus is a fast-growing plant that can form dense thickets. It's considered a environmental weed in some areas due to its ability to displace native vegetation. However, it can also provide habitat for small animals and insects.

Succulent blue chalksticks is a quietly creeping plant that will hug the ground at the front of a border or on a sunny slope. Easy to grow and well-behaved in a sunny, warm spot, its evergreen blue-gray foliage will be an attractive complement to salvias and other purple perennials.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance fertilise annually but lightly. Remove dead leaves and foliage. Can be pruned back to where the stem is firm. Can be affected by mealybugs. Treat with neem oil.

species.description: Persicaria decipiens is a trailing plant whose stems grow horizontally at first but become more vertical with time, reaching 30 cm (1 ft) high. Its narrow elliptic to lanceolate (spear-shaped) leaves are 5–12 cm (2–4.5 in) long and 0.5–1.3 cm (0.20–0.51 in) across.

Solanum aviculare, commonly known as the Kangaroo Apple or Poroporo, is a fast-growing, soft-wooded shrub native to Australia, New Zealand, and New Guinea. It is notable for its use as a food source in traditional Indigenous culture, its application in modern medicine and cosmetics, and the caution required regarding its fruit. It is a widespread pioneer species, often found on coastal rainforest margins and in disturbed or cleared areas. It is a hardy plant that grows well in well-drained soils and can tolerate a range of conditions from full sun to partial shade. It is relatively short-lived in cultivation, typically lasting a few years, but self-seeds readily.
species.maintenance: Prune for dense habit

species.description: Such a tiny plant, so many nicknames! Usually called baby's tears for the size of the leaf, you may also know it as angel's tears, friendship plant, Corsican creeper, bread and cheese, Paddy's wig, or mind your own business! It loves damp shade, and will even grow in swamps and bogs. It's often planted as an ornamental ground cover - but be warned! If it likes you, it will spread.
species.maintenance: Key maintenance includes keeping soil consistently moist, providing high humidity, pruning regularly to manage spread, and avoiding direct sunlight and frost.

species.description: An attractive screening or specimen plant for sheltered positions with white flowers and whitish new growth that brightens a garden in winter. The flowers form tight flat clusters of tiny honey-scented flowers at the ends of branches, surrounded by hairy white floral leaves.  it covers the ground like a small cloud. But there’s nothing airy-fairy about this tough little plant, despite its delicate looks. Whether used in a cottage garden, as a container specimen, along path edges or lapping up against rock work, It offers a soft restful foil in bolder brightly hued plantings. Suited to cool temperate, sub-tropical and arid climates in open gravelly clay or loam soils, low alkaline to low acid pH. Tolerates moderate frosts and exposed coastal conditions.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance with a light trim once or twice a year,.

species.blurb: Soft silver leaves you want to touch — already growing here, and lifted and replanted into the new scheme.
species.description: Lamb's Ears is known for its soft, fuzzy leaves that resemble the ears of a lamb, hence the common name. The plant forms a dense, low-growing mound of foliage, with each leaf reaching a length of 2 to 4 inches (5 to 10 cm). The leaves are densely covered with silver-gray hairs, giving them a velvety texture and a silvery appearance. The overall growth habit of Stachys byzantina is clump-forming, spreading slowly through its underground rhizomes.
species.maintenance:
1. Pruning: Lamb's Ears generally require minimal pruning. However, you can trim back any spent flower spikes or damaged foliage to maintain a neat appearance.
2. Watering: Once established, Lamb's Ears are quite drought-tolerant and prefer well-draining soil. Watering is typically only necessary during dry spells or prolonged periods without rain.
3. Division: Over time, the clumps of Lamb's Ears may become crowded. To rejuvenate the plant and maintain its vigor, divide the clumps every few years in spring or fall.

species.description: The most spectacular of grasses that won't take over the garden. A tidy clump of fine dark leaves support 2m stems topped by fat glossy seed heads that start silver then age to copper-gold. Truly magnificent. Can be slow to get going but it is worth a bit of patience as you wait for it to mature. Best in well drained, sunny sites, this stunning grass will provide drama and movement when it produces its tall flower stalks and oat like flowers that persist well into late winter.
species.maintenance: Cut back spent flower stems in late winter and tidy foliage clumps by removing any dried or damaged leaves.

species.blurb: Fine hair-like foliage that moves with the slightest breeze and bleaches to pale straw.
species.description: Stipa tenuissima, widely known as Mexican Feather Grass, is a popular ornamental grass prized for its ethereal, wispy appearance and graceful movement in the breeze. While still commonly referred to by its older scientific name, it is now officially classified as Nassella tenuissima.
species.maintenance: You can either comb through the clumps with gloved hands in spring to remove dead blades or cut the entire plant back to about 5–10 cm above the ground in late winter/early spring.

species.description: An evergreen tropical with round palm-like leaves with brightly-coloured flowers that bloom to look like tropical birds.
species.maintenance: Feed from spring to summer and water when plant is 50% dry. Do not overwater. Can be divided every 5 years.

species.description: Strobilanthes gossypinus is a striking evergreen shrub from the dry hill regions of southern India, prized for its soft, silvery, woolly foliage — each leaf is covered in dense felt-like hairs that give the plant a luminous metallic-silver appearance. Forms an upright, branching shrub to around 1–1.5m, producing clusters of small blue-purple flowers in winter and spring. The almost otherworldly silver texture pairs beautifully with deeper-toned foliage in dry-style and contemporary gardens. Drought-tolerant once established and well-suited to Mediterranean and warm-temperate climates.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance. Allow soil to dry between waterings — does not like wet feet. Tip-prune to maintain shape and encourage branching. Frost-tender; protect from heavy frost or grow in a sheltered position. Replace every few years if plants become leggy with age.

species.description: With an unusual method of ensuring pollination, Stylidium armeria earns itself the common name of Trigger Plant. The flower itself has a ‘Trigger’, when the pollinating insect touches the trigger, it springs forward and touches the insect. This both releases that plants pollen and removes pollen from other Trigger Plants. Over time the underground rhizomes will spread to form a small clump. In the garden this is a great plant for growing in a rock garden situation, in containers or in the general garden border. The pink flowers appear on tall stems above the grasslike foliage, with numerous flowers on each stem opening sequentially form the bottom upwards.
species.maintenance: Once established requires very little water. No maintenance

species.description: Swamp Crassula (Crassula helmsii) is a native Australian aquatic or semi-aquatic perennial herb. It is known for its ability to grow both submerged in water (up to 3m deep) and on damp ground, forming dense, mat-like cover. It is locally common in its native range and is valued in gardens as a fast-growing plant for suppressing weeds at the edges of ponds, and for providing habitat for frogs and other aquatic invertebrates.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance.

species.description: As a perennial, Greek mountain tea grows flat-topped and can reach a height of between 30 and 50cm. Greek mountain tea stems produce elliptical leaves that are grey-green and covered with a grey felt. During its flowering period from June to August, Greek mountain tea produces pale yellow, lip-shaped flowers that are grouped together in long spikes. The inflorescences of Sideritis scardica emit a lemony fragrance and serve as a rich source of nectar for many beneficial insects. After flowering, many small clover fruits containing seeds form.
species.maintenance: As a robust mountain herb, Greek mountain tea requires little care. Water sparingly and avoid waterlogging. You may need to water slightly more during especially dry spells. In addition, mountain tea appreciates an annual repotting. To ensure the plant takes root again, this should be done in spring, preferably in March. Carefully dig up the roots with a garden fork and place them in a larger pot with well-drained, nutrient-poor soil. As Greek mountain tea plants prefer poorer soils, there is no need for fertilising. This hardy herb appreciates being cut back in autumn, after the flowering period. To prune your Greek mountain tea, cut the plant down to the base of the stem. This will encourage it to sprout again vigorously the following spring. However, in especially harsh, frosty regions, it is better to leave the dead leaves and stem on the plant over the winter. Then, cut it back in spring before the new shoots appear.

species.description: It may come as a surprise to some that the plentiful reddish-pink to white berry like fruit of this widely used hedging plan is also one of Australia’s most potent superfoods.
species.maintenance: Water for around 3 months until established. In Spring use slow-release fertilizer. Prune twice yearly. Mulch with chunky mulch.

species.description: Aniseed Myrtle (Syzygium anisatum) is a native Australian rainforest tree with highly aromatic, glossy leaves that taste and smell strongly of aniseed/licorice, offering a sweet, cooling flavor used as a potent bush spice. Traditionally used by Aboriginal peoples as a tonic, its leaves are used fresh, dried, or powdered in teas, baking, marinades, and desserts, providing a strong, sweet anise flavor comparable to star anise but more intense. It's an ornamental shrub/tree that thrives in well-drained soil and is cultivated for both its culinary and fragrant properties.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance.

species.description: This small, bushy herb has small yellow and white daisy-like flowers that are produced over most of the year. The plant is a herbaceous perennial that grows into a small bush up to 70 cm high, with pungently scented leaves. The leaves are light yellowish green, variously pinnatifid. The conspicuous daisy-like flowers are up to 20 millimetres across, borne in lax corymbs. The outer, ray florets have white ligules and the inner, disc florets are yellow and tubular. It spreads rapidly by seed, and will cover a wide area after a few years The plant produces achene fruit, and grows in stony slopes and river beds
species.maintenance: Maintain even moisture. Apply balanced fertiliser in Spring.

species.description: A handsome large shrub to small tree, native to Tasmania, and a great bushfood plant. It has cream to pale yellow flowers in summer followed by the peppery berries which ripen in autumn and are very good for flavouring for savoury dishes and drinks. The berries have sweet fruity notes as well as the distinctive pepper flavour. The leaves can also be used, and both berries and leaves have good antimicrobial properties. Grows best in acidic, moist and well-drained soils. Likes partly shaded sheltered spots as it dislikes hot sun, It has separate male and female plants, so both of these will need to be grown to get the berries. It has leathery green leaves, younger stems are an attractive red. It can be pruned to form a dense bush.
species.maintenance: Organic fertiliser and Spring Mulch

species.description:
A large lobed leafy shrub that can grow to 4m.  Palmate leaves divided into lobes add interest and texture. Leaves are glossy green and flowers are small and white. With wonderful large leaves to nearly 50 cms across Tetrapanax papyrifer is commonly called the ‘Rice Paper Plant’. 
A great foliage plant with large palmate (divided into lobes) leaves add texture and interest to the garden. This is also a tall growing plant, quickly reaching over 2m in height, as such it can be grown at the back of the border to add a little height.
Tetrapanax is a suckering shrub with unbranched canes or stems, the leaves are a glossy green, flowers are small and white Tetrapanax prefer a well drained humus rich soil. Tetrapanax can be used to give the garden a tropical look.
species.maintenance: Very low care once established. Can be pruned back to the ground to contain size.

species.description: This is a delightful small shrub that provides a brilliant Spring display with its pendulous black-centred bell-shaped blooms. It forms a multi-stemmed plant that is surprisingly tough when grown in a well drained sunny or lightly shaded position in the garden. Give it a light trim and a feed after flowering. It makes an outstanding pot plant as well.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance

species.blurb: A silver-leaved shrub with small blue flowers — one of the plants that keeps the darker colours lifted.
species.description: Bush Germander is a compact, dense shrub that typically grows to a height and width of 3 to 6 feet (90 to 180 cm). It has an upright growth habit with woody stems covered in grayish-green, aromatic foliage. The leaves are small, narrow, and slightly serrated, giving them a delicate and textured appearance. The silvery-gray foliage provides an attractive contrast in the landscape and adds a touch of elegance to gardens. In late spring or early summer, clusters of small, tubular, lavender-blue flowers bloom along the stems, creating a profusion of color.
species.maintenance:
1. Watering: Once established, Bush Germander is drought-tolerant and requires minimal watering. It is important to provide regular watering during the establishment phase.
2. Pruning: Prune Bush Germander after flowering to maintain its shape and encourage bushier growth. Light pruning throughout the year can help control its size and promote a compact form.
3. Fertilization: In most cases, Bush Germander doesn't require regular fertilization. However, if the plant appears weak or lacks vigor, a balanced fertilizer can be applied in early spring.

species.description: Bold, deeply lobed glossy leaves on a sprawling trunk. Big tropical leaf for sheltered shade; give it room. Light frost tolerance once established.

species.botanical_name: The Weather Thistle: Nature's Living Barometer - Laidback Gardener

species.description:
Themeda triandra (formerly Themeda australis), commonly known as Kangaroo Grass, is a medium sized tufted native grass with green foliage which turns reddish brown to purplish in winter. Kangaroo Grass can be used as an informal native lawn or is ideal for softening hard surfaces such as paving and garden structures and buildings.  Kangaroo grass grows in soils of low to moderately high pH. You will find Kangaroo grass in almost all parts of Australia this is because it is one of the most widely distributed grassland and woodland species. It is a warm season grass that has its main growth in summer and is generally dormant in winter. A great adaption of this grass is its fire tolerant and responds well to regular burning and spelling. It responds quickly to the first rain of the season growing an upright green leaf from the crown of the plant.
Kangaroo grass is known for its deep root systems and its striking seed head that forms during summer. It is widely associated with revegetation due to its high persistence over many years. It is ideally suited to growth on poor and exposed soils, low fertility and rainfall sites and for situations where low maintenance is required. This grass makes a wonderful landscaping plant if allowed to grow to its full size. It also produces a large bulk of dry matter and makes excellent fodder for grazing.
species.maintenance: Trim annually to remove any untidy older leaves

species.description: Themeda triandra 'True Blue' (commonly known as Kangaroo Grass) is a highly ornamental, Australian native perennial tussock grass prized for its striking blue-grey foliage. Kangaroo Grass can be used as an informal native lawn or is ideal for softening hard surfaces such as paving and garden structures and buildings. Kangaroo grass grows in soils of low to moderately high pH. You will find Kangaroo grass in almost all parts of Australia this is because it is one of the most widely distributed grassland and woodland species. It is a warm season grass that has its main growth in summer and is generally dormant in winter. A great adaption of this grass is its fire tolerant and responds well to regular burning and spelling.
species.maintenance: Trim annually to remove any untidy older leaves

species.description: Masses of tiny pink flowers over a very long period and a compact low growing shrubby habit define this very useful Australian shrub. It is useful as background shrub or even as a low growing hedge plant that is very tough and adaptable but needs relatively good drainage. It can be pruned by occasionally trimming off branches to use as cut flowers, or else give it a light trim coming out of winter. The foliage is spicily fragrant.
species.maintenance: Low Maintenance

species.description: Creeping thymes are a specific species of thyme (Thymus serpyllum) with many cultivars, all sharing the same trailing habit. They, like all thymes, are part of the mint (Lamiaceae family) and have similarly powerful essential oils. Creeping thyme grows well in Australia and requires very little ongoing care, other than a trim once a year, and a little water to help see it through extreme drought. Creeping thyme is a perennial herb, so returns every year, though may lose some of its flowering vigour after about five years. One of the most intriguing modern uses of creeping thyme is as a lawn substitute. Creeping thyme helps to support native bees thanks to its prolific nectar-rich flowers, and its ability to withstand light foot traffic.
species.maintenance: Very low maintenance once established. In the first year water generously but do not soak. Prune back hard once a year to promote growth.

species.description:
Lemon Thyme (Thymus citriodorus) is a fragrant herb that combines the earthy flavor of thyme with a distinct lemony aroma and taste. It's a versatile herb that can be used in culinary, medicinal, and ornamental applications. Here's some information about Lemon Thyme, including its description, maintenance, growing conditions, culinary and medicinal uses, and notable characteristics:
Description:
• Lemon Thyme is a low-growing, herbaceous perennial that typically reaches a height of about 6 to 12 inches (15 to 30 cm).
• The leaves of Lemon Thyme are small, green, and oval-shaped, with a glossy appearance.
• What sets Lemon Thyme apart is its strong lemon scent and flavor, which is released when you crush or bruise the leaves. It provides a delightful citrusy twist to traditional thyme.
species.maintenance:
1. Watering: Lemon Thyme prefers well-drained soil and should be watered consistently to keep the soil evenly moist, especially during dry spells.
2. Pruning: Regular pruning helps to maintain a compact and bushy growth habit. You can also pinch off the tips to encourage branching.
3. Fertilization: Lemon Thyme doesn't require heavy fertilization. A light application of a balanced, all-purpose fertilizer in the spring is usually sufficient.

species.description: Woolly Thyme is one of the hardier herbs perfect for hot, sunny locations. Once established, it tolerates dry conditions and spreads slowly, eventually creating a thick mat of foliage. Tiny leaves on woolly thyme ground cover are green and often edged with gray to silver. In summer the plant adds a bonus and produces sweet little pink to purple flowers. The plants are low growing, rarely getting higher than 30.5 cm. and spreading out to 45.5 cm. in width. Woolly thyme plants are perennial. Little is needed from the gardener with woolly thyme care.
species.maintenance: Minimal care required. A light fertilize only if necessary. Cut back in Spring.

species.description: Thymus vulgaris (Thyme) is a dwarf, aromatic shrub primarily grown as a culinary herb in herb gardens. It forms a low cushion of branching, woody stems clothed with small, linear to ovate, dark grey-green leaves. The leaves are highly aromatic and are frequently used fresh or dried as a seasoning in a variety of culinary applications, including soups, sauces, vegetables, meats and fish dishes. Rich in nectar they attract butteries and bees. Great as a low edging for flower, vegetable and herb gardens. Excellent as a container plants. Evergreen in mild Winters.
species.maintenance: Cut back in Spring to limit woody growth or to stimulate new growth. Virtually pest and disease free.

species.description: A hardy, evergreen vine that can cover large areas with green glossy leaves and very fragrant flowers that bloom in Spring and Summer.
species.maintenance: Mulch and water regularly until established. Can be pruned to maintain a tidy look or can become invasive. Moderate drought tolerant when established. Fertilise one a year with all-purpose fertiliser in Spring.

species.description: An evergreen groundcover with small glossy dark green leaves. The Asiatic Jasmine bears a profusion of highly scented cream flowers during Summer and is quite a hardy plant.
species.maintenance: Grow in well-drained soil with protection from cold, drying winds. If growing indoors, plant in loam-based potting compost in full light but not direct sun. Water freely and apply a balanced liquid fertiliser during the growing season, and water sparingly

Water regularly and feed during the growing season. Tie young shoots until established. Can develop root rot in constant damp conditions. In spring tie stray shoots in the direction of growth. Can be pruned after flowering hard or light depending on desired look.

species.description: A deciduous tree that displays autumn colour. Green heart shaped leaves change in autumn to shades of crimson, yellow and orange. Fast growing small to medium tree around 8m X 8m
species.maintenance: Water well until established. Tree reseeds easily so care from spreading into Neighbours patch.

species.description: Triglochin procerum s.l. Robust plant with thick rhizomes ending in numerous tubers. Green, fleshy ribbon-like, erect or floating leaves, 0.1-2 m long and 0.5-4 cm wide. Sixty to two hundred small greenish flowers held in a dense flower spike, up to 350 cm long and 2 cm wide.

Handsome and easy going, Tropaeolum majus (Nasturtium) is a popular annual or short lived perennual with creeping or sprawling stems that command attention in any landsacpe. Blooming from Winter through Spring in mild Winter areas and from Summer to Autum in colder climates, Nasturtium boasts a profusion of long stalked funnel-shaped flowers ranging in colour from creamy white to orange to mahogany, red and yellow. The blossoms may be single or double and have an unusual and refreshing fragrance. Nasturtiums rank amongst the most common edible flowers. The delicate blossoms have a sweet, peppery taste similar to watercress. Leaves and unripe seed pods add a citrusy and peppery flavour to salads. Flower buds contain mustard oil and may be used for seasonings. The flowers add eye catching beauty to the plate and can be used to garnish salads, platters and savoury dishes.
species.maintenance: Deadhead to prolong flowering. Water regularly throughout the growing season. No serious pests or disease issues.

species.description: Tulbaghia violacea, also known as Society Garlic, has sweetly fragrant lilac-pink flowers that elegantly rise above a foliage clump of narrow, strap-shaped, grey-green leaves. The flowers are dainty and tubular in appearance, spreading to an open star with six-pointed petals. This plant will bloom on and off all through summer and into autumn. The flowers emit a fragrance resembling a hyacinth; the leaves and rhizomes, however, have a strong garlic smell. Tulbaghia violacea is excellent for garden beds and borders, edging, herb gardens, and pots.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance. Deadheading of flowers after flowering.

species.description: Tulips are a genus of spring-blooming perennial herbaceous bulbiferous geophytes. The flowers are usually large, showy and brightly coloured, generally red, pink, yellow, or white.
species.maintenance: Relatively maintenance free

species.description: A small shrub between 30 - 50cm high with small yellow flowers and small narrow leaves with serrated edges. Native to mexico Damiana likes a well drained sunny position and is happy in a rocky garden. It is an aromatic plant and was popular with the Mayans as an aphrodisiac.
species.maintenance: Keep soil moist but not waterlogged. Remove spent flowers and prune occasionally

species.description: A medium size deciduous tree which has a vase shape when young but develops a rounded can0py as it matures. Fast growing and wide spreading. It has golden foliage which turns yellow in autumn before falling.
species.maintenance: Adequate moisture is essential for growth. It has medium frost tolerance. It is susceptible to Dutch Elm Disease.

species.description: "Uncinia Belinda's Find," also known as Red Hook Sedge, is a clumping, evergreen ornamental grass known for its vibrant foliage. The plant features glossy, dark leaves with a bronze tone and bright red edges. Belinda's Find has striking, strappy foliage with a rich cherry red and bronze color palette, making it a popular choice for adding visual interest to garden
species.maintenance: It's a relatively low-maintenance plant, and occasional removal of dead or damaged foliage is sufficient.

species.description: This low chill compact southern highbush variety of blueberry produces a heavy crop of mid-sized summer fruit in almost any climate. Self pollinating.
species.maintenance: Pick and Eat. Apply a complete fertiliser in spring. Mulch with pine needles.

species.description: Widespread throughout much of Victoria, mostly in the lowlands. An erect herb to 1 m. Leaves linear to ovate up to 4 cm long and 7 mm wide and variously toothed. White or purplish-pink flowers to 13 mm long.

species.blurb: Small violet flowers on tall, see-through stems — you look through it rather than at it.
species.description: *Verbena bonariensis* attracts hoverflies, bees, and butterflies like a magnet — especially Monarchs and Painted Ladies.Despite its delicate look, it's tough, drought-tolerant, and self-seeds easily.Its stiff, see-through stems let you plant it at the front of a bed without blocking views — a designer’s secret weapon!
species.maintenance: Low maintenance. Drought tolerant. Deadhead to encourage blooms. Mulch annually.

species.description: An upright, perennial shrub prized for its attractive foliage and striking purple-blue flowers that bloom through summer. The soft, blue-green leaves grow in perfoliate pairs, hugging the slender stems, and long nodding spikes of star-shaped purple flowers stand above the foliage creating a striking feature. Each spike can carry up to 25-70 flowers.
species.maintenance: Low Maintenance. Can be rejuvenated by pruning to almost ground level. Fairly pest and disease-free.

species.description: Veronicastrum virginicum album looks amazing planted as a drift in a perennial border. It is the white flowered form with a very tiny touch of pink. It flowers for an extended time during summer and early autumn won top of long stems with lance shaped dark green leaves. These plants are drought tolerant once established and also make outstanding cut flowers.
species.maintenance: Remove flower spikes as they fade.

species.description: Fast growing, glossy leaved hedging shrub with large vibrant lime-green glossy leaves. In Spring large clusters of white flowers turn into berries in summer.
species.maintenance: Mulch and water well. Fertilise with slow release fertilizer. Prune twice yearly.

species.description: Growing as a small tree around 6m tall, qdd lush foliage and beautiful blooms to your garden with this fast growing, evergreen shrub. Enjoy glossy green leaves and clusters of fragrant flowers in Spring and early Summer, along with small red berries.
species.maintenance: Mulch, water and fertilise in Spring. Prune twice yearly to promote new growth.

species.description: Mainly grown for its ball shaped flower bunch and the red coloured berries. The plant produces pure white flowers that are sterile, and look like snowballs, flowering from the end of the winter season into the spring. These plants are easy to grow and can become the focal point of your garden when they are in bloom. Once established, the plant is frost tolerant and the blooms last for around 5 weeks before the blooms, fall to the ground petal by petal resembling falling snow. This deciduous shrub grows to a height of 4-5 m. The leaves are broad, and three-lobed and opposite in arrangement and the leaf margins are serrated. The flower clusters start out lime green and mature to white. They flower on the bush profusely. The leaves, which turn to purplish red during the autumn, offer a good spring and autumn display in the garden. Cut stems arranged in a large crystal vase, make wonderful indoor flower arrangements.
species.maintenance: Older growth and dead or damaged wood can be removed to promote a healthy plant. A little slow release fertilizer in early spring seems sufficient, but try to keep a cool root run, use well rotted compost and cow manure as mulch, but keep mulch well away from the base of the trunk.

species.description: Broad beans are an annual plant that belongs to the legume family. They produce large, flat pods that contain edible seeds. Broad beans come in various sizes and colours, ranging from green to brown to black.
species.maintenance: Broad beans are a low-maintenance crop that are easy to grow. They prefer well-draining soil and a position in full sun. Broad beans should be watered regularly, but not excessively, and should be fertilized with a nitrogen-rich fertilizer during the growing season. They can be planted in fall or early spring, depending on the climate.

species.description: Grows as a shrub or small tree reaching heights of up to 6m.  Its slender trunk has dark fibrous bark with a crown of soft green branches. Ordinary leaves are absent instead a mass of growth of phyllodes which are 25mm long, stringy,smooth and flexible. Its smooth trunk and ascending branches often droop. Flowering occurs from September to January, the flowers growing on racemes to about 25 cm in length. Measuring 0.8 cm in diameter, they are yellow with an orange corolla and are typically pea-shaped. They are followed by small pods containing single seeds. This plant grows in fire-prone areas and likely regenerates from seed after fire.
species.maintenance: Regular watering.

species.description: Blue periwinkle, also known as Vinca major, is a trailing, herbaceous perennial ground cover with broad, glossy green leaves and large blue-purple flowers. It spreads rapidly through creeping stems that root at the nodes (joints where leaves attach), forming a dense mat. While it can be attractive in gardens, it's also an invasive species, particularly in moist, shady areas, and can outcompete native plants.
species.maintenance: Blue vinca, also known as periwinkle, is a low-maintenance groundcover. It thrives in well-drained soil and tolerates a range of conditions, including full sun to full shade and drought. Proper watering, occasional pruning, and potentially light fertilizing are the main maintenance needs.

species.blurb: An indigenous groundcover for shade, flowering for most of the year and closing the soil against weeds.
species.description: A pretty ground cover and lawn substitute for shady areas, with round leaves and purple and white flowers held above the foliage.
species.maintenance: Provide plenty of water during the first 12 weeks or until the plant is established and regularly in dry periods. Feed with liquid fertiliser monthly during spring and summer for lush coverage.

species.description: Dainty little groundcover that will bloom in the coldest shadiest places. It is perfect for planting under leafy trees and in gloomy urban gardens, where it will settle in and create a carpet of heart-shaped leaves topped by tiny sapphire spring flowers. Like all Violets, this variety prefers a damp shady positon however will cope with full sun in cooler regions. Violets can can be used in baskets containers or under larger plants as they will form a compact dense ground cover with the right amount of shelter and watering. Likes a well-drained soil in full to part shade and grows better if regularly fertilised.
species.maintenance: Plenty of water in the first 12 weeks and during dry spells.

species.description: The king of autumn colours. In April the thick, dinner plate sized foliage explodes (there’s really no other word for it) into riotous autumnal shades, stopping everyone who visits us in their tracks. A must-have for those chasing autumn colours and the perfect feature climber. Vigorous, deciduous climber about 15m tall, with large, slightly 3-5 lobed, broadly heart-shaped, dark green leaves to 30cm in length, brown felted beneath, turning scarlet and crimson in autumn. Insignificant tiny greenish summer flowers are followed by bunches of small blue-black berries 1cm across
species.maintenance: Heavy winter pruning to control its fast growth, trimming to 2-3 buds, and regular watering in the first few years.

species.description:
Vittadinia cervicularis, commonly known as Annual New Holland Daisy, is a small, annual herb native to southeastern Australia. It's a lovely wildflower with white to purplish daisy flowers and is a popular choice for wildflower gardens.
Here's a closer look at its characteristics:
• Appearance: It's a small, bushy herb growing up to 40 cm tall. The stems and leaves are covered in short hairs. The leaves are narrow and often folded lengthwise. The daisy flowers have purplish to whitish ray florets and a fluffy seedhead in the center.
• Habitat: It grows in pastures, grasslands, dry sclerophyll forests, and Callitris woodlands. It's found in southern parts of Australia, from Western Australia to New South Wales.
• Flowering: It flowers mainly from September to December.

Vittadinia muelleri, commonly known as the Narrow-leaf New Holland daisy, is a small, tufted perennial herb native to Australia. It belongs to the daisy family, Asteraceae, and is a popular groundcover in horticultural settings. This plant typically grows to a height of 10 to 20 cm and a width of 30 to 50 cm. It has narrow, bright green leaves with scattered coarse hairs and develops several stems from a woody rootstock. It produces numerous small, attractive purple or dark blue daisy-like flowers with yellow centres, followed by distinctive fluffy white seed heads when ripe. The flowers are an important nectar and pollen source, attracting native bees, butterflies, and other nectar-foraging insects. The plant also provides a food source for seed-eating birds.
species.maintenance: Due to its hardiness and attractive appearance, Vittadinia muelleri is used as a groundcover in gardening and is suitable for green roofs. It prefers full sun to part shade and can tolerate moderately dry conditions once established. Plants will grow larger and flower more profusely in more fertile soils.

species.description: Voodoo lily, also called Devil's tongue, is a member of the genus Amorphophallus. The voodoo lily, A. titanum, is the largest flower in the world. A. konjac has smaller flowers, but it is still quite large compared to other garden flowers. Each bulb produces one stalk, about 6 feet tall (2 m.), topped by one gigantic leaf. After the leaf stalk withers, the voodoo lily bulb produces a flower stalk. The flower is actually a spathe and spadex arrangement similar to a calla lily. The spadex can be 10 to over 50 inches (25.5 cm. to 1.27 m.) long. The blossom only lasts a day or two.
species.maintenance: Plant lily corm deep beneth the surface as the top-heavy plant can pull free from the soil. Likes the addition of well-rotted organic matter. Does not like too much watering and periods of drying out are recommended, Warm tempretures and high humidity are recommended,

species.description: Wahlenbergia communis, commonly known as Tufted Bluebell, is a native Australian perennial herb belonging to the bellflower family, Campanulaceae. It is valued for its delicate, bell-shaped blue flowers and its ability to attract pollinators. Due to its charming appearance and long flowering season, Tufted Bluebell is an excellent choice for cottage gardens, rockeries, pots, and mass plantings.
species.maintenance: It is a low-maintenance plant that performs well with moderate watering, but it can survive periods of drought.

species.description: The Australian Bluebell belongs to the genus Wahlenbergia, that includes both annuals and perennials. The bluebell genus have a fleshy tap root and sometimes underground stems, whilst the stems above ground are erect, terete, and sometimes branched. The bluebells may be almost hairless to hairy. The leaves are at the base and on the lower stems of the plant. The leaf margins may be toothed, although they are mostly linear, flat or wavy. The flowers are usually pale to blue, bell-shaped with five lobes and are on long leafless stalks. The flowers open around mid-morning and close late in the afternoon. Petals are edible and can be used in salads.
species.maintenance: No Maintenance

species.description: Wahlenbergia stricta, the Tall Bluebell, is a tall, clumping, much branched perennial herb, growing to 40-90cm tall, widespread in plains, grassland, red gum woodland, in wet and damp valleys and dry sclerophyll forests and grassy low open forest. It grows in all states except the Northern Territory. The foliage is hairy, ovate, opposite, lower leaves are 10-70mm long with wavy edges, set at right angles to the stem. Upper leaves are smaller and more linear. The lovely light blue flowers (occasionally all white) have a white throat and are 25mm wide with a conspicuous tube. This species tolerates some dryness. The petals are edible and are most attractive added to a salad or to decorate cakes or baked goods.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance. Tolerates light frost.

species.description: Waterhousea floribunda, commonly known as Weeping Lilly Pilly, is a highly favored Australian native ideal for creating dense screens, effective windbreaks, or as a striking container plant. This fast-growing tree, reaching up to 12 meters, offers lush, dense foliage that not only provides excellent privacy but also contributes to noise reduction, making it perfect for urban gardens. With its low maintenance and adaptability to various soil types, it is well-suited for gardeners looking for lasting visual impact with minimal effort.
species.maintenance: Mulch and water regularly until established at least 12 weeks. Water during dry spells.

species.description: Westringia 'Blue Gem' is a hardy Australian native shrub prized for its long display of soft blue-mauve flowers from spring through autumn, set against fine grey-green foliage. Forms a dense, rounded shrub to around 1–1.5m, making it an ideal choice for coastal gardens, informal hedging, and low-maintenance native plantings. Tolerates wind, salt, drought, and frost once established, and responds well to light pruning to keep its compact shape.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance. Tip-prune lightly throughout the year to maintain shape; tolerates a harder cut every few years to rejuvenate. Drought-hardy and frost-tolerant once established. Mulch and water in during the first season.

species.description: A small shrub with soft grey-green and white variegated foliage with small white flowers, which are attractive to butterflies and harmless native bees. Attractive as a specimen or flowering container plant; ideal for formal hedging and for mid level screening.  Grows in a wide range of soils, and is well suited to coastal positions, as it is very salt tolerant. Despite their resemblance and acquaintance to rosemary, these shrubs don’t have a strong aroma but are rather used for their ornamental and functional purposes.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance

species.description: Westringia 'Grey Box' is an award-winning, ultra-compact Australian native shrub. Widely celebrated as the best native alternative to traditional English Box hedging, it requires minimal water and maintenance while keeping a tidy, dense shape. It has triking silver-grey, tight-knit narrow leaves that offer excellent colour contrast against deeper green garden plants. Small, white star-like flowers bloom heavily from September through to May, attracting bees and beneficial insects.
species.maintenance: Needs very little maintenance. To maintain a crisp, formal hedge look, trim lightly 1–3 times a year after a flowering flush. For a natural look, it can be left unpruned for several years without losing its shape. Extremely hardy. It is highly drought-tolerant, frost-hardy, and easily withstands harsh coastal winds and salt spray.

species.description: A small shrub with soft grey-green and white variegated foliage with small white flowers, which are attractive to butterflies and harmless native bees. Attractive as a specimen or flowering container plant; ideal for formal hedging and for mid level screening.  Grows in a wide range of soils, and is well suited to coastal positions, as it is very salt tolerant.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance. Westringia 'Smokey' is a low-maintenance shrub, ideal for coastal gardens and low-maintenance landscapes. It requires well-drained soil, full sun to part shade, and tolerates drought, wind, and salt spray once established. Regular pruning helps maintain its shape, but overall it's relatively pest and disease-free.

species.description: Westringia hybrid ‘Aussie Box’ is a compact, dense Australian native shrub ideal for low-maintenance hedging, offering a sustainable alternative to European box. Growing 40–95 cm high, it features light green foliage, mauve flowers in spring/summer, and requires minimal pruning compared to other Westringias, featuring high drought/frost tolerance.
species.maintenance: Drought tolerant once established; requires less water than exotic box plants.

species.description: Westringia 'Wynyabbie Gem' is a popular Australian native plant, known for its compact growth habit and beautiful mauve flowers. Very hardy native with pale purple flowers throughout the year. Tolerates dry conditions. Can be used in shrubs rockeries, low maintenance gardens or as a screen plant.
species.maintenance: Prune lightly after flowering to maintain a dense, bushy shape. This plant is drought-tolerant once established, making it a low-maintenance choice.

species.description: A deciduous woody climber it has stunning flowers and a heady perfume. It comes in an array of colours pink, purple and white.
species.maintenance: A light spray of slow-release fertilizer only. Prune in Spring when needed to help train plant.

species.description: Withania somnifera is a small shrub growing up to 1 meter high and 75cm wide. The ovate leaves are about 8cm by 5cm at the widest point, tapering to the end. The central vein is prominent and the sides of the leaf fold in slightly towards the centre. The pale green flowers are held in an olive green calyx which surrounds the berry/fruit when the flower falls away, as the berry ripens the calyx browns and shrivels revealing the red fruit. Both the stem and leaves have a downy, grey sheen produced by a covering of tiny hairs. The fruit is a bright red and the seeds are tiny and brown. Withania is from the Solanaceae or nightshade family and is also known as Indian Ginseng, ashwagandha, poison gooseberry or winter cherry in Australia (not to be confused with Physallis alkekengi). The species name ‘somnifera’ means sleep-inducing in Latin. The alternative name ashwagandha is derived from Sanskrit, in particular ‘ashva’ meaning ‘horse’ and ‘gandha’ meaning ‘smell’. The root of the plant is said to have a strong horse-like smell, resulting in the name. Indian Ginseng is a name derived from Ayurvedic medicine, where the plant holds the same degree of prestige as ginseng does in China. The plant is thought to be native to the drier regions of India and Nepal, with cultivation occurring in India.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance.

species.description: Xanthorrhoea australis, the Austral Grass-tree, is an extremely slow-growing perennial of south-eastern Australian heathlands, heathy woodlands and dry forests. Over many decades it forms a dark, often fire-blackened trunk topped by a dense crown of fine, arching grey-green leaves. Tall cream flower spikes appear in spring, often triggered by fire, and are rich in nectar for birds, bees and other insects. Needs excellent drainage and resents root disturbance and overwatering. A protected plant in Victoria: buy only tagged, legally sourced stock.

The grass tree is an iconic Australian plant, slow growing, long lived and will give character to the landscape. It grows incredibly slowly but you know that saying ‘slow and steady wins the race’? This tree might be a slow grower, but it can live up to 600 years. It has a tuft of grassy leaves atop a dark thick trunk, with cream flowers borne on a tall spear-like spike.
