Native to Western Australia, it will grow on a variety of soils but needs to be well drained. If the soil is on the clay side, it will need to be formed into a raised bed to help prevent root rot. Best in full sun. Water regularly while the plant is establishing, but don’t overwater. Will flower only every few years. Tolerates some frost, and dry periods.
species.maintenance: Very low maintenance. The trees grow well in soil without many nutrients and wildfire is no threat to them.

species.description: A low growing soft-wooded perennial which can be used as an annual in bedding situations and renewed every year. This is a true breeding seed line in colours of crimson and red. A great general garden or pot plant and a brilliant cut flower, attract butterflies and small moths. To preserve the flowers, pick while in bud and hang upside down until dry.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance, Responds to dead heading. General purpose liquid fertiliser every month or so. To use as dried flowers pick while in bud and hang upside down to dry.

species.description: A vigorous evergreen shrub with fleshy greyish green leaves bearing masses of long stemmed gold and bronze everlasting daisy flowers with a bright yellow centre. Flowering time is from spring right through until winter and this long flowering nature makes them a valuable landscaping plan Reasonably drought tolerant and disease resistant, a great Australian plant that is also widely used for cut flowers. The flowers are dried and a are very long lasting..
species.maintenance: Prune back after flowering to stimulate new flowering shoots and to maintain bushiness.

species.description: Australian native daisy with large flowers featuring golden orange centres and white papery textured petals. Great for native gardens, container plantings, garden beds, borders, coastal areas and rockeries. Low maintenance, tolerant of poor soil conditions and drought. Makes a fantastic cut or dried flower lasting indefinitely. Flowers over a long period from Spring through to Autumn. Great for attracting native bees and hoverflies. Also known as "Paper daisy" or "Strawflower". Each daisy ‘flower’ is actually made up of lots of individual flowers in the central disc, and these offer lots of pollen and nectar for passing pollinators. The colourful papery outer ‘petals’ are actually modified leaves called bracts.
species.maintenance: Low maintenance, Responds to dead heading. General purpose liquid fertiliser every month or so. To use as dried flowers pick while in bud and hang upside down to dry.

species.description: A low growing soft-wooded perennial with grey-green leaves and yellow everlasting flowers. Great general garden or pot plant and cut flower. Good heat tolerant plant, performs best in full sun but will tolerate light shade. Dry soil conditions will reduce the flowering. To preserve the flowers, pick while in bud and hang upside down until dry
species.maintenance: Low maintenance, Responds to dead heading. General purpose liquid fertiliser every month or so. To use as dried flowers pick while in bud and hang upside down to dry.

species.description: Xerochrysum viscosum is a common daisy native to Australia. It is also known as Sticky Everlasting, Yellow Paper Daisy, Shiny Everlasting or Golden Everlasting. *X. viscosum* is an erect low growing perennial herb of multiple stem growth. It grows between 20-80cm high and 30-80cm wide with bright green linear or elliptic leaves of 30-100mm long and 2-10mm wide with a sticky, rough surface. The bright yellow flower heads are 20-30mm wide, attractive and long lasting. The papery bracts display the colours of lemon, gold, splotchy orange to bronze.f
species.maintenance: Prune back after flowering to stimulate new flowering shoots and to maintain bushiness.

species.height_raw: 2–3m h over many years x 1m w
species.description: Sculptural sphere of fine silver-blue leaves on a trunk. Slow-growing architectural accent for the hottest, driest spot; needs sharp drainage.

Zamia furfuracea, commonly known as the Cardboard Palm or Cardboard Cycad, is a slow-growing, palm-like cycad native to eastern Mexico. Despite its common name, it isn't a palm — it's a primitive gymnosperm with a thick underground stem that produces a rosette of stiff, leathery, dull-green pinnate leaves that feel like cardboard to the touch. Reaches around 1–1.5m tall and wide over many years. Produces conspicuous brown reproductive cones rather than flowers. Highly architectural, drought-tolerant, and salt-tolerant, making it a striking sculptural specimen for contemporary and coastal gardens. Toxic if ingested — handle with care around children and pets.
species.maintenance: Very low maintenance once established. Drought-tolerant; water sparingly. Remove old yellowing fronds as needed. Frost-tender — protect in cooler climates or grow in a container that can be moved. Slow-growing, so worth siting carefully from the start.

species.common_name: Korean Velvet Grass or No mow grass
